name: SEHOP
displayName: Enable Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP)
explainText:
SEHOP blocks exploits that use the Structured Exception Handling overwrite technique, a common buffer overflow attack.

This policy is only effective on 32-bit systems.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: NLA
displayName: Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) for RDP connections
explainText:
This policy enables Network Level Authentication for RDP connections, with the following settings:

- TLS is required for server authentication and link encryption.
- High level of encryption (128-bit) for the data link.
- User authentication is required at connection time.

Disabling this policy does nothing.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: LMAuth
displayName: Harden network logons and authentication security
explainText:
Enable this policy to disable LM and NTLM authentication modes and enable the use of NTLMv2 only.

Disable this policy to restore LM and NTLMv1 capabilities, in addition to NTLMv2.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 8.1 or Windows RT 8.1

name: WDigest
explainText:
Enabling this policy will disable the WDigest protocol, now considered obsolete.

Keeping WDigest enabled could allow an attacker to retrieve plain-text passwords stored in the LSA service with a tool such as Mimikatz, and it is therefore recommended to enable this policy.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: Logon
explainText:
Enabling this policy modifies two settings related to how the local system handles domain-related credentials:

- Reduce the caching count (2 cached credentials) of domain-related credentials for offline authentication if no domain controller is available
- The delay before the credentials are cleared from memory after a logoff is reduced to 30 seconds.

These settings reduce the exposure time of credentials to attack tools such as Mimikatz.

NOTE: These settings can prevent a new session opening if the network is not available or if a domain controller is not reachable.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: ASLR
displayName: Force the randomization of relocatable images (ASLR)
explainText:
Enabling this policy will enable ASLR even for relocatable images that do not explicitly expose this capability.

Disabling this policy will explicitly disable the ASLR mechanism.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: User32_Exception
explainText:
Enable this policy to change the registry value FEATURE_ALLOW_USER32_EXCEPTION_HANDLER_HARDENING to 1.

This modification is necessary to fully fix an ASLR bypass vulnerability (CVE-2015-6161). For more information, refer to the MS15-124 security bulletin (https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/security-updates/SecurityBulletins/2015/ms15-124).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: Info_Disclosure
explainText:
Enable this policy to change the registry value FEATURE_ENABLE_PRINT_INFO_DISCLOSURE_FIX to 1.

This modification is necessary to fully fix an information disclosure vulnerability in Microsoft browsers (CVE-2017-8529). For more information, refer to the related security update guide (https://portal.msrc.microsoft.com/en-US/security-guidance/advisory/CVE-2017-8529).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: KCET_Enable
explainText:
This policy enables kernel-level shadow stacks, also known as Intel CET (Control-flow Enforcement Technology) or AMD Shadow Stack.

Please note that this security function requires specific hardware support (AMD Zen 3 or Intel 11th Gen processors) and OS support (Windows 21H2 or newer).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10 Version 2106

name: WPBT_Disable
explainText: This policy disables the Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) functionality, which can be used for persistence through a UEFI implant.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 8.1 or Windows RT 8.1

name: TTD_Disable
explainText: This policy disables the Time-Travel Debugging (TTD) functionality, which can be used to dump sensitive process memory content and to launch third-party executables.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 8.1 or Windows RT 8.1

name: CWDIllegalInDllSearch_Enable
displayName: Remove current working directory from DLL search
explainText: The CWDIllegalInDllSearch registry entry is used to remove the current working directory (CWD) from the DLL search order.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 8.1 or Windows RT 8.1

name: AMSI_FeatureBits
explainText:
This policy enables the verification of the Authenticode signature of the AMSI provider.

If you enable this policy, the AMSI provider must be signed by a trusted certificate.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, the signature verification is disabled (default behavior).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: DisableRPCOverTCP
explainText:
This policy disables the RPC over TCP protocol.

If you enable this policy, the RPC over TCP protocol is disabled. RPC over Named Pipes (RPC/NP) will still be available.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, the RPC over TCP protocol is enabled.

See: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/services-and-rpc-tcp
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 8.1 or Windows RT 8.1

name: DisableRemoteScmEndpoints
displayName: Disable remote access to Service Control Manager (SCM)
explainText:
This policy disables remote access to the Service Control Manager (SCM).

If you enable this policy, remote access to the SCM is disabled. This will disable both RPC/TCP and RPC/NP on the system.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, remote access to the SCM is enabled.

See: https://www.gtworek.com/disabling-remote-access-to-windows-services/
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 8.1 or Windows RT 8.1

name: LockBatchFilesWhenInUse
displayName: Enable secure mode for batch file processing
explainText:
This policy gives administrators additional controls over the processing of batch files and CMD scripts.

If you enable this policy, a more secure mode for processing batch files is enabled, which ensures they do not change during execution by holding an opportunistic lock. This enhances the performance and security of batch file processing when Code Integrity is enabled, as signature validation will only be required to be performed a single time, instead of per statement executed in the batch file.

Note: This functionality is supported on Windows 11 Insider Preview Build 26300.7939 or later.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: VulnerableDriverBlocklist
explainText:
This policy setting configures whether the Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is enabled on the system.

The vulnerable driver blocklist is a security feature designed to prevent known insecure, kernel-mode third-party drivers from loading.

If you enable this policy setting, the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is enabled.

If you disable this policy setting, the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is disabled, allowing known vulnerable drivers to load. Note: Disabling this feature reduces system security.

If you do not configure this policy setting, the system defaults (enabled on Windows 11 by default, or configured by HVCI/S-mode/Windows Defender Application Control) will apply.

See: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: WpadOverride
explainText:
This policy setting determines whether WPAD (Web Proxy Auto-Discovery) override is enabled for the current user.

If you enable this policy setting, WPAD override is enabled (value 1), which blocks the automatic detection and override of proxy settings via WPAD for this user, hardening the system against WPAD-based poisoning attacks.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, WPAD override is disabled (value 0).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: HideFileExt
displayName: Show file extensions for known file types
explainText:
By default, Windows Explorer hides file extensions for known file types (such as .exe, .dll, .vbs, .pdf.exe), which can allow attackers to disguise malicious files using fake file extensions or icon spoofing.

If you enable this policy setting, Windows Explorer will display file extensions for all known file types.

If you disable this policy setting, Windows Explorer will hide file extensions for known file types.

If you do not configure this policy setting, the user setting or default Windows behavior will apply.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: DefaultCategory
displayName: Specify default category for Add New Programs
explainText:
Specifies the category of programs that appears when users open the "Add New Programs" page.

If you enable this setting, only the programs in the category you specify are displayed when the "Add New Programs" page opens. Users can use the Category box on the "Add New Programs" page to display programs in other categories.

To use this setting, type the name of a category in the Category box for this setting. You must enter a category that is already defined in Add or Remove Programs. To define a category, use Software Installation.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, all programs (Category: All) are displayed when the "Add New Programs" page opens.

You can use this setting to direct users to the programs they are most likely to need.

Note: This setting is ignored if either the "Remove Add or Remove Programs" setting or the "Hide Add New Programs page" setting is enabled.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoAddFromCDorFloppy
displayName: Hide the "Add a program from CD-ROM or floppy disk" option
explainText:
Removes the "Add a program from CD-ROM or floppy disk" section from the Add New Programs page. This prevents users from using Add or Remove Programs to install programs from removable media.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, the "Add a program from CD-ROM or floppy disk" option is available to all users.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to add or remove program components.

Note: If the "Hide Add New Programs page" setting is enabled, this setting is ignored. Also, if the "Prevent removable media source for any install" setting (located in User Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Installer) is enabled, users cannot add programs from removable media, regardless of this setting.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoAddFromInternet
displayName: Hide the "Add programs from Microsoft" option
explainText:
Removes the "Add programs from Microsoft" section from the Add New Programs page. This setting prevents users from using Add or Remove Programs to connect to Windows Update.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, "Add programs from Microsoft" is available to all users.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to connect to Windows Update.

Note: If the "Hide Add New Programs page" setting is enabled, this setting is ignored.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoAddFromNetwork
displayName: Hide the "Add programs from your network" option
explainText:
Prevents users from viewing or installing published programs.

This setting removes the "Add programs from your network" section from the Add New Programs page. The "Add programs from your network" section lists published programs and provides an easy way to install them.

Published programs are those programs that the system administrator has explicitly made available to the user with a tool such as Windows Installer. Typically, system administrators publish programs to notify users that the programs are available, to recommend their use, or to enable users to install them without having to search for installation files.

If you enable this setting, users cannot tell which programs have been published by the system administrator, and they cannot use Add or Remove Programs to install published programs. However, they can still install programs by using other methods, and they can view and install assigned (partially installed) programs that are offered on the desktop or on the Start menu.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, "Add programs from your network" is available to all users.

Note: If the "Hide Add New Programs page" setting is enabled, this setting is ignored.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoAddPage
explainText:
Removes the Add New Programs button from the Add or Remove Programs bar. As a result, users cannot view or change the attached page.

The Add New Programs button lets users install programs published or assigned by a system administrator.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, the Add New Programs button is available to all users.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to install programs.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoAddRemovePrograms
explainText:
Prevents users from using Add or Remove Programs.

This setting removes Add or Remove Programs from Control Panel and removes the Add or Remove Programs item from menus.

Add or Remove Programs lets users install, uninstall, repair, add, and remove features and components of Windows 2000 Professional and a wide variety of Windows programs. Programs published or assigned to the user appear in Add or Remove Programs.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, Add or Remove Programs is available to all users.

When enabled, this setting takes precedence over the other settings in this folder.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to install or uninstall programs.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoChooseProgramsPage
displayName: Hide the Set Program Access and Defaults page
explainText:
Removes the Set Program Access and Defaults button from the Add or Remove Programs bar.  As a result, users cannot view or change the associated page.

The Set Program Access and Defaults button lets administrators specify default programs for certain activities, such as Web browsing or sending e-mail, as well as which programs are accessible from the Start menu, desktop, and other locations.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, the Set Program Access and Defaults button is available to all users.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to change program access or defaults.

This setting does not prevent the Set Program Access and Defaults icon from appearing on the Start menu.  See the "Remove Set Program Access and Defaults from Start menu" setting.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoRemovePage
displayName: Hide Change or Remove Programs page
explainText:
Removes the Change or Remove Programs button from the Add or Remove Programs bar. As a result, users cannot view or change the attached page.

The Change or Remove Programs button lets users uninstall, repair, add, or remove features of installed programs.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, the Change or Remove Programs page is available to all users.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to delete or uninstall programs.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoServices
explainText:
Prevents users from using Add or Remove Programs to configure installed services.

This setting removes the "Set up services" section of the Add/Remove Windows Components page. The "Set up services" section lists system services that have not been configured and offers users easy access to the configuration tools.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, "Set up services" appears only when there are unconfigured system services. If you enable this setting, "Set up services" never appears.

This setting does not prevent users from using other methods to configure services.

Note: When "Set up services" does not appear, clicking the Add/Remove Windows Components button starts the Windows Component Wizard immediately. Because the only remaining option on the Add/Remove Windows Components page starts the wizard, that option is selected automatically, and the page is bypassed.

To remove "Set up services" and prevent the Windows Component Wizard from starting, enable the "Hide Add/Remove Windows Components page" setting. If the "Hide Add/Remove Windows Components page" setting is enabled, this setting is ignored.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoSupportInfo
explainText:
Removes links to the Support Info dialog box from programs on the Change or Remove Programs page.

Programs listed on the Change or Remove Programs page can include a "Click here for support information" hyperlink. When clicked, the hyperlink opens a dialog box that displays troubleshooting information, including a link to the installation files and data that users need to obtain product support, such as the Product ID and version number of the program. The dialog box also includes a hyperlink to support information on the Internet, such as the Microsoft Product Support Services Web page.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, the Support Info hyperlink appears.

Note: Not all programs provide a support information hyperlink.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: NoWindowsSetupPage
explainText:
Removes the Add/Remove Windows Components button from the Add or Remove Programs bar. As a result, users cannot view or change the associated page.

The Add/Remove Windows Components button lets users configure installed services and use the Windows Component Wizard to add, remove, and configure components of Windows from the installation files.

If you disable this setting or do not configure it, the Add/Remove Windows Components button is available to all users.

This setting does not prevent users from using other tools and methods to configure services or add or remove program components. However, this setting blocks user access to the Windows Component Wizard.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2003, Windows XP, and Windows 2000 only

name: POL_AdmPwd_Enabled
explainText:
Enables management of password for local administrator account

If you enable this setting, local administrator password is managed

If you disable or not configure this setting, local administrator password is NOT managed
supportedOn: At least Microsoft Windows Vista or Windows Server 2003 family

name: POL_AdmPwd
explainText:
Configures password parameters

Password complexity: which characters are used when generating a new password
  Default: Large letters + small letters + numbers + special characters

Password length
  Minimum: 8 characters
  Maximum: 64 characters
  Default: 14 characters

Password age in days
  Minimum: 1 day
  Maximum: 365 days
  Default: 30 days
supportedOn: At least Microsoft Windows Vista or Windows Server 2003 family

items.displayName: Large letters + small letters + numbers + specials

name: POL_AdmPwd_AdminName
displayName: Name of administrator account to manage
explainText:
Administrator account name: name of the local account you want to manage password for.
  DO NOT configure when you use built-in admin account. Built-in admin account is auto-detected by well-known SID, even when renamed

  DO configure when you use custom local admin account
supportedOn: At least Microsoft Windows Vista or Windows Server 2003 family

name: POL_AdmPwd_DontAllowPwdExpirationBehindPolicy
displayName: Do not allow password expiration time longer than required by policy
explainText:
When you enable this setting, planned password expiration longer than password age dictated by "Password Settings" policy is NOT allowed. When such expiration is detected, password is changed immediately and password expiration is set according to policy.

When you disable or not configure this setting, password expiration time may be longer than required by "Password Settings" policy.
supportedOn: At least Microsoft Windows Vista or Windows Server 2003 family

name: bToggleFillSign_Acrobat
explainText:
Disables Adobe Fill and Sign.

Possible values include: 0: Enable Adobe Fill and Sign. 1: Disable Adobe Fill and Sign.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bBoxConnectorEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable connection to the Box cloud when bToggleWebConnectors is set to 1.

Overrides a bToggleWebConnectors value of 1. Only supported on the Continuous track. Possible values include: 0: Disable connection to Box 1: Enable connection to Box
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleAdobeDocumentServices_Acrobat
explainText:
Enable Document Cloud services (except those controlled by other prefs).

Does not affect Sign, prefs sync, or third-party connectors. Reader removes Create/Export/Organize/Combine without subscription. Use bUpdater to disable all services. Values: 0 = enabled; 1 = disabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000060 (V-213178) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleDocumentCloud_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable Document Cloud storage.

DC storage is enabled by default. Possible values include: 0: Enable Document Cloud storage. 1: Disable Document Cloud storage.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDropboxConnectorEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable connection to the Dropbox cloud when bToggleWebConnectors is set to 1.

Overrides a bToggleWebConnectors value of 1. Only supported on the Continuous track. Possible values include: 0: Disable connection to Dropbox 1: Enable connection to Dropbox
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iAcroLoginType_Acrobat
explainText:
Forces Acrobat to use the default system browser for sign-in instead of the embedded CEF browser.

Applies to Acrobat DC only. Use when CEF-based sign-in fails Conditional Access or device identity checks. Selecting this value writes iAcroLoginType = 5 under FeatureLockDown. Disabled or Not Configured removes the value and restores Adobe's default CEF sign-in. Not compatible with Federated Login Domain when external browser sign-in is configured. Adobe documents this as Workaround 1 for Azure AD Conditional Access.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: login_domain_Acrobat
explainText:
Sets the federated login domain so sign-in redirects to the organization's identity provider for the claimed domain.

Applies to Acrobat DC only. Requires a domain claimed in the Adobe Admin Console and Federated ID accounts. Specify the exact claimed domain (no wildcards). Not compatible with External Browser Sign-In. Adobe excludes Acrobat Reader from this feature.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableGentech_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable generative AI features in Acrobat and Reader.

Possible values include: 0: Disable generative AI features. 1: Enable generative AI features. Generative AI capabilities may rely on cloud services; verify organizational policies and Adobe documentation for data handling.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bGoogleDriveConnectorEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable connection to the Google Drive cloud when bToggleWebConnectors is set to 1.

Overrides a bToggleWebConnectors value of 1. Only supported on the Continuous track. Possible values include: 0: Disable connection to Google Drive 1: Enable connection to Google Drive
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleSendACopy_Acrobat
displayName: Hide Fill & Sign Send a Copy Button
explainText:
Specifies whether to hide the Send a Copy button from the Fill & Sign tool in Acrobat and Reader.

Possible values include: 0: Hide the button. 1: Show the button.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bSuppressSignOut_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether the sign-in and sign-out Help menu item should be enabled.

Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't disable the menu item. 1: Disable the Help menu item.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iNGLCEFWorkflowEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Forces Acrobat to use the legacy HTTPS calls sign-in engine instead of the embedded CEF browser.

Applies to Acrobat DC only. Use when CEF-based sign-in fails and external browser sign-in is not suitable. Selecting this value writes iNGLCEFWorkflowEnabled = 0 under FeatureLockDown. Disabled or Not Configured removes the value and restores Adobe's default CEF sign-in. Adobe documents this as Workaround 2 for Azure AD Conditional Access.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bOneDriveConnectorEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable connection to the OneDrive cloud when bToggleWebConnectors is set to 1.

Overrides a bToggleWebConnectors value of 1. Only supported on the Continuous track. Possible values include: 0: Disable connection to OneDrive 1: Enable connection to OneDrive
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bTogglePrefsSync_Acrobat
explainText:
Sync desktop preferences across signed-in devices.

Values: 0 = enabled; 1 = disabled and locked.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000065 (V-213179) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001290 (V-213132) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bUpdater_Updates_Acrobat
explainText:
Web-plugin updates and cloud services.

Disables all services including sign-in. Not the same as FeatureLockDown\bUpdater (product updates). Values: 0 = disable services and component updates; 1 = enable.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000120 (V-213187) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleWebConnectors_Acrobat
explainText:
Third-party cloud storage connectors (Continuous track).

Controls Box, OneDrive, and Dropbox (not SharePoint). Disables Home, Add Account, and custom Open/Save entry points. Values: 0 = enabled; 1 = disabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000075 (V-213181) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001300 (V-213134) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bUIDensityAutoDetectionEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the auto detection logic and bezel for changing Acrobat's display size.

By default, the UI is enabled so that a user may change the display size based on device screen size, resolution, and monitor scaling. 0: Disable the UI. 1: Show the UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableCloudPoweredSearchTokenCaching_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to cache locally cloud-based search service suggestions.

Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't cache cloud search service suggestions 1: Cache suggestions
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableCloudPoweredSearch_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the cloud-based search service in the Find Tool.

Interacts with bEnableCloudPoweredSearchTokenCaching. Data sent to the cloud is not stored and is encrypted. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't enable the cloud search service 1: Enable the cloud search service
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableContextualTips_Acrobat
explainText:
Controls whether to automatically display help tips based on the current context.

Possible values include: 0: Disable contextual tips. 1: Enable tips.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableContextualToolbar_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the context toolbar (popup) when selecting a PDF object.

When enabled, a popup, floating toolbar appears when a user interacts with a PDF. For example, selecting text displays text markup tools. Selecting an image displays sticky note and editing tools. Possible values include: 0: Don't show context toolbars. 1: Show toolbars.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableExtractPageRange_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the page range UI in the Extract Page dialog.

0: Don't show the page range UI. 1: Show the page range UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableAcrobatShortcutCustomization_Acrobat
explainText:
Prevents end users from modifying the tool shortcuts in the right hand pane.

Possible values include: 0: Don't disable shortcuts. 1: Disable shortcuts.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableAV2Enterprise_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the Modern Viewer.

The new app UI is rolling out in phases over 2023. As of June, 25% of users will see the updated user interface. This preference may interact with bShownViewerOnboarding and bEnableAV2 . Possible values include: 0: Don't show the Modern Viewer 1: Show the Modern Viewer
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableRCMNewPOPUp_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the new context menu and use the legacy version.

A new right-click context menu displays icons and additional menu options. 0: Disable the new context menu. 1: Enable the new menu.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bFindMoreWorkflowsOnline_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the menu item that opens the online Actions file library.

Possible values include: 0: Disable the menu item. 1 or null: Don't disable the menu item.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bFindMoreCustomizationsOnline_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the menu item that opens the online Acrobat Tool Set Exchange.

Possible values include: 0: Disable the menu item. 1 or null: Don't disable the menu item.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bOrganizePagesFromThumbnails_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show shortcut UI for the Organize tool from thumbnails.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show Organize Pages tool shortcut from thumbnails 1: Show the Organize Pages tool shortcut
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bRCMCombineFeatureKey_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to display the Combine Files item in a document's right-click context menu.

This preference only applies to machines that display the Modern Viewer (a phased rollout over 2023). When the Modern Viewer is disabled, admins can toggle the Combine Files UI off/on. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the Combine Files UI. 1: Do show the Combine Files UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableAutoCompleteExactMatchLoader_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a "Working on it" message when using the cloud-based search service.

The message appears in the Suggestions section of the Find tool's autocomplete list. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't show the message 1: Show the message
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableAutoCompleteNoInternetConnectionHeader_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a "Requires internet connection" message when using the cloud-based search service.

The message appears in the Suggestions section of the Find tool's autocomplete list. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't show the message 1: Show the message
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableAutoCompleteNoExactMatchHeader_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a "No exact match" message when using the cloud-based search service.

The message appears in the Suggestions section of the Find tool's autocomplete list. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't show the message 1: Show the message
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bCloudATFeatureEnable_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the new auto tagging experience or revert to the old experience.

Possible values include: 0: Disable the new auto tagging feature in the accessibility UI. 1: Enable the new auto tagging feature in the accessibility UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bBatesLogOriginalFileName_Acrobat
explainText:
Use original filename in Bates numbering log output.

When users choose Bates-based output filenames. Values: 0 = Bates numbers in log; 1 = original filename.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bGlobalBarMenuFeatureKey_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Create Split Menu under Create a PDF menu item.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the Create Split menu. 1: Show the Create Split menu.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableReflowEditing_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to lock ReflowEditing and the reflow feature.

See ReflowEditing for feature details. Possible values include: 0: Disable and lock the feature. 1: Don't lock the feature and allow the user to toggle it off and on from the Preferences UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bIgnoreDataSchema_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether all data in a form is saved rather than only data related to the form's schema.

Possible values include: null: Save form data even when it's not part of a schema. 1: Save only form data that's part of the schema.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bMIPCheckPolicyOnDocSave_Acrobat
explainText:
Lock MIP labeling checks on save (admin).

Requires default or mandatory labeling in the Purview portal. Grays out related Preferences UI. HKLM lockdown, not per-user MicrosoftAIP prefs. Values: 0 = do not lock; 1 = lock enabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bMIPLabelling_Acrobat
explainText:
Lock Enable MIP labeling in Preferences > Security.

Machine-level lockdown; complements per-user MicrosoftAIP prefs. Values: 0 = do not lock; 1 = lock enabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableDKEAdmin_Acrobat
explainText:
Locks double key encryption (DKE) label support for Microsoft Purview Information Protection.

Machine-level FeatureLockDown lockdown for MIP DKE workflows. Possible values include: 0: Lock DKE disabled. 1: Lock DKE enabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bMIPExternalAuthAdmin_Acrobat
explainText:
Locks browser-based authentication for Microsoft Purview Information Protection operations.

Machine-level FeatureLockDown lockdown. Possible values include: 0: Lock external browser auth disabled. 1: Lock external browser auth enabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iMIPCloud_Acrobat
explainText:
Locks which Microsoft cloud instance Acrobat and Reader use for MIP SDK operations.

Machine-level FeatureLockDown lockdown. Relevant for sovereign and government tenants. MIP SDK Cloud enum values: 0: Unknown. 1: Custom. 2: Test. 3: Commercial (default/global). 4: Germany. 5: US DoD. 6: US GCC. 7: US GCC High. 8: US Sec. 9: US Nat. 10: China.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bSilentAuth_Acrobat
explainText:
Locks whether operating-system authentication prompts are suppressed during MIP operations.

By default, OS-driven auth prompts for MIP are suppressed. Set policy Disabled to write DWORD 0 and allow OS auth prompts (useful when troubleshooting AADSTS50020-type errors). Possible values include: 0: Allow OS auth prompts. 1: Suppress OS auth prompts.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnable3D_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to trust and render 3D content in PDFs.

This setting can override b3DEnableContent. Possible values include: 0: Don't render 3D content. 1: Trust and render 3D files.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableProtectedModeAppContainer_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the AppContainer sandbox.

Possible values include: 0: Disable Microsoft's AppContainer sandbox 1: Enable Microsoft's AppContainer sandbox
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableBlacklistForOpenSave_Acrobat
explainText:
Hide tBuiltInPermList level-3 extensions from Open/Save dialogs.

New behavior since build 21.011.20029; enabled by default. Values: 0 = legacy behavior (extensions visible); 1 = retain new behavior (hidden).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableJavaScript_Acrobat
explainText:
Blocks and locks JavaScript execution in PDF documents, preventing users from bypassing via privileged locations.

This lockable setting overrides bEnableJS and prevents users from re-enabling JavaScript through the Yellow Message Bar or Trusted Locations. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't disable JS. 1: Disable and lock JS.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iFileAttachmentPerms_Acrobat
explainText:
Block opening non-PDF/FDF file attachments.

Values: 0 = allow (not STIG-compliant); 1 = block (recommended; DISA STIG and NSA hardening guidance).

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000035 (V-213174) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000275 (V-213119) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisablePDFRedirectionActions_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to block specific PDF actions (listed below) which result in opening a link.

This preference does not block regular web links. Enabling this feature blocks PDF actions that open links, including GoToE, GoToR, Launch, Thread, Import Data, Export Form Data, Submit Form, and Reset Form. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't block these opening links. 1: Block links.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnablePVCertificateBasedTrust_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether a document's certification status should appear in the Protected View document message bar.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the document's certification status. 1: Do show the document's certification status.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnhancedSecurityInBrowser_Acrobat
explainText:
Enhanced security when running in the browser.

GUI checkbox sets this with bEnhancedSecurityStandalone. On 8.x, use bEnhancedSecurityStandalone for both. Values: 0 = disabled; 1 = enabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000010 (V-213169) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000210 (V-213118) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnhancedSecurityStandalone_Acrobat
explainText:
Enhanced security in the standalone application.

GUI checkbox sets this with bEnhancedSecurityInBrowser. On 8.x, this controls both browser and standalone. Values: 0 = disabled; 1 = enabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000005 (V-213168) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000205 (V-213117) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableFlash_Acrobat
explainText:
Render Flash content in PDFs.

Privileged locations do not override this setting. Values: 0 = empty box and security warning; 1 = play if Flash player present.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000045 (V-213175) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000290 (V-213122) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bProtectedMode_Acrobat
explainText:
Enables Protected Mode which sandboxes Acrobat and Reader processes.

Protected Mode should be enabled to protect user systems and data. Possible values include: 0: Don't enable protected mode. 1: Do enable protected mode.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000015 (V-213170) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001010 (V-213127) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iProtectedView_Acrobat
explainText:
Protected View mode.

Values: 0 = off (default); 1 = untrusted locations only (recommended); 2 = all files.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000020 (V-213171) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001015 (V-213128) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

items.displayName: Enable Protected View for unsafe locations only
Enable Protected View for all files

name: iUnlistedAttachmentTypePerm_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies the default permissions for file types that aren't listed in the default or user-specified lists.

Possible values include: 0: Prompt user without ability to set file type as Allowed (two choices: Open File, Never Allow). 1 (default): Prompt user with ability to Allow or Prohibit (three choices). 2: Always open unlisted file types. 3: Never open unlisted file types.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

items.displayName: Prompt without ability to allow (most restrictive prompt)
Prompt with ability to allow or prohibit (default)
Never open unlisted file types (most restrictive)

name: bMSStoreTrusted_Acrobat
displayName: Allow Changes to Windows Certificate Store Trust
explainText:
Locks the UI so that end users cannot change the value set by iMSStoreTrusted.

Set iMSStoreTrusted first, then use this preference to lock it. Allowable values include: 0: Lock the UI. 1: Same as null. Don't lock the UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAllowInvisibleSig_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow invisible certification signatures.

False disables the menu option, prevents signing and certifying with invisible signatures, and limits JavaScript support by signature fields.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAllowPasswordSaving_Acrobat
explainText:
Controls whether certain passwords can be cached to disk; for example, passwords for digital IDs.

If false, users are prompted to enter a password every time one is required. Not all passwords are affected by this setting.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableSignatureClear_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable and lock the ability for a signer to clear their own signature.

Possible values include: 0: Disable signature clearing. 1: Enable signature clearing.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bVerifyUseAlways_Acrobat
explainText:
Qualifies the use of aVerify.

If true and aVerify is set to a handler name, then this handler is used to verify all signatures. If false, then the aVerify handler is used only to verify signatures when the handler specified by the signature dictionary Filter attribute is not present.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableExpandEnvironmentVariables_Acrobat
displayName: Block User Library Trust in Protected View
explainText:
Allow user-specific paths as trusted locations in Protected View.

When off, only static org-wide trusted locations apply. Paths like C:\Users\%username%\Desktop can be trusted when enabled. Values: 0 = trust user locations; 1 = do not trust user locations.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bWinCacheSessionHandles_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to retain cryptographic service provider (CSP) handles when a user authenticates to a digital ID.

If true, a user does not have to re-authenticate to use the ID unless they log out or the session ends. The impact of this preference will vary based on the CSP in use; however, the setting does not affect the Windows CSPs.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableADCFileStore_Acrobat
explainText:
Disables Acrobat.com file storage integration.

When enabled, disables storage of files on Acrobat.com (Adobe Document Cloud). Aligns with DISA STIG Acrobat Pro DC V-213131 (AADC-CN-000250). Possible values include: 0: Allow Acrobat.com file storage. 1: Disable Acrobat.com file storage.

Security Reference: STIG AADC-CN-000250 (V-213131) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableOSTrustedSites_Acrobat
displayName: Disable IE Trusted Sites as Privileged Locations
explainText:
Locks the ability to treat IE trusted sites as privileged locations either on or off so the users can't change the bTrustOSTrustedSites value via the user interface.

If set, bTrustOSTrustedSites is simply ignored. Possible values include: 0 or null: Enables and locks trusting sites from IE. 1: Disables and locks trusting sites from IE.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAllowAPSConfig_Acrobat
explainText:
Prevents a LiveCycle Rights Management Server from being configured by disabling the menu option in the Security Settings Console.

By default, configuration is allowed.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bReqRevCheck_Acrobat
explainText: Locks Security\cASPKI\cASPKI\cVerify\iReqRevCheck and disables the user interface item.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bReasons_Acrobat
explainText:
Prevents users from modifying reason settings.

v8.1: If locked and cReasons is empty, bAllowSigningReasons is 0 and read only. If locked and cReasons has values, then bAllowSigningReasons is true and read only.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableTrustedFolders_Acrobat
explainText:
Disable and lock trusted folders and files.

Prevents users from adding folder or file privileged locations. Values: 0 or null = allowed; 1 = disabled and locked.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000315 (V-213188) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000840 (V-213124) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableTrustedSites_Acrobat
explainText:
Disable and lock host-based privileged locations.

Values: 0 or null = enable and lock host-based locations; 1 = disable and lock host-based locations.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000320 (V-213189) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001325 (V-213139) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableCEFBasedUI_Acrobat
explainText:
Modern CEF-based digital signature UI.

All values disable the user preference toggle. Block self-signed ID creation (post-June 2016) with bSelfSignCertGen=0 and bEnableCEFBasedUI=0. Values: 0 = legacy UI; 1 = modern UI.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bUseTSAsSigningTime_Acrobat
explainText:
Show timestamp server time in signature appearance.

Default uses local clock. Requires bReqSigPropRetrieval=1 (HKCU). Verify time against iMaxClockSkew (default 65 min). Values: 0 = hide timestamp; 1 = show timestamp.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bShowSignMenu_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Sign menu in Acrobat's top level menu bar.

Possible values include: 0 or null: Disable the Sign menu item. 1: Enable the menu item.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAllowReasonWhenSigning_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether the reason UI will appear during signing.

The preference can be overridden by a document seed value set on a field. For 8.1 and later, if cReasons is locked and is empty, bAllowSigningReasons is 0 and read only (The UI is turned off). If cReasons is locked and has values, then bAllowSigningReasons is true and read only.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableCertificateBasedTrust_Acrobat
explainText:
Trust certified documents as privileged locations (admin lock).

Lockable counterpart to bTrustCertifiedDocuments. Does not apply in Protected View. Values: 0 or null = not trusted; 1 = trusted.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iUnknownURLPerms_Acrobat
explainText:
Access policy for URLs not in the user list.

Overrides privileged location host settings in some versions. Values: 1 = ask; 2 = allow; 3 = block.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000030 (V-213173) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000280 (V-213120) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bValidateOnOpen_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to automatically validate all signatures on document open.

Note that the lockable setting does not configure the feature; instead, it locks what is set in HKCU and the user interface. 0: Don't validate signatures on document open. 1: Validate signatures on document open.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleAdobeSign_Acrobat
explainText:
Adobe Acrobat Sign (Send for Signature).

On Continuous track, also set bToggleManageSign. Values: 0 = enabled; 1 = disabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000085 (V-213183) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleSendAndTrack_Acrobat
explainText:
Disables Adobe Send and Track (some UI is renamed to "Share" since October, 2018)

Possible values include: 0: Enable Adobe Send and Track. 1: Disable Adobe Send and Track.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableRecipientMention_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow participants in a shared review to @mention people who are not review collaborators.

Prior to this release, reviewers could only @mention other reviewers in the review comments. Possible values include: 0: Don't allow mentioning non-reviewers. 1: Allow mentioning non-reviewers.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableSharePointFeatures_Acrobat
explainText:
Disable SharePoint and Office 365 integration.

Disables SharePoint detection, check-out prompt, and SharePoint menu items. Values: 0 or null = enabled; 1 = disabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000100 (V-213185) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001315 (V-213137) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableWebmail_Acrobat
explainText:
Disable WebMail integration.

Values: 0 = enable WebMail profiles; 1 = disable. With bSendMailShareRedirection=1, the email icon attaches the PDF directly.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000090 (V-213184) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-001305 (V-213135) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleAdobeReview_Acrobat
explainText:
Document Cloud Review service UI.

When disabled, removes cloud review UI and legacy review types are used. Values: 0 or null = enabled; 1 = disabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bSendMailShareRedirection_Acrobat
displayName: Email Icon Attach to Email Behavior
explainText:
Email icon attaches document instead of opening the share pane.

Values: 0 or null = open share pane; 1 = attach to email.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bMixRecentFilesFeatureLockDown_Acrobat
displayName: Hide Shared Files from Recent List
explainText:
Show shared files in the Recent list.

Covers shares, reviews, signing, and Send and Track workflows. Values: 0 = add to Recent; 1 = do not add.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleFSSSignatureSaving_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to save a newly created signature in the cloud.

When a user creates a new signature, the dialog offers the option to store the signature in the cloud for later use. This preference also controls saving user initials. Possible values include: 0: Show the Save Signature UI 1: Hide the Save Signature UI
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAdobeSendPluginToggle_Acrobat
explainText:
Adobe Send and Track button in Outlook.

Uploads attachments to Document Cloud and inserts public preview/download links in email. Values: 0 = enabled; 1 = disabled.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000055 (V-213177) Low; STIG AADC-CN-000295 (V-213123) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableReviewPromote_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to display a Share/Review feature reminder message when users have used those features in the past.

If the user has not used the review service for 30 days AND has previously opened a PDF with review comments, Acrobat displays a tip reminding the user the review/share service is available. Possible values include: 0: Don't show a tip. 1: Show tip.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableSharePointInChromeExtn_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to integrate SharePoint into the Acrobat's Chrome extension.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable SharePoint integration. 1: Enable.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleManageSign_Acrobat
explainText:
Signature tab on Home, notifications, and sign tracking.

Hides agreements, notifications, and To Do sign cards when disabled. Values: 0 = show; 1 = hide.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableOnBehalfOfText_Acrobat
displayName: Show Comment Author in Shared Review
explainText:
If false, the string "On behalf of" does not append the author's name in the comment when another person opens the document in a shared-review workflow.

This preference is only used in shared review workflows. Possible values include: 0: Don't display the comment author's name. 1: Do display the comment author's name.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iClientType_Gmail_Acrobat
explainText:
Identifies the Gmail Mail client type for WebMail.

The value can only be: 1
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iClientType_Yahoo_Acrobat
explainText:
Identifies the Yahoo Mail client type for WebMail.

The value can only be: 2
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iIMAPPort_Acrobat
explainText:
Identifies the My Profile Mail IMAP server port number for WebMail.

The value can be: Any valid port number.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iIMAPSecurity_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the My Profile Mail IMAP security for WebMail.

The value can be: 0: Don't enable security. 1: Enable security.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iSMTPPort_Acrobat
explainText:
Identifies the My Profile Mail SMTP server port number for WebMail.

The value can be: Any valid server port number.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: iSMTPSecurity_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the My Profile Mail SMTP security for WebMail.

The value can be: 0: Don't enable security. 1: Enable security.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bShowMsgAtLaunch_Acrobat
explainText:
Show Adobe messages at product launch.

Also hides Share Feedback, EOL warnings, profile prompts, and the Home banner. Values: 0 = hide; 1 = show.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAllowUserToChangeMsgPrefs_Acrobat
displayName: Allow Users to Change Message Preferences
explainText:
Locks the features associated with bShowMsgAtLaunch and bDontShowMsgWhenViewingDoc so that end users can't change the settings.

Possible values include: 0: Locks the feature so end users can't change the settings. 1: Allows users to change the settings. A value of 1 has the same effect as this key not existing at all.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleNotifications_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable all in-product and desktop notifications.

When 0 (or null), feature-specific notifications are managed via the related service preference. When set to 1, this preference disables all notifications irrespective of the values of all other keys. Possible values include: 0: Enable desktop notifications. 1: Disable all desktop notifications.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bShowWelcomeScreen_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Welcome screen at product launch.

When enabled (DWORD 0), the Welcome screen is disabled. Aligns with DISA STIG Reader V-213186 and Acrobat Pro V-213136. Possible values include: 0: Do not show Welcome screen. 1: Show Welcome screen.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000040 (V-213186) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000260 (V-213136) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleFTE_Acrobat
explainText:
First Time Experience (welcome tour and page).

Also disabled when bUpdater, bToggleAdobeDocumentServices, bToggleAdobeSign, bTogglePrefsSync, or bToggleWebConnectors is set. Values: 0 or null = enabled; 1 = disabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDontShowMsgWhenViewingDoc_Acrobat
displayName: Hide Adobe Messages on Document Open
explainText:
Specifies whether to show messages from Adobe when a document opens.

This preference also controls messages in the right-hand pane for 12.x and later products as well as the "Learn More" link, including the "Start Free Trial" message promoting Acrobat. Possible values include: 0: Don't show messages from Adobe when a document opens. 1: Show messages from Adobe when a document opens.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableBellButton_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to hide in-product messages.

A value of 1 hides notifications, but the product still fetches and caches them. Possible values include: 0: Show in-product notifications. 1: Hide in-product notifications.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleShareFeedback_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Send Feedback icon.

By default, the UI displays a feedback icon so that users can easily send feedback to Adobe with one click. This preference replaces bUsageMeasurement for 12.x and later products. Setting bShowMsgAtLaunch to 0 also hides the icon. Possible values include: 0: Hide the icon. 1: Show the icon.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleToDoList_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a "to do" list on the Home screen.

By default, the Home screen displays a list of action items such as Take a Tour, Export PDF, and so on. For details, see the What's New . Possible values include: 0: Enable the feature. 1: Disable the feature.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bIsSCReducedModeEnforcedEx_Acrobat
explainText:
Enforce Reader-like reduced mode on Unified Acrobat (64-bit MUI).

Opens PDFs without Adobe ID sign-in. Values: 0 = not enforced; 1 = enforced. May require additional cIPM values per Adobe enterprise KB.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bShowScanTabInHomeView_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the Scan tab in Home view.

When enabled, links to scans appear under the Scan tab in the Home view. Possible values include: 0: Hide the scan tab. 1: Show the Scan tab.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleNotificationToasts_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to hide desktop notifications.

A value of 1 hides notifications, but the product still fetches and caches them. Possible values include: 0: Show desktop notifications. 1: Hide desktop notifications.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bTogglePDFOwnershipToasts_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a notification on machine startup that allows the user to make Acrobat the default PDF viewer.

When enabled and both Acrobat and Reader are installed, the user can click on the notification to change the default PDF viewer. Possible values include: 0: Show PDF ownership notification on application startup. 1: Don't show ownership notification.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bToggleToDoTiles_Acrobat
displayName: Show To Do Cards in Recent Tab
explainText:
Specifies whether to show To Do Cards in the Recent Tab view

To Do cards list potential action items for members of certain workflows (for example, collaborative reviews). When set to 1, To Do cards do not appear in the Recent tab. Possible values include: 0 or null: Show cards for unaccepted workflows (reviews, views and sign). 1: Hide cards for unaccepted workflows (reviews, views and sign).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bUsageMeasurement_Acrobat
explainText:
Legacy master switch for usage measurement and analytics.

Superseded by bToggleShareFeedback in 12.x and later, but still honored on some builds. When disabled (DWORD 0), usage measurement is off. Possible values include: 0: Disable usage measurement. 1: Enable usage measurement.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bWhatsNewExp_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the What's New experience.

This feature was phased in incrementally over 2022. When enabled, the default user on first launch will see a What's New screen as well as a See new features notification. These UI items appear once. Possible values include: 0: Enable the What's New experience. 1: Disable.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableThirdPartyPluginNotif_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to notify users with 32 bit plugins that the app will soon update to 64 bit.

32 bit plugins will not work in the 64 bit app. The notification provides a "Learn more" link that provides additional details about how to upgrade their plugin. Possible values include: 0: Do not warn the user about 32 bit plugins. 1: Do warn the user.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bEnableAutoDockUndockHUD_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to automatically dock and undock the HUD bar based on the window size.

Possible values include: 0: Disable automatic behavior. 1: Enable auto docking and undocking.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bHasAcrobatConsent_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether the Reader process should automatically open Acrobat for the current file.

PDF ownership does not change. Reader will continue as the default PDF viewer on this machine. Possible values include: 0: Don't automatically use Acrobat. 1: Use Acrobat
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bCrashReporterEnabled_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the crash reporter dialog on application crash (Windows only).

This feature is part of the CrashReporter integration on Windows. The dialog allows users to send crash logs to the CrashReporter team. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the dialog. 1: Show the dialog
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableHarmonyInstallationFeature_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether Acrobat can install the Adobe Express Photos app for eligible users.

Possible values include: 0: Install Adobe Express Photos for eligible users on Acrobat launch. 1: Disable installation of Adobe Express Photos for eligible users on Acrobat launch. Adobe also documents this as the opt-out for Acrobat auto-update install of Adobe Express Photos (June 2026). Windows and Acrobat Continuous track only. Unified 64-bit Reader uses the Acrobat hive.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bAcroSuppressOpenInReader_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable and lock the PDF viewer Chrome extension.

See also ENABLE_CHROMEEXT . Possible values include: 0 or null: Extension is enabled; users can open PDFs in a browser with Acrobat Reader 1: Disable the browser-based PDF viewer. A tooltip says "The Acrobat Reader extension is currently disabled. Please contact your IT admin."
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bSuppressMessageBar_Acrobat
explainText:
Prevents the appearance of the document message bar.

Adversely affects signing when preview mode is used.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisablePDFHandlerSwitching_Acrobat
explainText:
Lock the default PDF viewer handler.

Adobe PDF handler only; does not switch to or from non-Adobe products. UI changes invoke the installer (HKLM), not HKCU. Values: 0 or null = allow change; 1 = block change.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000050 (V-213176) Low; STIG AADC-CN-001280 (V-213130) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bDisableThumbnailPreviewHandler_Acrobat
explainText:
Lock Explorer PDF thumbnail preview checkbox.

Values: 0 = users can enable via installer; 1 = disable and lock.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: PatchCleanFlag_Acrobat
explainText:
Clean cached MSI/MSP patches on next update.

Patches accumulate under ProgramData\Adobe\ARM and Windows\Installer. Values: 0 = no cleanup; 1 = cleanup on next update.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bUpdater_Updater_Acrobat
explainText:
Controls Adobe Acrobat/Reader product updates.

Disables or enables automatic product updates (distinct from cloud services in FeatureLockDown\cServices). For 12.x and later, this setting overrides the ARM Legacy Mode preference; setting to 0 also removes the updater UI (Preferences > Updater and Help > Check for updates). Values: 0 = disable product updates; 1 = enable product updates.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC

name: bShouldUseScalableCursor_Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the scalable cursor.

name: iClientType_Yahoo_Reader
explainText:
Identifies the Yahoo Mail client type for WebMail.

The value can only be: 2
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: iIMAPPort_Reader
explainText:
Identifies the My Profile Mail IMAP server port number for WebMail.

The value can be: Any valid port number.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: iIMAPSecurity_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the My Profile Mail IMAP security for WebMail.

The value can be: 0: Don't enable security. 1: Enable security.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: iSMTPPort_Reader
explainText:
Identifies the My Profile Mail SMTP server port number for WebMail.

The value can be: Any valid server port number.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: iSMTPSecurity_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the My Profile Mail SMTP security for WebMail.

The value can be: 0: Don't enable security. 1: Enable security.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bShowMsgAtLaunch_Reader
explainText:
Show Adobe messages at product launch.

Also hides Share Feedback, EOL warnings, profile prompts, and the Home banner. Values: 0 = hide; 1 = show.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bAllowUserToChangeMsgPrefs_Reader
displayName: Allow Users to Change Message Preferences
explainText:
Locks the features associated with bShowMsgAtLaunch and bDontShowMsgWhenViewingDoc so that end users can't change the settings.

Possible values include: 0: Locks the feature so end users can't change the settings. 1: Allows users to change the settings. A value of 1 has the same effect as this key not existing at all.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleNotifications_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable all in-product and desktop notifications.

When 0 (or null), feature-specific notifications are managed via the related service preference. When set to 1, this preference disables all notifications irrespective of the values of all other keys. Possible values include: 0: Enable desktop notifications. 1: Disable all desktop notifications.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bShowWelcomeScreen_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Welcome screen at product launch.

When enabled (DWORD 0), the Welcome screen is disabled. Aligns with DISA STIG Reader V-213186 and Acrobat Pro V-213136. Possible values include: 0: Do not show Welcome screen. 1: Show Welcome screen.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000040 (V-213186) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000260 (V-213136) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleFTE_Reader
explainText:
First Time Experience (welcome tour and page).

Also disabled when bUpdater, bToggleAdobeDocumentServices, bToggleAdobeSign, bTogglePrefsSync, or bToggleWebConnectors is set. Values: 0 or null = enabled; 1 = disabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bDontShowMsgWhenViewingDoc_Reader
displayName: Hide Adobe Messages on Document Open
explainText:
Specifies whether to show messages from Adobe when a document opens.

This preference also controls messages in the right-hand pane for 12.x and later products as well as the "Learn More" link, including the "Start Free Trial" message promoting Acrobat. Possible values include: 0: Don't show messages from Adobe when a document opens. 1: Show messages from Adobe when a document opens.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bEnableBellButton_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to hide in-product messages.

A value of 1 hides notifications, but the product still fetches and caches them. Possible values include: 0: Show in-product notifications. 1: Hide in-product notifications.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleShareFeedback_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Send Feedback icon.

By default, the UI displays a feedback icon so that users can easily send feedback to Adobe with one click. This preference replaces bUsageMeasurement for 12.x and later products. Setting bShowMsgAtLaunch to 0 also hides the icon. Possible values include: 0: Hide the icon. 1: Show the icon.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleToDoList_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a "to do" list on the Home screen.

By default, the Home screen displays a list of action items such as Take a Tour, Export PDF, and so on. For details, see the What's New . Possible values include: 0: Enable the feature. 1: Disable the feature.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bShowScanTabInHomeView_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the Scan tab in Home view.

When enabled, links to scans appear under the Scan tab in the Home view. Possible values include: 0: Hide the scan tab. 1: Show the Scan tab.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleNotificationToasts_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to hide desktop notifications.

A value of 1 hides notifications, but the product still fetches and caches them. Possible values include: 0: Show desktop notifications. 1: Hide desktop notifications.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bTogglePDFOwnershipToasts_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a notification on machine startup that allows the user to make Acrobat the default PDF viewer.

When enabled and both Acrobat and Reader are installed, the user can click on the notification to change the default PDF viewer. Possible values include: 0: Show PDF ownership notification on application startup. 1: Don't show ownership notification.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleToDoTiles_Reader
displayName: Show To Do Cards in Recent Tab
explainText:
Specifies whether to show To Do Cards in the Recent Tab view

To Do cards list potential action items for members of certain workflows (for example, collaborative reviews). When set to 1, To Do cards do not appear in the Recent tab. Possible values include: 0 or null: Show cards for unaccepted workflows (reviews, views and sign). 1: Hide cards for unaccepted workflows (reviews, views and sign).
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bUsageMeasurement_Reader
explainText:
Legacy master switch for usage measurement and analytics.

Superseded by bToggleShareFeedback in 12.x and later, but still honored on some builds. When disabled (DWORD 0), usage measurement is off. Possible values include: 0: Disable usage measurement. 1: Enable usage measurement.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bWhatsNewExp_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the What's New experience.

This feature was phased in incrementally over 2022. When enabled, the default user on first launch will see a What's New screen as well as a See new features notification. These UI items appear once. Possible values include: 0: Enable the What's New experience. 1: Disable.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bDisableThirdPartyPluginNotif_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to notify users with 32 bit plugins that the app will soon update to 64 bit.

32 bit plugins will not work in the 64 bit app. The notification provides a "Learn more" link that provides additional details about how to upgrade their plugin. Possible values include: 0: Do not warn the user about 32 bit plugins. 1: Do warn the user.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bEnableAutoDockUndockHUD_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to automatically dock and undock the HUD bar based on the window size.

Possible values include: 0: Disable automatic behavior. 1: Enable auto docking and undocking.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bHasAcrobatConsent_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether the Reader process should automatically open Acrobat for the current file.

PDF ownership does not change. Reader will continue as the default PDF viewer on this machine. Possible values include: 0: Don't automatically use Acrobat. 1: Use Acrobat
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bAcroSuppressOpenInReader_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable and lock the PDF viewer Chrome extension.

See also ENABLE_CHROMEEXT . Possible values include: 0 or null: Extension is enabled; users can open PDFs in a browser with Acrobat Reader 1: Disable the browser-based PDF viewer. A tooltip says "The Acrobat Reader extension is currently disabled. Please contact your IT admin."
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bSuppressMessageBar_Reader
explainText:
Prevents the appearance of the document message bar.

Adversely affects signing when preview mode is used.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bDisablePDFHandlerSwitching_Reader
explainText:
Lock the default PDF viewer handler.

Adobe PDF handler only; does not switch to or from non-Adobe products. UI changes invoke the installer (HKLM), not HKCU. Values: 0 or null = allow change; 1 = block change.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000050 (V-213176) Low; STIG AADC-CN-001280 (V-213130) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bDisableThumbnailPreviewHandler_Reader
explainText:
Lock Explorer PDF thumbnail preview checkbox.

Values: 0 = users can enable via installer; 1 = disable and lock.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: PatchCleanFlag_Reader
explainText:
Clean cached MSI/MSP patches on next update.

Patches accumulate under ProgramData\Adobe\ARM and Windows\Installer. Values: 0 = no cleanup; 1 = cleanup on next update.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bUpdater_Updater_Reader
explainText:
Controls Adobe Acrobat/Reader product updates.

Disables or enables automatic product updates (distinct from cloud services in FeatureLockDown\cServices). For 12.x and later, this setting overrides the ARM Legacy Mode preference; setting to 0 also removes the updater UI (Preferences > Updater and Help > Check for updates). Values: 0 = disable product updates; 1 = enable product updates.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bEnableAcrobatPromptForDocOpen_Reader
displayName: Prompt to Use Acrobat from Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to prompt users to use Acrobat when both Reader and Acrobat are installed.

When Acrobat and Reader are both present, opening a file in Reader prompts the user to switch to Acrobat as well as make Acrobat the default PDF viewer. Possible values include: 0: Don't prompt to use Acrobat. 1: Prompt to use Acrobat.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bShouldUseScalableCursor_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the scalable cursor.

Because Citrix does not provide support for scalable cursors (32-bit cursors with an alpha channel) in legacy graphics mode, scalable cursor performance may be impaired on Citrix. Use this setting to improve performance on Citrix by using a non-scalable cursor. Possible values include: 0: Don't use a scalable cursor. 1: Use a scalable cursor.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bFavoritesFeaturesLockDown_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable and lock the starred file feature.

A starred file is somewhat similar to a "favorited" file. This preference overrides bFavoritesStripInRFL. Possible values include: 0: Disable and lock starred files in the recent files list. 1: Use bFavoritesStripInRFL to control this feature.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleSophiaWebInfra_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to show users messages which promote (Trials, Acrobat, PDF Pack etc.)

Subscription users may be prompted to download Acrobat. Theoretically, this preference does not interact with any other upsell preferences. Possible values include: 0 or null: Disable campaigns in Reader's right-hand pane bottom banner 1: Enable campaigns
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bLimitPromptsFeatureKey_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to limit the number of prompts a user will see in a 24 hour period.

Prompts include items like tips, calls-to-action, and feature walk throughs. These are not necessarily upsell items. Possible values include: 0: Don't restrict informational prompts. 1: Limit prompts to 1 per day and 3 per week.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bReaderRetentionExperiment_Reader
displayName: Prompt Reader Users to Download Acrobat
explainText:
Specifies whether to prompt Acrobat subscribers using Reader to download Acrobat.

When enabled, download Acrobat prompts appear in Reader workflows where the user might benefit from Acrobat (purchased but not yet downloaded). Possible values include: 0: Disable "download Acrobat" prompts in Reader. 1: Enable download prompts.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bToggleDCAppCenter_Reader
explainText:
App Center and get-apps banner on Home.

Values: 0 or null = show; 1 = hide.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bShowRhpToolSearch_Reader
explainText:
Specifies whether to show "for purchase" tools when searching for tools in Reader.

When enabled, searching for tools in Reader shows all possible tool subscriptions. Possible values include: 0: Don't show tool subscriptions. 1: Show tools which can be purchased.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: bAcroSuppressUpsell_Reader
explainText:
Disable upgrade and upsell messages (12.x+).

Controls Reader tool purchase and Standard-to-Professional prompts. Values: 0 or null = show upsell; 1 = disable upsell.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000080 (V-213182) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC (32-bit)

name: ADC4275035_ClickEdit_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Auto-enter edit mode when the user clicks a PDF object.

Clicking image or text opens edit tools; clicking a form field enables form authoring. Values: 0 or null = disabled; 1 = enabled.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: ADC4275034_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the color picker in the Fill and Sign tool.

The color picker is only supported on the Continuous track. Possible values include: 0: Disable the color picker 1: Enable the color picker

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: ProtectOldExperience_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Use legacy Protect tool menus instead of the new UI.

Values: 0 or null = new UI; 1 = pre-Oct 2019 menus.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: ADC4302862_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Paste copied elements to the same location as the source.

Applies to form fields, annotations, and links. Values: 0 = disabled; 1 = enabled.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: ADC4275035_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Remove Oct 2019 AddText and EditText form tools from the UI.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: BlockEMFParsing_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Block EMF to PDF conversion.

Shows an unsupported dialog when blocked. Values: 0 = allow; 1 = block.

When this policy is Enabled, EMF-to-PDF conversion is blocked. When Disabled, conversion is allowed.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)
