This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: DisableScannedDocumentEditing_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable text recognition while editing scanned PDFs.

Possible values include: 0: Text recognition will be performed when invoking editing on scanned PDFs. 1: Text recognition will not be performed when invoking editing on scanned PDFs.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: EnablePDFMakerGroupImagesTagCorrectionFeature_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable accessibility fixes for tagging grouped images.

0: Disable. 1: Enable.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: EnablePDFMakerTableHeaderCellTagAndScopeUpdateFeature_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable accessibility fixes for tagging table headers.

0: Disable. 1: Enable.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: EnablePDFMakerSplitTextPathElemsFeature_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Fix Text Path rendering bug in PDFMaker tags.

Mitigates incorrect border/alt-text rendering from a 2020 bug. Enabled by default. Values: 0 = disable correction; 1 = enable.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: EnableFlashEditing_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable the Flash tools for adding annotations or Flash in the Rich Media app.

Possible values include: 0 or null: Remove "Disable Flash > Add SWF menu item." 1: Show the menu item.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: bEnablePVSwitchoutShortcut_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Shortcut key to exit Protected View for the current document.

Allows Protected View by default with on-demand exit. Values: 0 = disabled; 1 = enabled.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: EULA_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Accept EULA for the built-in updater.

Alternative to EULA_ACCEPT=YES at install time. Values: 0 = not accepted; 1 = accepted.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit)

name: DisableMaintenance_AcrobatX64
explainText:
Disable Help > Repair for all users.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.

This non-Policies setting applies to Acrobat and Reader DC (64-bit) installations and writes to the native 64-bit registry view.

explainText:
Use login name as comment author.

Uses identity preferences login name, then login-name, then shared-review author. Default true for Acrobat, false for Reader. Values: 0 = use login name; 1 = do not use login name.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bOpenInPlaceDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to open cross document links in the same window.

Possible values include: 0: Don't open links in the same window. 1: Do open links in the same window.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bOverprintPreviewUseShiftClickDC_User
explainText:
Shift+Click behavior in the output preview dialog.

Values: 0 = Shift+Click adds color-value sticky note; 1 = Shift+Click multi-select; Alt/Option+Click adds sticky note.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAccessOverrideDocColorsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to replace black text or line art colors when iAccessColorPolicy is enabled and a replacement color has been specified.

While the default is 1, the preference is not read unless iAccessPolicy is enabled (1). Possible values include: 0: Don't replace black text or line art colors. 1: Replace black text or line art colors.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bOverrideLineArtColorsDC_User
explainText:
Limits color changes to black text and line art when iAccessColorPolicy is enabled and a replacement color has been specified.

While the default is 1, the preference is not read unless "Accessibility" enabled (1). Possible values include: 0: Don't replace text or line art colors. 1: Replace text or line art colors. See also bAccessOverrideDocColors in Originals.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iPageLayoutDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the user selected page layout override.

When bOverridePageLayout is set to 1, the override drop down list becomes enabled so that the user can set the desired page layout. Possible values include: 1: Single Page 2: Single Page Continuous 3: Two Up Continuous 5: Two Up
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bOverrideZoomDC_User
explainText:
Let users set a default zoom for all documents.

Overrides author Page Display settings and sets iZoomScale when enabled. Values: 0 = document default; 1 = enable zoom dropdown.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iZoomTypeDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the zoom scale for all other documents other than a % scale and overrides Page Display settings.

% scales are stored in iZoomScale. Possible values include: 1: Fit Page 2: Fit Width 3: Fit Height 4: Fit Visible 6: Reflow
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iParagraphDirectionDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the paragraph direction.

Possible values include: 0: Right to Left 1: Left to Right
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bPopupsOpenIffSelectedDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether to open a popup when it is selected.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bPopupsScrollWithPageDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether popups are visible when a document is scrolled.

Possible values include: 0: Hide popups on document scroll. 1: Show popups on document scroll.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUseDetailsNavigatorDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show portfolio component files and file details in an accessible list.

This preference replaces bUsePlatformNavigator. Files mode provides a better reading experience for people with disabilities such as mobility impairments, blindness, and low vision. Possible values include: 0: Don't show portfolio components in a list. 1: Do show portfolio components in a list.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bPrintAnnotsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to print notes, popups, and other annotations.

Setting a similar preference from the Print panel sets a corresponding setting in HKU. Possible values include: 0: Don't print annotations. 1: Do print annotations.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bprintCommentPopupsDC_User
explainText:
Enables printing of comments and other annotations.

Notes and popups that are open will be printed when the rest of the document is printed. Possible values include: 0: Don't print comments. 1: Do print comments.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bprintNotesOpaqueDC_User
explainText:
Makes popups opaque regardless of other settings.

Prints the popups as opaque without honoring the popup opacity specified by the user in commenting preferences (popup-opacity). Possible values include: 0: Don't make popups opaque. 1: Do make popups opaque.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUserAskedToEnableAutoCompleteDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the user is asked to enable auto complete at runtime.

This option is enabled for the Advanced option. Possible values include: 0: Don't ask the user. 1: Do ask the user.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iShowOrderDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the type of grouping order to display in the touchup reading order panel.

Possible values include: 0: Order (numbered). 1: Structure type. 2: None.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRecordNewEntriesDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remember form field entries for use with future auto-complete actions.

This option is enabled for both the Basic and Advanced options. Possible values include: 0: Don't remember entries. 1: Do remember entries.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iRememberViewDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to restore last view settings when reopening documents.

Possible values include: 1: Don't restore the last view settings. 2: Do restore the last view settings.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Don't restore the last view settings
Do restore the last view settings

name: bRTLUIDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable right to left language options.

Possible values include: 0: Disable right to left language options. 1: Enable right to left language options.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDigitsUIDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to display digits in a way that's consistent with right to left language display.

The value is automatically set when bRTLUI is set via the UI. Possible values include: 0: Don't display digits in a way that's consistent with right to left language display. 1: Do display digits in a way that's consistent with right to left language display.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bPrintSaveTonerDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to optimize content so that the printer uses less ink.

When checked, this setting optimizes the content so that the printer uses less ink during printing. In some cases, toner savings may reach 15%. Print quality is usually not impaired in any discernable way. Possible values include: 0: Don't optimize printing. 1: Optimize printing.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSDIModeDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to open documents in a new window or in tabs in the same window.

Possible values include: 0: Open documents in tabs in the same window . 1: Open documents in separate windows.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bsendFinalApprovalEmailDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to send a notification email when the current approval is identified as the final one.

Only valid for an approval workflow. Possible values include: 0: Don't send an email on final approval. 1: Do send an email on final approval.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowOptionsDialogDC_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to display the options dialog when running an accessibility full check.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show options dialog. 1: Show options dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bcommentPanelOnImportDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to open the comment list when comments are imported.

Possible values include: 0: Don't open the comment list when comments are imported. 1: Do open the comment list when comments are imported.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowAnnotConnectorDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show lines connecting comment markups to their popups on mouse rollover.

Possible values include: 0: Hide lines connecting comments to popups. 1: Show lines connecting comments to popups.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFocusRectDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to surround a field with a rectangle when it has focus.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show a rectangle. 1: Do show a rectangle.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowKeyboardSelectionCursorDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the keyboard selection cursor should always be active in the document.

Select this option if you use a screen magnifier. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the cursor. 1: Always show the cursor.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bshowMarkupModifiersDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show markup tool-tips and text indicators.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show markup tool-tips and text indicators. 1: Show markup tool-tips and text indicators.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRulersVisibleDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show or hide rulers for every new document launch.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show rulers on new document launch. 1: Show rulers on new document launch.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bStampsPaletteInvisibleDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the stamps palette automatically when the commenting toolbar is displayed.

Possible values include: 0: Show the palette. 1: Don't show the palette.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowAnnotSequenceDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether to show tab order of fields for Acroforms and XFA forms.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bsideNotesDC_User
explainText:
Creates new popups aligned to the edge of the document.

Controls popup positioning. Possible values include: 0: Don't align popups at the document edge. 1: Align popups at the document edge.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAntialiasImagesDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use anti-aliasing (smoothing) for images.

Turning this preference off can improve scrolling performance in Citrix environments. Possible values include: 0: Don't smooth images. 1: Smooth images.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAntialiasGraphicsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use anti-aliasing (smoothing) for line art.

Turning this preference off can improve scrolling performance in Citrix environments. Possible values include: 0: Don't smooth line art. 1: Smooth line art.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAntialiasTextDC_User
explainText:
Anti-alias text when Smooth Text is Monitor or Laptop/LCD.

With benableDDR=1, DDR further smooths text on capable displays. Values: 0 = none; 1 = monitor and laptop/LCD.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSmoothZoomingDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether smooth zooming should be enabled.

Possible values include: 0: Disables smooth zooming 1: Enables smooth zooming
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSpellingUnderlineDC_User
explainText:
Turns off and on spell checking as you type.

This key is also duplicated under cPICommonPrefs\cSpelling.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bStoreNumericEntriesDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to store user entered numeric values.

This option is enabled for both the Basic and Advanced options. Possible values include: 0: Don't store numeric entries. 1: Do store numeric entries.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUseStructTabOrderDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use the PDF document structure for determining the tab order.

Possible values include: 0: Don't use document structure. 1: Use document structure.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUseSystemSelectionColorDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the default selection color (blue) is overridden with a color that the system specifies.

Possible values include: 0: Don't use the system selection color. 1: Use the system selection color.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUseLocalFontsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use local fonts.

Possible values include: 0: Don't use local fonts. 1: Do use local fonts.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iEmailClientSelectionDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the email client to use when submitting an XFA form.

Adobe's preference reference does not describe this value; use the URL column for the documentation link.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iRXOPolicyDC_User
explainText:
Sets XObject access to either Never (0), Always (1), or Only PDF/X-5 Compliant Ones (2).

The user must also set cRXOLocation and (Windows only) specify a privileged location for each parent (referencing) document. Possible values include: 0: Never 1: Always 2: Only PDF/X-5 Compliant Ones
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableLoggingDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable debug logging for Microsoft Purview Information Protection operations.

Useful for troubleshooting MIP label and authentication issues. Possible values include: 0: Disable MIP debug logging. 1: Enable MIP debug logging.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnablePolicyAuthenticationDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether MIP policy authentication is enabled for the current user.

Used alongside bShowDMB. Setting both bShowDMB and bEnablePolicyAuthentication to 0 hides the applied label from the current file. Possible values include: 0: Disable MIP policy authentication. 1: Enable MIP policy authentication.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowDMBDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show Microsoft Purview Information Protection label information in the document message bar.

Per-user preference under MicrosoftAIP. Possible values include: 0: Do not show MIP label info in the document message bar. 1: Show MIP label info in the document message bar.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: b3DEnableContentDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to trust and render 3D content.

This setting can be overridden by bEnable3D . Possible values include: 0: Don't trust and render 3D content. Show the Yellow Message Bar so the end user can trust the document. 1: Trust and render 3D files.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bCrossDomainLoggingDC_User
explainText:
Enable cross-domain logging for non-same-origin server communication.

Create an empty AcrobatCrossDomain.log in the user Application Data Adobe product folder.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tEditorFontNameDC_User
explainText: Specifies the font for the script editor.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tEditorFontSizeDC_User
explainText: Specifies the font size for the script editor.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tEditorPathDC_User
explainText:
Provides a path to an external editor.

The field becomes active when bChooseDialog is set to 1.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableJSDC_User
explainText:
Toggles JavaScript execution on and off globally; when off, the PDF cannot execute JavaScript.

Maps to Preferences > JavaScript > Enable Acrobat JavaScript. Default is 1 (enabled). If machine policy Block JavaScript Execution (bDisableJavaScript) is Enabled, it overrides this setting and locks JavaScript off; users cannot re-enable JavaScript via the Yellow Message Bar or Trusted Locations while that lock is in place.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableDebuggerDC_User
explainText:
Enables the debugger.

Requires an application restart.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bChooseDialogDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether or not to use the Acrobat editor or an external editor.

When true, the "Choose an external editor" field becomes enabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFIPSModeDC_User
explainText:
Turns FIPS mode on and off thereby requiring stronger encryption algorithm and limiting certain application behavior.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000345 (V-213193) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000955 (V-245874) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bConsoleInputDC_User
explainText: Toggles whether or not the console appears if script execution results in an error or message.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bConsoleOpenDC_User
explainText: Enables the interactive debugger console.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iExceptionsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies how exceptions should be handled.

Allowable values include: 0: Ignore 1: Trace 2: Break
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableGlobalSecurityDC_User
explainText:
Controls whether or not a script in one sandbox can access a script object in another sandbox.

By default, scripts can not access objects outside the current document sandbox. With 9.x and later, such communication only works in the standalone application since both the Acrobat and Reader browser-based viewer opens each window in a discrete browser instance.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableMenuItemsDC_User
explainText: Toggles off and on JavaScript's ability to execute menu items.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableAlwaysOutlookAttachmentProtectedViewDC_User
explainText:
Protected View for Outlook attachments.

Older Office versions may not mark download origin; such files may not auto-open in Protected View. Values: 0 = PV enabled for attachments; 1 = PV disabled for attachments.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bOldRecentFilesMigratedDC_User
explainText:
Indicates whether the recent files list has been migrated.

Admins should not change the preference value.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSaveBreakpointsDC_User
explainText:
Stores breakpoints in a PDF file

When enabled, stores JavaScript debugger breakpoints inside the PDF file so they persist across sessions.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUseExpiredTimestampsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether expired timestamps should be used.

If true, an expired timestamp will not invalidate a signature.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowConnectViaHTTPDC_User
explainText:
If true, the server connection URI uses the format HTTP server:port/path; otherwise, it uses the format HTTPS server:port/path.

In either case, if the connection fails, an error message appears. For more information, see Guidelines for Developing CSPs for Acrobat on Windows .
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowCertNonGreenDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a certification signature may be applied to a document containing Legal PDF warnings.

If false, then its not allowed and the author is informed of the reason.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowOCSPNoCheckDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether the OCSPNoCheck extension is allowed in the response signing certificate.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAlwaysConsultDC_User
explainText:
Determines when the URL is used for an additional URL CRL distribution point.

If false, the URL is only used when the certificate does not have a CRLDp extension.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iAuthMechanismsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies which registered provider(s) to use.

0: Use none of the registered providers. 1: Use first registered provider. 2: Use all registered providers.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Use none of the registered providers

name: iAutoAcceptEDCPrivacyNotificationDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show an alert confirming acceptance of the privacy policy.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show an alert. 1: Do show an alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iAutoAddLTVDC_User
explainText:
Auto-add LTV information to signatures.

Large LTV may prompt when over 10% of file size plus 10 KB. Choosing Do not show again and No sets this to 0. Values: 0 = never; 1 = ask if too big (default); 2 = always.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Ask whether to add LTV if too big (default)

name: bSavePasswordDC_User
explainText: Indicates whether the password has been cached for this server.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iMaxRevokeInfoCacheLifetimeDC_User
explainText:
Maximum lifetime in hours the cached CRL is used for revocation checking.

iMaxRevokeInfoCacheLifetime is only used if the validation method is set to "current time". Possible values include: The number of hours for which the cached CRL is valid.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bCustomPrefsCreatedDC_User
explainText:
Indicates whether a custom certificate specific preference (e.g. Identrus) has already been created and written to the registry.

If true, it doesn't get created again. Deleting or setting this key to 0 forces Acrobat to recreate custom certificate preferences after which it will reset this key to 1.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: aDefDirectoryDC_User
explainText:
Default directory when searching for digital IDs.

Windows only. ADSI directories from Security Settings Console use names like Adobe.PPKMS.ADSI.dir0. Not supported on Linux or Mac.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iDirectoryProviderDC_User
explainText:
Specifies a directory provider for signature validation.

0: Use none of the registered providers. 1: Use first registered provider. 2: Use all registered providers.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Use none of the registered providers

name: bEnforceSecureChannelDC_User
explainText:
Block signing when original and signed message digests differ.

Shows a warning on mismatch. Skipped for certs without a public key (e.g. DSA with omitted key). Do not enable if such certs are used. Values: 0 = no enforcement; 1 = enforce.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAutoLaunchAtDocCloseDC_User
explainText: Automatically examines the document for hidden content when it is closed.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAutoLaunchAtSendMailDC_User
explainText: Automatically examines the document for hidden content when it is sent in an email.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bExpiredCertGoOnlineDC_User
explainText:
Go online for revocation on expired certificates.

11.0.16+ invalidates signatures on expired certs without embedded revocation. Values: 0 = do not go online; 1 = go online (pre-11.0.16 behavior).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFDFRequestExcludeCertDC_User
explainText:
Similar to the bFDFRequestSave.

False includes the user's certificate in all certificate requests. True excludes it.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFDFExportSaveDC_User
explainText: Persists whether user chose to save (1) or email (0) the FDF during export.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFDFExportSignDC_User
explainText: Persists whether the user chose to sign the FDF during export.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFDFRequestSaveDC_User
explainText: Caches a user's answer to the question whether they want to save the request as an FDF or email it directly when that user requests a certificate.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFollowURIsFromAIADC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow the chain builder to follow URIs in AIA certificate extensions so that certificates can be downloaded if they are not available locally.

The default does not allow phone-home capability. CRLdps and OCSP AIA extensions do allow following URIs because they require that the certificate chain up to a trust anchor.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSigAPStatusIconDisableDC_User
explainText:
Controls whether the signature status icon is displayed in the signature appearance on the document.

If true, status icon is not displayed regardless of signature status. This setting overrides iDisplayValidIcon and bShowWarningForChanges.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: cDialogs_xSelHandlerDC_User
explainText:
The last on-screen coordinates of a handler's digital ID selection dialog

It is a subkey containing 4 keys: Top, Bottom, Left, and Right. This preference could be used by 3rd party handlers or by someone invoking a non-signing digital ID selection dialog via JavaScript.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: xDefEnrollmentURLDC_User
explainText: The destination URL when the user selects "Enroll at an online CA" while adding a new digital ID.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bIgnoreNextUpdateDC_User
explainText:
Use embedded OCSP when nextUpdate is absent (with iMaxClockSkew).

Supports long-term validation using signing-time responses. Values: 0 = apply iMaxClockSkew on both sides of validation time; 1 = if no nextUpdate, accept OCSP indefinitely.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iImportAddressBookDC_User
explainText:
Import addressbook.acrodata on new install.

Values: 0 = do not import, no prompt; 1 or null = prompt user (default); 2 = silent import.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Do not copy; user not prompted
Ask whether to install the address book (default)

name: bCertStoreImportEnableDC_User
explainText: If true, then users can import from MSCAPI certificate stores into their Trusted Identity Manager.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDontRemoveOverlappingDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remove hidden content when sanitizing a document.

During sanitization workflows, the app automatically rasterizes the document if overlapping content exists. This can result in a large file size increase. Disable this feature to avoid extremely large files. 0: Remove hidden (overlapping) content. 1: Do not remove hidden content when sanitizing a document.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: cReasonsDC_User
explainText:
Custom signing reason list.

Entries named t0, t1, etc. Overridable by document seed value. Defaults: author, reviewed, approving, attest accuracy, agree terms, agree portions.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bLoadSettingsFromURLAdobeDC_User
displayName: Load Security Settings from Server (Adobe Certificates) (User)
explainText:
Controls whether trust anchors are periodically downloaded from Adobe's certificate server.

0: Don't load settings from a URL. 1: Do load settings from a URL.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000335 (V-213191) Low; STIG AADC-CN-001320 (V-213138) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bLoadSettingsFromURLEUTLDC_User
displayName: Load Security Settings from Server (European Certificates) (User)
explainText:
Controls whether trust anchors are periodically downloaded from the European Union Trusted Lists (EUTL) server.

0: Don't load settings from a URL. 1: Do load settings from a URL.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000330 (V-213190) Low; STIG AADC-CN-000990 (V-213126) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tLoadSettingsNAMEDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the signing certificate for the imported settings file.

Admins can specify specific certificates that must be used to sign a settings file. 0: Allow Any Certificate 1: Any user-specified certificate
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bIsEnabledDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the signature revocation status is included in the signature.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable LTV and include the signature revocation status information in the signature. 1: Enable LTV.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iMaxRevInfoArchiveSizeDC_User
explainText:
The maximum size of the revocation archival information in kilobytes.

An attempt is made to store as much revocation information as possible without exceeding the limit. Note that older product versions may have a smaller supported size limit.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iMaxVerifySessionDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the maximum number of nested verification sessions allowed.

This is used to prevent the application from going into infinite loop verifying the OCSP and/or CRL signer certificates caused by incorrect OCSP and/or CRL certificate setup.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iCreateNewSigFieldAVAlertDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the alert asking whether a new signature field should be created.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show an alert. 1: Do show an alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnNonEmbFontLegPDFWarnDC_User
explainText:
Turns on and off warnings about non-embedded fonts.

A warning appears when the LegalPDF dictionary NonEmbeddedFonts attribute has a non zero value. Turning this value on causes a warning to appear in the PDF Signature Report which indicates the document contains unembedded fonts.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iSendNonceDC_User
explainText:
Specifies signature validation behavior with respect to nonces.

With 10.0, this preference replaces bSendNonce. Possible values include: 0: No nonces are sent. 1: Nonces are included in the OCSP request and expected to be present in the response and should match the request's nonce. 2: Nonces are included in the OCSP request, but if none are present in the response, their absence is ignored.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Send nonces; expect matching nonce in response
Send nonces; ignore absent nonce in response

name: iURLToConsultDC_User
explainText:
Specifies how the revocation checker chooses which responder to use.

Possible values include: 0: Use the AIA extension in the certificate. 1: Use the URL key in sURL. 2: Use the AIA extension in the certificate. If it is not present, use the URL key in sURL. 3: Use the OCSP request signer's certificate AIA extension. Relevant only if SignRequest is 0.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Use the AIA extension in the certificate
Use the URL key in sURL
Use AIA; if absent use URL key in sURL
Use OCSP request signer certificate AIA (SignRequest=0 only)

name: iResponseFreshnessDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the amount of time in minutes after the response's published thisUpdate time for which the response will be valid.

After that time, the response will be invalid.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowOpenFileDC_User
explainText:
Open non-PDF attachments in native applications.

Works with bSecureOpenFile and tBuiltInPermsList; any block setting prevents opening. Values: 0 = block; 1 = allow.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tLockboxIdDC_User
explainText:
Set if bSavePassword is not 0 to look up the password in a user's secure password cache.

This is not directly exposed via the user interface.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bPreviewModeBeforeSigningDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a signer is forced to use preview mode during signing.

If true, preview mode is automatically invoked on a sign action. Users should read the document message bar text, view a report about any warnings, and then choose Sign Document.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRequireAKIDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether the Authority Key Identifier extension must be present in a CRL.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRequireOCSPCertHashDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether a certificate public key hash extension must be present in OCSP responses.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iRequireReviewWarningsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the user is required to review document warnings before signing via the signing dialog.

Interacts with iShowDocumentWarnings. The possible values include: 0: Never 1: Show when certifying only 2: Always
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bReqSigPropRetrievalDC_User
explainText:
Require successful timestamp retrieval when signing.

On failure, signing aborts with an error instead of using local time. Values: 0 = best effort (local time fallback); 1 = must succeed.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRequireValidSigForChainingDC_User
explainText:
Stop chain building at invalid RSA signatures on intermediates.

Example: invalid ICA signature excludes the CA from the chain. Does not affect DSA. Values: 0 = build full chain; 1 = stop at invalid signature.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bReturnRevInfoToUserDC_User
explainText:
If true, the revocation information is maintained within the SignatureInfo object and can be retrieved through JavaScript.

For more information, see the Acrobat JavaScript Reference .
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iRevocationCheckerDC_User
explainText:
Specifies a provider for revocation checking.

0: Use none of the registered providers. 1: Use first registered provider. 2: Use all registered providers.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Use none of the registered providers

name: bRevCheckTrustDC_User
explainText:
Revocation-check intermediate (non-root) trust anchors.

Detects compromise of third-party trust anchors. Root and self-signed certs are exempt. Values: 0 = no check; 1 = check.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: aRSAPSSHashAlgorithmDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the hash algorithm used for RSA-PSS signing.

If bEnableRSAPSSSigning is enabled, this preference specifies the hash algorithm. If this preference is not present or has a null value, then the value specified by aSignHash is used. If aSignHash is not specified, then SHA256 is used. Possible values include: SHA1 SHA224 SHA256 SHA384 SHA512
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iRSAPSSSaltLengthDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the Salt Length the RSA-PSS algorithm uses.

When setting the salt length, you must assure the default base is hexadecimal. Either change the base to decimal or input its hex value. For example, if the salt length decimal value is 32, then set the hex value to 20.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableRSAPSSSigningDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a signature should be created with the RSA-PSS algorithm.

Possible values include: 0: Do not sign with the RSA-PSS algorithm. 1: Use the RSA-PSS algorithm.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tSAML_Assertion_SourceDC_User
explainText: Holds the URL of the authentication server from which the SAML assertion stored in cSAML_Assertion was obtained.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tSAML_Name_FormatDC_User
explainText:
SAML_NAME_ comprise the subject name identifier taken from the SAML assertion received during the account's last user authentication.

The identifier is essentially a machine-readable user name that is unaffected by the choice of authentication mechanisms.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tSAML_Name_QualifierDC_User
explainText:
SAML_NAME_ comprise the subject name identifier taken from the SAML assertion received during the account's last user authentication.

The identifier is essentially a machine-readable user name that is unaffected by the choice of authentication mechanisms.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iDigSigSaveAsCertifiedDC_User
explainText:
Controls whether to show an alert when saving a certified document.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show an alert. 1: Do show an alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSecureOpenFileDC_User
explainText:
Restrict attachment opens to PDF only.

Works with bAllowOpenFile and tBuiltInPermsList; any block setting prevents opening. Values: 0 = allow non-PDF; 1 = PDF only.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSelfSignCertGenDC_User
explainText:
Allow Create a self-signed ID in Add ID workflows.

Post-June 2016 products require bSelfSignCertGen=0 and bEnableCEFBasedUI=0 to fully block. Values: 0 = disallow; 1 = allow.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tServerURLDC_User
explainText: The default server URL.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowAllChainsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show all chains in the Certificate Viewer.

If true, the Certificate Viewer shows all the chains; otherwise, it shows only the trusted chain. If there are no trusted chains, then all the chains are shown and this preference is ignored.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iShowDocumentWarningsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a button to allow reviewing document warnings shows up on the signing dialog.

Interacts with iRequireReviewWarnings. The possible values include: 0: Never 1: Show when certifying only 2: Always
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowWarningForChangesDC_User
explainText:
Show blue info icon when a validated approval signature document changes after signing.

Does not affect certification signatures. Requires iDisplayValidIcon not set to 2. Values: 0 = no warning (green check); 1 = show warning.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowOtherInfoWhenSigningDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether the location and contact information UI will appear during signing.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowSignerWarningsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a warning that there is a greater forgery risk when revocation information is embedded in the signature.

Because this warning was removed from 10.x products, this preference is only applicable to 9.4.6 and later products in the 9.x line. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the warnings. 1: Do show the warnings.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iDisplayValidIconDC_User
explainText:
When to show signature status icon in appearance.

Value 2 disables bShowWarningForChanges and the GUI hide option. Does not affect Signatures pane icons. Values: 0 = always; 1 = except when valid; 2 = never.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Hide icon when signature is valid

name: bReqSigPropVerificationDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether signature property verification must succeed for a signature to be valid.

As of 8.0, the only property used is the timestamp URL.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iSigVerificationTimeDC_User
explainText:
Indicates the time at which signature validation should occur.

Possible values include: 0: Always carry out the verification at current time 1: Use the signing time if it's secure (e.g. timestamped), else use current time 2: Always use signing time
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Use signing time if secure, else current time

name: bAllowSigCertOnlyDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether any subsequent signers can sign a certified document containing LegalPDF warnings with additional approval signatures.

In other words, the presence of any LegalPDF warning prevents any additional signatures.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: isignDoneDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a dialog indicating that a document was successfully signed.

Possible values include: 0: Show the dialog after signing successfully. 1: Don't show the dialog after signing successfully.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowSigCertGreenOnlyDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether any subsequent signers can sign a certified document that does not contain LegalPDF warnings with additional approval signatures.

In other words, the presence of any LegalPDF warning does not prevent any additional signatures.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tSignHashDC_User
explainText:
A text entry that contains the OID of the hashing algorithm.

For an alternative, see aSignHash. Allowable values include: 1.2.840.113549.2.5: MD5 1.3.14.3.2.26: SHA1 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1: SHA256 (v. 7.0) 1.3.36.3.2.1: RIPEMD160 (v. 8.0) 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.2: SHA384 (v. 8.0) 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.3: SHA512 (v. 8.0)
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSignRequestDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the OCSP request should be signed.

Some OCSP providers require that OCSP requests are signed (e.g IdenTrust). 0: Don't sign the OCSP request. 1: Force Acrobat to sign OCSP requests prior to sending.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tContactInfoDC_User
explainText:
When bAllowOtherInfoWhenSigning is true (on), the signing dialog displays a location and contact field.

User data is saved and reused during subsequent signing events.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iHashAlgoDC_User
explainText:
Identifies the hashing algorithm used to hash the timestamped data.

The valid values are: 0: MD5 1: SHA1 2: SHA256 For an alternative, see sHashAlgo which supports more options.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iSizeDC_User
explainText: ASPKI requires the signature property to predict the size (in bytes) so that enough space can be set aside.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tServerDC_User
explainText:
The DNS server name (i.e. alrms.adobe.com).

There is no scheme specified.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bTrueTypeFontPDFSigQWarnDC_User
explainText: Turns on and off warnings about True Type fonts.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bTrustCertifiedDocumentsDC_User
explainText:
Trust certified documents as privileged locations.

Does not apply in Protected View. Lock via bEnableCertificateBasedTrust. Values: 0 or null = not trusted; 1 = trusted.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bTrustOSTrustedSitesDC_User
explainText:
Treat IE Trusted Sites and Local Intranet as privileged locations.

Local Intranet included since 10.1.2/9.5. Disable with bDisableOSTrustedSites. Values: 0 = do not trust OS zones; 1 = trust OS zones.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tHostPermsDC_User
explainText:
Stores trusted and blocked URLs when URL Access Permissions (iURLPerms) is set to Custom Setting (DWORD 0).

Pipe-separated Adobe TrustManager host permission list syntax: version:1|host:N where N is 2 (Allow) or 3 (Block).

Only effective when iURLPerms is 0; Allow or Block overrides this list.

Not lockable via HKLM - this preference only exists at User scope.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iURLPermsDC_User
explainText:
Allow, block, or custom website access.

Allow or Block resets tHostPerms; Custom uses tHostPerms. Values: 0 = custom; 1 = block all; 2 = allow all.

When set to Custom Setting (0), configure the URL list using the Trusted/Blocked URL List (tHostPerms) text policy.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tURLDC_User
explainText: The URL of the Roaming ID server.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iUseArchivedRevInfoDC_User
explainText:
Indicates whether the revocation information archived with the signature is used for revocation checking.

Allowable values include: 0: Never (always require fresh revocation information to be successfully downloaded). 1: Deprecated. Do not use. 2: Always use (if embedded revocation information is available do not download fresh revocation information).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

items.displayName: Always use embedded revocation if available

name: iValidityModelDC_User
explainText:
Signature and certificate validity model.

German signature law may require chain validation. Values: 0 = PKIX shell model; 1 = chain model (for qualified policy or chain model extension OIDs).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iMSStoreTrustedDC_User
explainText:
Trust Windows Certificate Store certs for signing and certifying.

Lock via bMSStoreTrusted. Values: 0x00 = none; 0x60 = validating signatures; 0x62 = certified documents and signatures.

Windows Store trust is a hex bitmask stored as a DWORD. Documented values: 0x00 (0) = no trust; 0x60 (96) = validating signatures; 0x62 (98) = validating certified documents and signatures. Other bit combinations may be set using the numeric control (0-255).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iSendMailDefaultAccountAlertDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a dialog should appear asking if a PDF should be sent via the user's default email account.

When a new user tries to send a PDF via email, a dialog appears and asks "How would you like to send this email." Users then need to select a choice and check Remember my choice . Possible values include: 0: Don't show the dialog. 1: Do show the dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDefaultSetDC_User
explainText:
Indicates whether a default email client has been set.

Possible values include: 0: Default webmail client is not set. 1: Default webmail client is set.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDisableSharedReviewDC_User
explainText:
Control cloud-based shared review availability.

For full DC Review disable, use bToggleAdobeReview or disable all services. Values: 0 = remove DC review option (legacy only); 1 = enable DC review.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bNeedSynchronizerDC_User
explainText:
Enable the synchronizer.

Used by services, AATL, shared reviews, and recent files (11.0.07+). Disabling not recommended. Acrobat and Reader use separate synchronizers. Values: 0 = disable; 1 = enable.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEnableFillSignDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remove the Fill and Sign pane without removing the Work with Certificates menu.

11.x products only. This setting allows users to remove the Acrobat Sign menu items without removing the menu item for using digital signatures on the local machine. Possible values include: 0: Remove the Fill and Sign pane. 1: Don't remove the Fill and Sign pane.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRemoveCommaDelimiterDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remove the comma in comma-delimited addressbook entries.

During shared review workflows, the user invokes the addressbook to invite participants. In cases where the addressbook is comma-delimited, pre DC versions of the product display an error dialog. Use this preference to remove commas. Possible values include: 0: Don't remove commas. 1: Remove commas.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowConnectDialogDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to display the Connect dialog in Shared Reviews.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the Connect dialog. 1: Do show the Connect dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bIsUsedShareReviewDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a popup tip that informs users of the collaborative review feature.

The popup only appears if the user has opened a review file but has not sent a review file. Once the user has initiated a review, the application sets this value to 1, and the popup no longer appears. Possible values include: 0: Show the tip. 1: Don't show the tip.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bIsUsedShareDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a popup tip that informs users of the share file feature.

The popup only appears if the user has opened a shared file but has not shared a file. Once the user has shared a file, the application sets this value to 1, and the popup no longer appears. Possible values include: 0: Show the tip. 1: Don't show the tip.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowWelcomeDialogDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Welcome dialog when a shared review is initiated.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the welcome dialog. 1: Do show the welcome dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bActivatedDC_User
explainText:
Records whether the application has been activated online after installation.

Possible values include: 0: Not activated 1: Activated
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bHasLaunchedDC_User
explainText:
Records whether the application has been launched after installation.

Possible values include: 0: Not launched 1: Launched
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAppInitializedDC_User
explainText:
Records whether the application has been initialized after installation.

Possible values include: 0: Not initialized 1: Initialized
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bLaunchedDC_User
explainText:
Caches whether or not the application has ever been launched.

Application behavior may vary across versions depending on whether the application has been launched. Possible values include: 0: The application has not been launched. 1: The application has been launched.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bIsAutoDocOpenFeatureEnabledDC_User
explainText:
Controls whether PDFs downloaded in Chrome or Edge automatically open in Acrobat or Reader.

Maps to Preferences > General > Always open PDFs downloaded from the web. Not a FeatureLockDown setting; users may be able to change it in the UI. Unified 64-bit Reader uses the Acrobat user hive, not Reader DC (User). Separate from the browser extension Open in Acrobat setting. Possible values include: 0: Do not auto-open downloaded PDFs. 1: Auto-open downloaded PDFs.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAutoOpenFromAllBrowsersDC_User
explainText:
Controls whether auto-open applies for PDFs downloaded from all supported browsers.

Companion to bIsAutoDocOpenFeatureEnabled under AutoDocOpen. Not a FeatureLockDown setting. Possible values include: 0: Do not auto-open from all supported browsers. 1: Auto-open from all supported browsers.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bIsAutoDocOpenEnabledForEdgeDC_User
explainText:
Controls whether PDFs downloaded in Microsoft Edge automatically open in Acrobat or Reader.

Companion to bIsAutoDocOpenFeatureEnabled under AutoDocOpen. Not a FeatureLockDown setting. Possible values include: 0: Do not auto-open PDFs downloaded in Edge. 1: Auto-open PDFs downloaded in Edge.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: EULAAcceptedForBrowserDC_User
explainText:
For Acrobat's browser plugin, caches whether the browser-based EULA has been accepted.

On Macintosh, this preference can not be set in the plist. Use the Mac Wizard or the PRTK tool. Reader uses the key EULA. If the EULA is not accepted, the application stops running after a set period of time. Possible values include: 0: Show the EULA because it has not been accepted. 1: Don't show the EULA.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bChooseLangAtStartupDC_User
explainText: Allows the user to choose the language at startup.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bCreateFormDiscoveryShownDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Create Form panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bEditDiscoveryShownDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Edit panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFillSignDiscoveryShownDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Fill & Sign panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bHideHelpWelcomeDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the Welcome menu item under Help.

Possible values include: 0 or null: Enable the Welcome menu item. 1: Disable the Welcome menu item.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShownHomeOnboardingDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to invoke the home onboarding tour when the modern viewer is invoked the first time.

Once the home onboarding tour displays, the app automatically resets this value to 0. This preference has no effect if AVGeneral/bEnableAv2 is 0. Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding tour (not yet shown). 1: Don't show the onboarding tour (already shown or declined).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bLoadAllPluginsAtStartupDC_User
explainText: Specifies whether all plugins should be loaded when the application is started.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bOrganizeDiscoveryShownDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Organize panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bUsePageCacheDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to cache pages that have been loaded.

Possible values include: 0: Don't cache pages. 1: Do cache pages
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bRedactDiscoveryShownDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Redaction panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDisplayAboutDialogDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether or not to display the startup splash screen at every launch.

Possible values include: 0: Don't display the startup splash screen. 1: Display the startup splash screen at every launch.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: idontShowAllImagesHaveAltTextDC_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to show an alert when a user executes the Set Alternate Text dialog and there are no images missing alternate text.

Possible values include: 0: Show alert. 1: Don't show alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bshowEULADC_User
explainText: Toggles on and off whether the end user license agreement appears.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bLastShowStatusDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show "Get Started with Acrobat" on startup.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the Getting Started page. 1: Show the Getting Started page.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowHorizontalScrollbarDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a horizontal scrollbar when the viewing area is narrower than the width of the loaded document.

Possible values include: 0: Disable the horizontal scrollbar. 1: Enable the horizontal scrollbar.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowExistingAttachedReportAlertDC_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to show an alert when a user tries to attach a report if there is already a report attached.

Possible values include: 0: Show alert. 1: Don't show alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: idontShowSetAltTextInfoDC_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to show an informative alert when a user executes the Set Alternate Text dialog.

Possible values include: 0: Show alert. 1: Don't show alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowedSkipCardDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the skipped onboarding coachmark.

Possible values include: 0: Disables the feature. 1: Enables the feature.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bSplashDisplayedAtStartupDC_User
explainText: Toggles whether the splash screen appears on startup.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDisplayedSplashDC_User
explainText:
Indicates whether or not the application has started up and invoked the splash screen.

Possible values include: 0: The splash screen has not been invoked yet. 1: The splash screen has been invoked.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bInTrialModeDC_User
explainText:
Records whether the application is operating in Trial Mode.

Possible values include: 0: Not in trial mode 1: In trial mode
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShownViewerOnboardingDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to invoke the new viewer onboarding tour when a PDF opens in the modern viewer the first time.

Once the viewer onboarding tour displays, the app automatically resets this value to 0. This preference has no effect if AVGeneral/bEnableAv2 is 0. Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding tour (not yet shown). 1: Don't show the onboarding tour (already shown or declined).
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iDelayBeforeQuitViewerDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the number of seconds the standalone application stays in memory before it shuts down.

Possible values include: 30 Any integer
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bDownloadEntireFileDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow background downloading of resources the view thinks it needs to properly display the PDF.

Possible values include: 0: Don't allow background downloading. 1: Do allow background downloading.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iDelayBeforeQuitBrowserDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the number of seconds the browser-based application stays in memory before it shuts down.

Possible values include: 30 Any integer
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bBrowserDisplayInReadModeDC_User
explainText:
Open browser PDFs in Read Mode.

Hides standard toolbars; compact menu appears on hover. Values: 0 = standard toolbars; 1 = Read Mode.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bInstalledCleanupCheckDoneDC_User
explainText: A preference used by the usage measurement feature to determine whether the previously set UsageMeasurement-related keys should be reset.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bLoadOnStartDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the collaboration executable should be invoked and run as a background process on startup.

When enabled, AdobeCollabSync.exe runs on application startup. This process is used for features like shared reviews and forms data collection . Possible values include: 0: Start the process. 1: Don't start the process.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAllowByteRangeRequestsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable Fast Web View by allowing display of the PDF before the entire file is downloaded.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable Fast Web View. 1: Enable Fast Web View.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFavoriteFilesRememberChoiceDC_User
explainText:
Specifies the user's choice

When a user selects "Ask every time" and iFavoriteFilesAccessOption is set to 0, this new preference remembers the user's choice for each file. Possible values include: Application generated.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bFavoritesStripInRFLDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show starred files in the recent files list.

A starred file is somewhat similar to a "favorited" file. Note that the lockable version of this preference is named bFavoritesFeaturesLockDown . Possible values include: 0: Show starred files in the recent files list. 1: Don't show starred files in the recent files list.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iFavoriteFilesAccessOptionDC_User
explainText:
Specifies what action to take when starring a file.

A starred file is somewhat similar to a "favorited" file. Possible values include: 0: Show a dialog and ask whether to save or upload. This option also results in creating a new bFavoriteFilesRememberChoice . 1: Upload to Document Cloud 2: Save the file locally
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bStoreCredentialsDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the user logon credentials for the Tracker should be stored.

Possible values include: 0: Don't store credentials. 1: Store credentials.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: iAVARMNoAutoUpdateWarningDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to turn off the "Updater has not been able to check for updates recently" dialog.

Possible values include: 0: Don't turn off the dialog. 1: Do turn off the dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bAcrobatAppInstalledDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Acrobat mobile app promotion and link in the Home banner.

Disable and lock both the App Center and Home banner with bToggleDCAppCenter under FeatureLockDown. Possible values include: 0: Promote the mobile app. 1: Don't promote the mobile app.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bScanAppInstalledDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Adobe Scan mobile app promotion and link in the Home banner.

Disable and lock both the App Center and Home banner with bToggleDCAppCenter under FeatureLockDown. Possible values include: 0: Promote the mobile app. 1: Don't promote the mobile app.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: bShowTrialNagDC_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a "Trial Expired" dialog should appear after 30 days.

This preference is automatically set by the application. When the 30 day trial period expires, Acrobat is launched in reduced functionality mode, and a dialog appears asking if the user would like to purchase the product. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the "Trial Expired" dialog. 1: "Trial Expired" dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Acrobat DC

name: tBaseFolderName_User
explainText:
An alias referring to a particular folder.

The two standard values are "install" and "user", which refer to the application-level Sequences folder and the user-level Sequences folders, respectively. The name can also refer to an administrator-specified folder. Possible values include: install user
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iColumnSelectHalo_User
explainText: Adobe's preference reference does not describe this value; use the URL column for the documentation link.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tFileFormat_User
explainText:
The version number associated with the file format.

The two valid values are "11" for an Acrobat 11-format .sequ file or "pre-11" for an Acrobat 10-or-earlier format .sequ file. Possible values include: Any valid version number.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAlwaysUseFileNameAsDocTitle_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use the PDF file name as the display name in the application's title bar.

PDF documents have an Initial View property that's set to "Document Title" by default. Enabling this preference overrides any document-level setting with the app-level setting. Possible values include: 0: Don't use file names. 1: Use file names for the PDF title.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseFixedSnapshotResolution_User
explainText: Adobe's preference reference does not describe this value; use the URL column for the documentation link.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: ADC4318556_User
explainText:
Enables playing 3D and multimedia content using a Flash player in PDF.

Since Flash is no longer supported, admins must install and configure the player. Possible values include: 0 or null: Don't play content with a Flash player. 1: Use the Flash player.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bHandSelects_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the hand tool should be able to select text and images.

With the DC 10/13/2015 release, this setting also works on Windows Touch devices. Possible values include: 0: Don't select text and images. 1: Select text and images.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iMaxMRUCntToBeStored_User
explainText:
Stores the number of recent files that should be listed in the recent files list.

The recent files list appears under the file menu (5 item limit), the splash screen (5 item limit), and in My Files View (100 item limit). A number from 0-100. The default is 100.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableAv2_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the modern viewer first released in July 2022.

0: Show the classic viewer. 1: Show the modern viewer.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowMultipleExpandedPanels_User
explainText:
Specifies whether multiple comment panels can be expanded.

Possible values include: 0: Don't allow more than one visible panel. 1: Do allow multiple visible panels.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iNumSwitcherContextualToolTipAV2Shown_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the "Acrobat has a new look" coachmark after launching Acrobat the first time.

Once the coachmark displays, the app automatically resets this value to 0. This preference has no effect if bEnableAv2 is 0. 0: Do not show the coachmark. 1: Show the coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bPinHUD_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to pin the HUD to the toolbar.

The application automatically creates this key when you click the "pin to menu" icon on the right-hand side of the HUD. Possible values include: 0: Don't pin the HUD to the toolbar. 1: Pin the HUD to the toolbar.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bPromptBeforeClosingMultipleTabs_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to warn the user before closing documents open in multiple tabs.

The ability to open documents in separate tabs was introduced in October, 2015. Possible values include: 0: Don't warn the user. 1: Warn the user.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bImagesFirst_User
explainText: Adobe's preference reference does not describe this value; use the URL column for the documentation link.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bInfobubble_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the popup tooltips for the Tools, Comments, and Share panes should appear.

Possible values include: 0: Disable popup tooltips. 1: Enable popup tooltips.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bKeyPrefsShowVirtualKeyoard_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the touch keyboard if device is in touch or tablet mode on Win 8 and later.

In general, the virtual keyboard should only appear on touch devices running Windows 8 and later where the user has detached a soft keyboard. The keyboard should appear when a user taps a text area such as a search box, comment popup, form field, and so on. Possible values include:
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iSnapshotResolution_User
explainText: Adobe's preference reference does not describe this value; use the URL column for the documentation link.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: irightPaneState_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to automatically open the Tools Pane on launch.

Possible values include: 0: Use the default. 1: Always closed. 2: Always open.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iBasicSharePaneStickyStatus_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remember the Tools Pane state across sessions.

For example, if the user closes the Tools Pane, it will not automatically open on launch. Interacts with irightPaneState. Possible values include: 0: Don't remember the Tool Pane's state. The Pane is always closed on application open. 1: Do remember the Tool Pane's state.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Don't remember the Tool Pane's state (always closed on launch)
Do remember the Tool Pane's state

name: iNumSwitcherContextualToolTipAVShown_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the "Try the new Acrobat/Reader" coachmark after launching Acrobat the first time.

Once the coachmark displays, the app automatically resets this value to 0. This preference has no effect if bEnableAv2 is 0. 0: Do not show the coachmark. 1: Show the coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iNumSessionAV2_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the UI switcher coachmark based on the number of user sessions.

Interacts with iNumSwitcherContextualToolTipAV2Shown . Possible values include: 0 or 1: Don't show the UI switcher. 2 or greater: Show the UI switcher if iNumSwitcherContextualToolTipAV2Shown is 0.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUse2DGPUf_User
explainText:
Specifies whether 2D graphics acceleration should be used.

Possible values include: 0: Disable 1: Enable
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowDocsToHideUI_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow documents to hide the menu bar, toolbars, and window controls.

Possible values include: 0: Don't allow documents to hide UI elements. 1: Allow documents to hide UI elements.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: benableTextSelection_User
explainText:
Enable text selection on highlight, strikethrough, and underline annotations.

Values: 0 = enabled (][ cursor after 2s hover, reverts after 3s outside); 1 = disabled (][ only via context menu).
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableAT_User
explainText:
Enable assistive technology workflows.

When AT such as JAWS is detected, prompts for setup assistant on untagged docs and OCR on scans. Values: 0 = disabled; 1 = enabled.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAttachLog_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to attach the accessibility report to the checked document after running accessibility full check.

Possible values include: 0: Don't attach the report. 1: Do attach the report.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAutoCompleteOnTab_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to auto complete form field entries on a tab key action.

This option is enabled when the Advanced option is selected. Possible values include: 0: Don't auto complete on tab. 1: Auto complete on tab.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bautoOpenOther_User
explainText:
Automatically adds a popup note when another type of annotation is added.

In other words, a popup note appears when you create a new comment using a drawing tool, the Stamp tool, or the Pencil tool. Possible values include: 0: Don't add a popup note for other annot types. 1: Do add a popup note for other annot types.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAutoSaveDocsEnabled_User
explainText:
Specifies whether or not to automatically save documents.

Interacts with iAutoSaveDocsInterval. Possible values include: 0: Don't auto save documents 1: Auto save documents.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iAutoSaveDocsInterval_User
explainText:
Specifies the time interval in minutes at which to automatically save docs.

Interacts with bAutoSaveDocsEnabled. Possible values include: 5: Minutes User specified: Any value 1-99
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAutoSetLayers_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow the document's layer state to be set by user information.

Possible values include: 0: Don't allow layer state to be set by user information. 1: Allow layer state to be set by user information.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iPages_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to check all pages of a document or a subset of pages when running an accessibility full check.

Possible values include: 0: Don't check all pages. 1: Do check all pages.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: benableDDR_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to further smooth text on LCD screens.

Text smoothing essentially has two levels. First, the text is anti-aliased. Then DDR technology is applied for devices which allow RGB bands to be painted in individual pixels to further smooth text (LCD screens). Possible values include: 0: None and Monitor 1: Laptop/LCD Screens.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iAccessColorPolicy_User
explainText:
Replace Document Colors panel policy.

When disabled, the key is removed from registry. Values: null = user choice; 1 = Windows color scheme; 2 = custom colors; 4 = high contrast.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bCombineContent_User
explainText:
Specifies whether similar content should be displayed together or separately.

Possible values include: 0: Do display similar content types together. 1: Don't display similar content types together.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tauthor_User
explainText:
The author name specified by balwaysUseIdent.

Possible values include: N/A: User specified.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tNoteFontName_User
explainText:
Sets the comment font name for the viewer.

The UI displays all the available fonts on the user system. The font is not embedded in the PDF; this preference merely controls the viewer's preference rather than the author's preference. Possible values include: Tahoma: May vary with available system fonts. N/A: User specified.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: dNoteFontSize_User
explainText:
Sets the font size.

The font is not embedded in the PDF; this preference merely controls the viewer's preference rather than the author's preference. Possible values include: 10: Font size. N/A: User specified.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bComplexScript_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable support for writing direction switching (complex script).

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable Writing Direction Switching. 1: Enable Writing Direction Switching.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bconfirmEBRMerge_User
explainText:
Displays an alert on document open asking the user to confirm importing comments into an active review.

Possible values include: 0: Disable confirmation alert on import. 1: Enable confirmation alert on import.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bcopyTextToDrawAnnot_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to copy the encircled text into drawing comment popups.

Adds a popup comment automatically to other markup types so that they can be annotated. Possible values include: 0: Don't copy the encircled text into comments. 1: Do copy the encircled text into comments.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bcopyTextToMarkupAnnot_User
explainText:
Copies the selected text into highlight, cross-out, and underline comment popups.

Adds a popup comment automatically to specified markup types so that they can be annotated. Possible values include: 0: Copy selected text. 1: Don't copy selected text.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bCreateLog_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to create an accessibility report when running an accessibility full check.

Possible values include: 0: Don't create report. 1: Do create report.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iPageViewLayoutMode_User
explainText:
Specifies the default page layout when a PDF opens.

These settings can be overridden by Accessibility settings such as bOverridePageLayout. Possible values include: null: Automatic 1: Single Page 2: Single Page Continuous 3: Two Up Continuous 5: Two Up
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iParaDir_User
explainText:
Specifies the paragraph direction.

Possible values include: 0: Left to Right 1: Right to Left 2: Infer from document
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iDefaultZoomType_User
explainText:
Specifies the default zoom type (other than a %) to use when a PDF opens.

% scales are stored in iZoomScale. Possible values include: 1: Fit Page (automatic) 2: Fit Width 3: Fit Height 4: Fit Visible 6: Reflow
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tDictionaryName_User
explainText:
Identifies the default spelling dictionary name.

The value is the name from cDictionaryOrder\t0. The dictionary ID can be found in cDictionaryOrderID\i0.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: imaxPDFCommentsSize_User
explainText:
Sets the comment threshold size for determining whether comments are embedded or sent as FDF files.

When collaboration involves sending comments with a PDF, comments below the threshold size are embedded in the document. Comments above the threshold size are sent as FDF files. Possible values include: 3: Max size for Reader (Acrobat is 5)
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bemptyContentToolTip_User
explainText:
Displays a tooltip stating the comment being hovered over is empty.

Possible values include: 0: Don't indicate comment is empty. 1: Do indicate comment is empty.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseThinCode_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enhance thin lines to improve visibility.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enhance thin lines. 1: Enhance thin lines.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSuperFastDrawing_User
explainText:
Use low-resolution rendering during scroll, zoom, and pan.

Temporarily shows lower quality during fast interactions. Values: 0 = high quality intermediates; 1 = superfast low-res intermediates.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iaskFormsSelectEmailCLient_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the dialog confirming selection of desktop vs. internet email on XFA form submit appears.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the confirmation dialog on each XFA form submit. 1: Do show the confirmation dialog on each XFA form submit.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bHidePopupIfShowSummary_User
explainText:
Hide comment popups when comment's list is open.

Possible values include: 0: Don't hide popups. 1: Do hide popups.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bHindiDigit_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable support for Hindi digits.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable Hindi digits. 1: Enable Hindi digits.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bHoveringPopups_User
explainText:
Automatically open popups on mouse rollover.

Possible values include: 0: Don't open popups on mouse rollover. 1: Do open popups on mouse rollover.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bInlineAutoComplete_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to auto complete a field based on remembered values when a user starts typing.

This option is enabled for both the Basic and Advanced options. Possible values include: 0: Don't auto complete. 1: Do autocomplete.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iIntlSelectFont_User
explainText:
Specifies the font to use.

Possible values include: 0: Application default 1: GB18030 compatible font 2: HKSCS compatible font
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bLigatures_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable support for ligatures.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable ligatures. 1: Enable ligatures.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: balwaysUseIdent_User
explainText:
Use login name as comment author.

Uses identity preferences login name, then login-name, then shared-review author. Default true for Acrobat, false for Reader. Values: 0 = use login name; 1 = do not use login name.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bOpenInPlace_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to open cross document links in the same window.

Possible values include: 0: Don't open links in the same window. 1: Do open links in the same window.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bOverprintPreviewUseShiftClick_User
explainText:
Shift+Click behavior in the output preview dialog.

Values: 0 = Shift+Click adds color-value sticky note; 1 = Shift+Click multi-select; Alt/Option+Click adds sticky note.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAccessOverrideDocColors_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to replace black text or line art colors when iAccessColorPolicy is enabled and a replacement color has been specified.

While the default is 1, the preference is not read unless iAccessPolicy is enabled (1). Possible values include: 0: Don't replace black text or line art colors. 1: Replace black text or line art colors.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC
