name: bOverrideLineArtColors_User
explainText:
Limits color changes to black text and line art when iAccessColorPolicy is enabled and a replacement color has been specified.

While the default is 1, the preference is not read unless "Accessibility" enabled (1). Possible values include: 0: Don't replace text or line art colors. 1: Replace text or line art colors. See also bAccessOverrideDocColors in Originals.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iPageLayout_User
explainText:
Specifies the user selected page layout override.

When bOverridePageLayout is set to 1, the override drop down list becomes enabled so that the user can set the desired page layout. Possible values include: 1: Single Page 2: Single Page Continuous 3: Two Up Continuous 5: Two Up
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bOverrideZoom_User
explainText:
Let users set a default zoom for all documents.

Overrides author Page Display settings and sets iZoomScale when enabled. Values: 0 = document default; 1 = enable zoom dropdown.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iZoomType_User
explainText:
Specifies the zoom scale for all other documents other than a % scale and overrides Page Display settings.

% scales are stored in iZoomScale. Possible values include: 1: Fit Page 2: Fit Width 3: Fit Height 4: Fit Visible 6: Reflow
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iParagraphDirection_User
explainText:
Specifies the paragraph direction.

Possible values include: 0: Right to Left 1: Left to Right
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bPopupsOpenIffSelected_User
explainText: Specifies whether to open a popup when it is selected.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseDetailsNavigator_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show portfolio component files and file details in an accessible list.

This preference replaces bUsePlatformNavigator. Files mode provides a better reading experience for people with disabilities such as mobility impairments, blindness, and low vision. Possible values include: 0: Don't show portfolio components in a list. 1: Do show portfolio components in a list.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bPrintAnnots_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to print notes, popups, and other annotations.

Setting a similar preference from the Print panel sets a corresponding setting in HKU. Possible values include: 0: Don't print annotations. 1: Do print annotations.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bprintCommentPopups_User
explainText:
Enables printing of comments and other annotations.

Notes and popups that are open will be printed when the rest of the document is printed. Possible values include: 0: Don't print comments. 1: Do print comments.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bprintNotesOpaque_User
explainText:
Makes popups opaque regardless of other settings.

Prints the popups as opaque without honoring the popup opacity specified by the user in commenting preferences (popup-opacity). Possible values include: 0: Don't make popups opaque. 1: Do make popups opaque.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUserAskedToEnableAutoComplete_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the user is asked to enable auto complete at runtime.

This option is enabled for the Advanced option. Possible values include: 0: Don't ask the user. 1: Do ask the user.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iShowOrder_User
explainText:
Specifies the type of grouping order to display in the touchup reading order panel.

Possible values include: 0: Order (numbered). 1: Structure type. 2: None.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bRecordNewEntries_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remember form field entries for use with future auto-complete actions.

This option is enabled for both the Basic and Advanced options. Possible values include: 0: Don't remember entries. 1: Do remember entries.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iRememberView_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to restore last view settings when reopening documents.

Possible values include: 1: Don't restore the last view settings. 2: Do restore the last view settings.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Don't restore the last view settings
Do restore the last view settings

name: bRTLUI_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable right to left language options.

Possible values include: 0: Disable right to left language options. 1: Enable right to left language options.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bDigitsUI_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to display digits in a way that's consistent with right to left language display.

The value is automatically set when bRTLUI is set via the UI. Possible values include: 0: Don't display digits in a way that's consistent with right to left language display. 1: Do display digits in a way that's consistent with right to left language display.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bPrintSaveToner_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to optimize content so that the printer uses less ink.

When checked, this setting optimizes the content so that the printer uses less ink during printing. In some cases, toner savings may reach 15%. Print quality is usually not impaired in any discernable way. Possible values include: 0: Don't optimize printing. 1: Optimize printing.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSDIMode_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to open documents in a new window or in tabs in the same window.

Possible values include: 0: Open documents in tabs in the same window . 1: Open documents in separate windows.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bsendFinalApprovalEmail_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to send a notification email when the current approval is identified as the final one.

Only valid for an approval workflow. Possible values include: 0: Don't send an email on final approval. 1: Do send an email on final approval.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowOptionsDialog_User
explainText:
Toggles whether to display the options dialog when running an accessibility full check.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show options dialog. 1: Show options dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bcommentPanelOnImport_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to open the comment list when comments are imported.

Possible values include: 0: Don't open the comment list when comments are imported. 1: Do open the comment list when comments are imported.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowAnnotConnector_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show lines connecting comment markups to their popups on mouse rollover.

Possible values include: 0: Hide lines connecting comments to popups. 1: Show lines connecting comments to popups.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFocusRect_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to surround a field with a rectangle when it has focus.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show a rectangle. 1: Do show a rectangle.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowKeyboardSelectionCursor_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the keyboard selection cursor should always be active in the document.

Select this option if you use a screen magnifier. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the cursor. 1: Always show the cursor.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bshowMarkupModifiers_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show markup tool-tips and text indicators.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show markup tool-tips and text indicators. 1: Show markup tool-tips and text indicators.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bStampsPaletteInvisible_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the stamps palette automatically when the commenting toolbar is displayed.

Possible values include: 0: Show the palette. 1: Don't show the palette.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowAnnotSequence_User
explainText: Specifies whether to show tab order of fields for Acroforms and XFA forms.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bsideNotes_User
explainText:
Creates new popups aligned to the edge of the document.

Controls popup positioning. Possible values include: 0: Don't align popups at the document edge. 1: Align popups at the document edge.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAntialiasImages_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use anti-aliasing (smoothing) for images.

Turning this preference off can improve scrolling performance in Citrix environments. Possible values include: 0: Don't smooth images. 1: Smooth images.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAntialiasGraphics_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use anti-aliasing (smoothing) for line art.

Turning this preference off can improve scrolling performance in Citrix environments. Possible values include: 0: Don't smooth line art. 1: Smooth line art.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAntialiasText_User
explainText:
Anti-alias text when Smooth Text is Monitor or Laptop/LCD.

With benableDDR=1, DDR further smooths text on capable displays. Values: 0 = none; 1 = monitor and laptop/LCD.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSmoothZooming_User
explainText:
Specifies whether smooth zooming should be enabled.

Possible values include: 0: Disables smooth zooming 1: Enables smooth zooming
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSpellingUnderline_User
explainText:
Turns off and on spell checking as you type.

This key is also duplicated under cPICommonPrefs\cSpelling.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bStoreNumericEntries_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to store user entered numeric values.

This option is enabled for both the Basic and Advanced options. Possible values include: 0: Don't store numeric entries. 1: Do store numeric entries.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseStructTabOrder_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use the PDF document structure for determining the tab order.

Possible values include: 0: Don't use document structure. 1: Use document structure.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseSystemSelectionColor_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the default selection color (blue) is overridden with a color that the system specifies.

Possible values include: 0: Don't use the system selection color. 1: Use the system selection color.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseLocalFonts_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to use local fonts.

Possible values include: 0: Don't use local fonts. 1: Do use local fonts.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iEmailClientSelection_User
explainText:
Specifies the email client to use when submitting an XFA form.

Adobe's preference reference does not describe this value; use the URL column for the documentation link.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iRXOPolicy_User
explainText:
Sets XObject access to either Never (0), Always (1), or Only PDF/X-5 Compliant Ones (2).

The user must also set cRXOLocation and (Windows only) specify a privileged location for each parent (referencing) document. Possible values include: 0: Never 1: Always 2: Only PDF/X-5 Compliant Ones
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableLogging_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to enable debug logging for Microsoft Purview Information Protection operations.

Useful for troubleshooting MIP label and authentication issues. Possible values include: 0: Disable MIP debug logging. 1: Enable MIP debug logging.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnablePolicyAuthentication_User
explainText:
Specifies whether MIP policy authentication is enabled for the current user.

Used alongside bShowDMB. Setting both bShowDMB and bEnablePolicyAuthentication to 0 hides the applied label from the current file. Possible values include: 0: Disable MIP policy authentication. 1: Enable MIP policy authentication.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowDMB_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show Microsoft Purview Information Protection label information in the document message bar.

Per-user preference under MicrosoftAIP. Possible values include: 0: Do not show MIP label info in the document message bar. 1: Show MIP label info in the document message bar.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: b3DEnableContent_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to trust and render 3D content.

This setting can be overridden by bEnable3D . Possible values include: 0: Don't trust and render 3D content. Show the Yellow Message Bar so the end user can trust the document. 1: Trust and render 3D files.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tBrokerLogfilePath_User
explainText:
Specifies the path and log file name for the Protected Mode log.

The value should be path + log filename. Logging is available for users who need to troubleshoot problems where a workflow or plugin does not work when Protected Mode is enabled. The log may provide guidance as to whether a custom policy file should be used to re-enable broken workflows or plugins. Any valid path.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bCrossDomainLogging_User
explainText:
Enable cross-domain logging for non-same-origin server communication.

Create an empty AcrobatCrossDomain.log in the user Application Data Adobe product folder.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableJS_User
explainText:
Toggles JavaScript execution on and off globally; when off, the PDF cannot execute JavaScript.

Maps to Preferences > JavaScript > Enable Acrobat JavaScript. Default is 1 (enabled). If machine policy Block JavaScript Execution (bDisableJavaScript) is Enabled, it overrides this setting and locks JavaScript off; users cannot re-enable JavaScript via the Yellow Message Bar or Trusted Locations while that lock is in place.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableDebugger_User
explainText:
Enables the debugger.

Requires an application restart.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFIPSMode_User
explainText:
Turns FIPS mode on and off thereby requiring stronger encryption algorithm and limiting certain application behavior.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000345 (V-213193) Medium; STIG AADC-CN-000955 (V-245874) Medium
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableGlobalSecurity_User
explainText:
Controls whether or not a script in one sandbox can access a script object in another sandbox.

By default, scripts can not access objects outside the current document sandbox. With 9.x and later, such communication only works in the standalone application since both the Acrobat and Reader browser-based viewer opens each window in a discrete browser instance.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableMenuItems_User
explainText: Toggles off and on JavaScript's ability to execute menu items.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableAlwaysOutlookAttachmentProtectedView_User
explainText:
Protected View for Outlook attachments.

Older Office versions may not mark download origin; such files may not auto-open in Protected View. Values: 0 = PV enabled for attachments; 1 = PV disabled for attachments.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bOldRecentFilesMigrated_User
explainText:
Indicates whether the recent files list has been migrated.

Admins should not change the preference value.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bUseExpiredTimestamps_User
explainText:
Specifies whether expired timestamps should be used.

If true, an expired timestamp will not invalidate a signature.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowConnectViaHTTP_User
explainText:
If true, the server connection URI uses the format HTTP server:port/path; otherwise, it uses the format HTTPS server:port/path.

In either case, if the connection fails, an error message appears. For more information, see Guidelines for Developing CSPs for Acrobat on Windows .
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowCertNonGreen_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a certification signature may be applied to a document containing Legal PDF warnings.

If false, then its not allowed and the author is informed of the reason.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowOCSPNoCheck_User
explainText: Specifies whether the OCSPNoCheck extension is allowed in the response signing certificate.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAlwaysConsult_User
explainText:
Determines when the URL is used for an additional URL CRL distribution point.

If false, the URL is only used when the certificate does not have a CRLDp extension.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iAuthMechanisms_User
explainText:
Specifies which registered provider(s) to use.

0: Use none of the registered providers. 1: Use first registered provider. 2: Use all registered providers.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Use none of the registered providers

name: iAutoAcceptEDCPrivacyNotification_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show an alert confirming acceptance of the privacy policy.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show an alert. 1: Do show an alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iAutoAddLTV_User
explainText:
Auto-add LTV information to signatures.

Large LTV may prompt when over 10% of file size plus 10 KB. Choosing Do not show again and No sets this to 0. Values: 0 = never; 1 = ask if too big (default); 2 = always.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Ask whether to add LTV if too big (default)

name: bSavePassword_User
explainText: Indicates whether the password has been cached for this server.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iMaxRevokeInfoCacheLifetime_User
explainText:
Maximum lifetime in hours the cached CRL is used for revocation checking.

iMaxRevokeInfoCacheLifetime is only used if the validation method is set to "current time". Possible values include: The number of hours for which the cached CRL is valid.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bCustomPrefsCreated_User
explainText:
Indicates whether a custom certificate specific preference (e.g. Identrus) has already been created and written to the registry.

If true, it doesn't get created again. Deleting or setting this key to 0 forces Acrobat to recreate custom certificate preferences after which it will reset this key to 1.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: aDefDirectory_User
explainText:
Default directory when searching for digital IDs.

Windows only. ADSI directories from Security Settings Console use names like Adobe.PPKMS.ADSI.dir0. Not supported on Linux or Mac.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iDirectoryProvider_User
explainText:
Specifies a directory provider for signature validation.

0: Use none of the registered providers. 1: Use first registered provider. 2: Use all registered providers.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Use none of the registered providers

name: bEnforceSecureChannel_User
explainText:
Block signing when original and signed message digests differ.

Shows a warning on mismatch. Skipped for certs without a public key (e.g. DSA with omitted key). Do not enable if such certs are used. Values: 0 = no enforcement; 1 = enforce.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAutoLaunchAtDocClose_User
explainText: Automatically examines the document for hidden content when it is closed.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAutoLaunchAtSendMail_User
explainText: Automatically examines the document for hidden content when it is sent in an email.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bExpiredCertGoOnline_User
explainText:
Go online for revocation on expired certificates.

11.0.16+ invalidates signatures on expired certs without embedded revocation. Values: 0 = do not go online; 1 = go online (pre-11.0.16 behavior).
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFDFRequestExcludeCert_User
explainText:
Similar to the bFDFRequestSave.

False includes the user's certificate in all certificate requests. True excludes it.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFDFExportSave_User
explainText: Persists whether user chose to save (1) or email (0) the FDF during export.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFDFExportSign_User
explainText: Persists whether the user chose to sign the FDF during export.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFDFRequestSave_User
explainText: Caches a user's answer to the question whether they want to save the request as an FDF or email it directly when that user requests a certificate.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFollowURIsFromAIA_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to allow the chain builder to follow URIs in AIA certificate extensions so that certificates can be downloaded if they are not available locally.

The default does not allow phone-home capability. CRLdps and OCSP AIA extensions do allow following URIs because they require that the certificate chain up to a trust anchor.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSigAPStatusIconDisable_User
explainText:
Controls whether the signature status icon is displayed in the signature appearance on the document.

If true, status icon is not displayed regardless of signature status. This setting overrides iDisplayValidIcon and bShowWarningForChanges.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: cDialogs_xSelHandler_User
explainText:
The last on-screen coordinates of a handler's digital ID selection dialog

It is a subkey containing 4 keys: Top, Bottom, Left, and Right. This preference could be used by 3rd party handlers or by someone invoking a non-signing digital ID selection dialog via JavaScript.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: xDefEnrollmentURL_User
explainText: The destination URL when the user selects "Enroll at an online CA" while adding a new digital ID.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bIgnoreNextUpdate_User
explainText:
Use embedded OCSP when nextUpdate is absent (with iMaxClockSkew).

Supports long-term validation using signing-time responses. Values: 0 = apply iMaxClockSkew on both sides of validation time; 1 = if no nextUpdate, accept OCSP indefinitely.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iImportAddressBook_User
explainText:
Import addressbook.acrodata on new install.

Values: 0 = do not import, no prompt; 1 or null = prompt user (default); 2 = silent import.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Do not copy; user not prompted
Ask whether to install the address book (default)

name: bCertStoreImportEnable_User
explainText: If true, then users can import from MSCAPI certificate stores into their Trusted Identity Manager.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: cReasons_User
explainText:
Custom signing reason list.

Entries named t0, t1, etc. Overridable by document seed value. Defaults: author, reviewed, approving, attest accuracy, agree terms, agree portions.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bLoadSettingsFromURLAdobe_User
displayName: Load Security Settings from Server (Adobe Certificates) (User)
explainText:
Controls whether trust anchors are periodically downloaded from Adobe's certificate server.

0: Don't load settings from a URL. 1: Do load settings from a URL.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000335 (V-213191) Low; STIG AADC-CN-001320 (V-213138) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bLoadSettingsFromURLEUTL_User
displayName: Load Security Settings from Server (European Certificates) (User)
explainText:
Controls whether trust anchors are periodically downloaded from the European Union Trusted Lists (EUTL) server.

0: Don't load settings from a URL. 1: Do load settings from a URL.

Security Reference: STIG ARDC-CN-000330 (V-213190) Low; STIG AADC-CN-000990 (V-213126) Low
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tLoadSettingsNAME_User
explainText:
Specifies the signing certificate for the imported settings file.

Admins can specify specific certificates that must be used to sign a settings file. 0: Allow Any Certificate 1: Any user-specified certificate
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bIsEnabled_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the signature revocation status is included in the signature.

Possible values include: 0: Don't enable LTV and include the signature revocation status information in the signature. 1: Enable LTV.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iMaxRevInfoArchiveSize_User
explainText:
The maximum size of the revocation archival information in kilobytes.

An attempt is made to store as much revocation information as possible without exceeding the limit. Note that older product versions may have a smaller supported size limit.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iMaxVerifySession_User
explainText:
Specifies the maximum number of nested verification sessions allowed.

This is used to prevent the application from going into infinite loop verifying the OCSP and/or CRL signer certificates caused by incorrect OCSP and/or CRL certificate setup.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iCreateNewSigFieldAVAlert_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the alert asking whether a new signature field should be created.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show an alert. 1: Do show an alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnNonEmbFontLegPDFWarn_User
explainText:
Turns on and off warnings about non-embedded fonts.

A warning appears when the LegalPDF dictionary NonEmbeddedFonts attribute has a non zero value. Turning this value on causes a warning to appear in the PDF Signature Report which indicates the document contains unembedded fonts.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iSendNonce_User
explainText:
Specifies signature validation behavior with respect to nonces.

With 10.0, this preference replaces bSendNonce. Possible values include: 0: No nonces are sent. 1: Nonces are included in the OCSP request and expected to be present in the response and should match the request's nonce. 2: Nonces are included in the OCSP request, but if none are present in the response, their absence is ignored.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Send nonces; expect matching nonce in response
Send nonces; ignore absent nonce in response

name: iURLToConsult_User
explainText:
Specifies how the revocation checker chooses which responder to use.

Possible values include: 0: Use the AIA extension in the certificate. 1: Use the URL key in sURL. 2: Use the AIA extension in the certificate. If it is not present, use the URL key in sURL. 3: Use the OCSP request signer's certificate AIA extension. Relevant only if SignRequest is 0.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Use the AIA extension in the certificate
Use the URL key in sURL
Use AIA; if absent use URL key in sURL
Use OCSP request signer certificate AIA (SignRequest=0 only)

name: iResponseFreshness_User
explainText:
Specifies the amount of time in minutes after the response's published thisUpdate time for which the response will be valid.

After that time, the response will be invalid.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowOpenFile_User
explainText:
Open non-PDF attachments in native applications.

Works with bSecureOpenFile and tBuiltInPermsList; any block setting prevents opening. Values: 0 = block; 1 = allow.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tLockboxId_User
explainText:
Set if bSavePassword is not 0 to look up the password in a user's secure password cache.

This is not directly exposed via the user interface.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bPreviewModeBeforeSigning_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a signer is forced to use preview mode during signing.

If true, preview mode is automatically invoked on a sign action. Users should read the document message bar text, view a report about any warnings, and then choose Sign Document.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bRequireAKI_User
explainText: Specifies whether the Authority Key Identifier extension must be present in a CRL.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bRequireOCSPCertHash_User
explainText: Specifies whether a certificate public key hash extension must be present in OCSP responses.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iRequireReviewWarnings_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the user is required to review document warnings before signing via the signing dialog.

Interacts with iShowDocumentWarnings. The possible values include: 0: Never 1: Show when certifying only 2: Always
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bReqSigPropRetrieval_User
explainText:
Require successful timestamp retrieval when signing.

On failure, signing aborts with an error instead of using local time. Values: 0 = best effort (local time fallback); 1 = must succeed.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bRequireValidSigForChaining_User
explainText:
Stop chain building at invalid RSA signatures on intermediates.

Example: invalid ICA signature excludes the CA from the chain. Does not affect DSA. Values: 0 = build full chain; 1 = stop at invalid signature.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bReturnRevInfoToUser_User
explainText:
If true, the revocation information is maintained within the SignatureInfo object and can be retrieved through JavaScript.

For more information, see the Acrobat JavaScript Reference .
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iRevocationChecker_User
explainText:
Specifies a provider for revocation checking.

0: Use none of the registered providers. 1: Use first registered provider. 2: Use all registered providers.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Use none of the registered providers

name: bRevCheckTrust_User
explainText:
Revocation-check intermediate (non-root) trust anchors.

Detects compromise of third-party trust anchors. Root and self-signed certs are exempt. Values: 0 = no check; 1 = check.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: aRSAPSSHashAlgorithm_User
explainText:
Specifies the hash algorithm used for RSA-PSS signing.

If bEnableRSAPSSSigning is enabled, this preference specifies the hash algorithm. If this preference is not present or has a null value, then the value specified by aSignHash is used. If aSignHash is not specified, then SHA256 is used. Possible values include: SHA1 SHA224 SHA256 SHA384 SHA512
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iRSAPSSSaltLength_User
explainText:
Specifies the Salt Length the RSA-PSS algorithm uses.

When setting the salt length, you must assure the default base is hexadecimal. Either change the base to decimal or input its hex value. For example, if the salt length decimal value is 32, then set the hex value to 20.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableRSAPSSSigning_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a signature should be created with the RSA-PSS algorithm.

Possible values include: 0: Do not sign with the RSA-PSS algorithm. 1: Use the RSA-PSS algorithm.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tSAML_Assertion_Source_User
explainText: Holds the URL of the authentication server from which the SAML assertion stored in cSAML_Assertion was obtained.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tSAML_Name_Format_User
explainText:
SAML_NAME_ comprise the subject name identifier taken from the SAML assertion received during the account's last user authentication.

The identifier is essentially a machine-readable user name that is unaffected by the choice of authentication mechanisms.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tSAML_Name_Qualifier_User
explainText:
SAML_NAME_ comprise the subject name identifier taken from the SAML assertion received during the account's last user authentication.

The identifier is essentially a machine-readable user name that is unaffected by the choice of authentication mechanisms.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iDigSigSaveAsCertified_User
explainText:
Controls whether to show an alert when saving a certified document.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show an alert. 1: Do show an alert.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSecureOpenFile_User
explainText:
Restrict attachment opens to PDF only.

Works with bAllowOpenFile and tBuiltInPermsList; any block setting prevents opening. Values: 0 = allow non-PDF; 1 = PDF only.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSelfSignCertGen_User
explainText:
Allow Create a self-signed ID in Add ID workflows.

Post-June 2016 products require bSelfSignCertGen=0 and bEnableCEFBasedUI=0 to fully block. Values: 0 = disallow; 1 = allow.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tServerURL_User
explainText: The default server URL.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowAllChains_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show all chains in the Certificate Viewer.

If true, the Certificate Viewer shows all the chains; otherwise, it shows only the trusted chain. If there are no trusted chains, then all the chains are shown and this preference is ignored.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iShowDocumentWarnings_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a button to allow reviewing document warnings shows up on the signing dialog.

Interacts with iRequireReviewWarnings. The possible values include: 0: Never 1: Show when certifying only 2: Always
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowWarningForChanges_User
explainText:
Show blue info icon when a validated approval signature document changes after signing.

Does not affect certification signatures. Requires iDisplayValidIcon not set to 2. Values: 0 = no warning (green check); 1 = show warning.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowOtherInfoWhenSigning_User
explainText: Specifies whether the location and contact information UI will appear during signing.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowSignerWarnings_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a warning that there is a greater forgery risk when revocation information is embedded in the signature.

Because this warning was removed from 10.x products, this preference is only applicable to 9.4.6 and later products in the 9.x line. Possible values include: 0: Don't show the warnings. 1: Do show the warnings.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iDisplayValidIcon_User
explainText:
When to show signature status icon in appearance.

Value 2 disables bShowWarningForChanges and the GUI hide option. Does not affect Signatures pane icons. Values: 0 = always; 1 = except when valid; 2 = never.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Hide icon when signature is valid

name: bReqSigPropVerification_User
explainText:
Specifies whether signature property verification must succeed for a signature to be valid.

As of 8.0, the only property used is the timestamp URL.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iSigVerificationTime_User
explainText:
Indicates the time at which signature validation should occur.

Possible values include: 0: Always carry out the verification at current time 1: Use the signing time if it's secure (e.g. timestamped), else use current time 2: Always use signing time
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Use signing time if secure, else current time

name: bAllowSigCertOnly_User
explainText:
Specifies whether any subsequent signers can sign a certified document containing LegalPDF warnings with additional approval signatures.

In other words, the presence of any LegalPDF warning prevents any additional signatures.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: isignDone_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show a dialog indicating that a document was successfully signed.

Possible values include: 0: Show the dialog after signing successfully. 1: Don't show the dialog after signing successfully.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAllowSigCertGreenOnly_User
explainText:
Specifies whether any subsequent signers can sign a certified document that does not contain LegalPDF warnings with additional approval signatures.

In other words, the presence of any LegalPDF warning does not prevent any additional signatures.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tSignHash_User
explainText:
A text entry that contains the OID of the hashing algorithm.

For an alternative, see aSignHash. Allowable values include: 1.2.840.113549.2.5: MD5 1.3.14.3.2.26: SHA1 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1: SHA256 (v. 7.0) 1.3.36.3.2.1: RIPEMD160 (v. 8.0) 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.2: SHA384 (v. 8.0) 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.3: SHA512 (v. 8.0)
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bSignRequest_User
explainText:
Specifies whether the OCSP request should be signed.

Some OCSP providers require that OCSP requests are signed (e.g IdenTrust). 0: Don't sign the OCSP request. 1: Force Acrobat to sign OCSP requests prior to sending.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tContactInfo_User
explainText:
When bAllowOtherInfoWhenSigning is true (on), the signing dialog displays a location and contact field.

User data is saved and reused during subsequent signing events.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iHashAlgo_User
explainText:
Identifies the hashing algorithm used to hash the timestamped data.

The valid values are: 0: MD5 1: SHA1 2: SHA256 For an alternative, see sHashAlgo which supports more options.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iSize_User
explainText: ASPKI requires the signature property to predict the size (in bytes) so that enough space can be set aside.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tServer_User
explainText:
The DNS server name (i.e. alrms.adobe.com).

There is no scheme specified.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bTrueTypeFontPDFSigQWarn_User
explainText: Turns on and off warnings about True Type fonts.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bTrustCertifiedDocuments_User
explainText:
Trust certified documents as privileged locations.

Does not apply in Protected View. Lock via bEnableCertificateBasedTrust. Values: 0 or null = not trusted; 1 = trusted.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bTrustOSTrustedSites_User
explainText:
Treat IE Trusted Sites and Local Intranet as privileged locations.

Local Intranet included since 10.1.2/9.5. Disable with bDisableOSTrustedSites. Values: 0 = do not trust OS zones; 1 = trust OS zones.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tHostPerms_User
explainText:
Stores trusted and blocked URLs when URL Access Permissions (iURLPerms) is set to Custom Setting (DWORD 0).

Pipe-separated Adobe TrustManager host permission list syntax: version:1|host:N where N is 2 (Allow) or 3 (Block).

Only effective when iURLPerms is 0; Allow or Block overrides this list.

Not lockable via HKLM - this preference only exists at User scope.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iURLPerms_User
explainText:
Allow, block, or custom website access.

Allow or Block resets tHostPerms; Custom uses tHostPerms. Values: 0 = custom; 1 = block all; 2 = allow all.

When set to Custom Setting (0), configure the URL list using the Trusted/Blocked URL List (tHostPerms) text policy.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: tURL_User
explainText: The URL of the Roaming ID server.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iUseArchivedRevInfo_User
explainText:
Indicates whether the revocation information archived with the signature is used for revocation checking.

Allowable values include: 0: Never (always require fresh revocation information to be successfully downloaded). 1: Deprecated. Do not use. 2: Always use (if embedded revocation information is available do not download fresh revocation information).
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

items.displayName: Always use embedded revocation if available

name: iValidityModel_User
explainText:
Signature and certificate validity model.

German signature law may require chain validation. Values: 0 = PKIX shell model; 1 = chain model (for qualified policy or chain model extension OIDs).
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iMSStoreTrusted_User
explainText:
Trust Windows Certificate Store certs for signing and certifying.

Lock via bMSStoreTrusted. Values: 0x00 = none; 0x60 = validating signatures; 0x62 = certified documents and signatures.

Windows Store trust is a hex bitmask stored as a DWORD. Documented values: 0x00 (0) = no trust; 0x60 (96) = validating signatures; 0x62 (98) = validating certified documents and signatures. Other bit combinations may be set using the numeric control (0-255).
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: iSendMailDefaultAccountAlert_User
explainText:
Specifies whether a dialog should appear asking if a PDF should be sent via the user's default email account.

When a new user tries to send a PDF via email, a dialog appears and asks "How would you like to send this email." Users then need to select a choice and check Remember my choice . Possible values include: 0: Don't show the dialog. 1: Do show the dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bDefaultSet_User
explainText:
Indicates whether a default email client has been set.

Possible values include: 0: Default webmail client is not set. 1: Default webmail client is set.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bDisableSharedReview_User
explainText:
Control cloud-based shared review availability.

For full DC Review disable, use bToggleAdobeReview or disable all services. Values: 0 = remove DC review option (legacy only); 1 = enable DC review.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bNeedSynchronizer_User
explainText:
Enable the synchronizer.

Used by services, AATL, shared reviews, and recent files (11.0.07+). Disabling not recommended. Acrobat and Reader use separate synchronizers. Values: 0 = disable; 1 = enable.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEnableFillSign_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remove the Fill and Sign pane without removing the Work with Certificates menu.

11.x products only. This setting allows users to remove the Acrobat Sign menu items without removing the menu item for using digital signatures on the local machine. Possible values include: 0: Remove the Fill and Sign pane. 1: Don't remove the Fill and Sign pane.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bRemoveCommaDelimiter_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to remove the comma in comma-delimited addressbook entries.

During shared review workflows, the user invokes the addressbook to invite participants. In cases where the addressbook is comma-delimited, pre DC versions of the product display an error dialog. Use this preference to remove commas. Possible values include: 0: Don't remove commas. 1: Remove commas.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowConnectDialog_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to display the Connect dialog in Shared Reviews.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the Connect dialog. 1: Do show the Connect dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bShowWelcomeDialog_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the Welcome dialog when a shared review is initiated.

Possible values include: 0: Don't show the welcome dialog. 1: Do show the welcome dialog.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bActivated_User
explainText:
Records whether the application has been activated online after installation.

Possible values include: 0: Not activated 1: Activated
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bHasLaunched_User
explainText:
Records whether the application has been launched after installation.

Possible values include: 0: Not launched 1: Launched
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bAppInitialized_User
explainText:
Records whether the application has been initialized after installation.

Possible values include: 0: Not initialized 1: Initialized
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bLaunched_User
explainText:
Caches whether or not the application has ever been launched.

Application behavior may vary across versions depending on whether the application has been launched. Possible values include: 0: The application has not been launched. 1: The application has been launched.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bChooseLangAtStartup_User
explainText: Allows the user to choose the language at startup.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bCreateFormDiscoveryShown_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Create Form panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bEditDiscoveryShown_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Edit panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: EULA_User
explainText:
Accept EULA for the built-in updater.

Alternative to EULA_ACCEPT=YES at install time. Values: 0 = not accepted; 1 = accepted.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bFillSignDiscoveryShown_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to show the onboarding coachmark when the user invokes the Fill & Sign panel.

Possible values include: 0: Show the onboarding coachmark. 1: Don't show the onboarding coachmark.
supportedOn: Adobe Reader DC

name: bHideHelpWelcome_User
explainText:
Specifies whether to disable the Welcome menu item under Help.

name: AllowBuildPreview
displayName: Toggle user control over Insider builds
explainText:
This policy setting determines whether users can get preview builds of Windows, by configuring controls in Settings > Update and security > Windows Insider Program.

If you enable or do not configure this policy setting, users can download and install preview builds of Windows by configuring Windows Insider Program settings.

If you disable this policy setting, Windows Insider Program settings will be unavailable to users through the Settings app.

This policy is only supported up to Windows 10, Version 1703. Please use 'Manage preview builds' under 'Windows Update for Business' for newer Windows 10 versions.
supportedOn: Windows Server 2016, Windows 10 up to Version 1703

name: AppCompatPrevent16BitMach
explainText:
Specifies whether to prevent the MS-DOS subsystem (ntvdm.exe) from running on this computer. This setting affects the launching of 16-bit applications in the operating system.

You can use this setting to turn off the MS-DOS subsystem, which will reduce resource usage and prevent users from running 16-bit applications. To run any 16-bit application or any application with 16-bit components, ntvdm.exe must be allowed to run. The MS-DOS subsystem starts when the first 16-bit application is launched. While the MS-DOS subsystem is running, any subsequent 16-bit applications launch faster, but overall resource usage on the system is increased.

If the status is set to Enabled, the MS-DOS subsystem is prevented from running, which then prevents any 16-bit applications from running. In addition, any 32-bit applications with 16-bit installers or other 16-bit components cannot run.

If the status is set to Disabled, the MS-DOS subsystem runs for all users on this computer.

If the status is set to Not Configured, the OS falls back on a local policy set by the registry DWORD value HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\WOW\DisallowedPolicyDefault. If that value is non-0, this prevents all 16-bit applications from running. If that value is 0, 16-bit applications are allowed to run. If that value is also not present, on Windows 10 and above the OS will launch the 16-bit application support control panel to allow an elevated administrator to make the decision; on windows 7 and downlevel, the OS will allow 16-bit applications to run.

Note:  This setting appears in only Computer Configuration.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2003

name: AppCompatRemoveProgramCompatPropPage
explainText:
This policy controls the visibility of the Program Compatibility property page shell extension.  This shell extension is visible on the property context-menu of any program shortcut or executable file.

The compatibility property page displays a list of options that can be selected and applied to the application to resolve the most common issues affecting legacy applications.  Enabling this policy setting removes the property page from the context-menus, but does not affect previous compatibility settings applied to application using this interface.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2003

name: AppCompatTurnOffApplicationImpactTelemetry
explainText:
The policy controls the state of the Application Telemetry engine in the system.

Application Telemetry is a mechanism that tracks anonymous usage of specific Windows system components by applications.

Turning Application Telemetry off by selecting "enable" will stop the collection of usage data.

If the customer Experience Improvement program is turned off, Application Telemetry will be turned off regardless of how this policy is set.

Disabling telemetry will take effect on any newly launched applications. To ensure that telemetry collection has stopped for all applications, please reboot your machine.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: AppCompatTurnOffSwitchBack
explainText:
The policy controls the state of the Switchback compatibility engine in the system. 

Switchback is a mechanism that provides generic compatibility mitigations to older applications by providing older behavior to old applications and new behavior to new applications. 

Switchback is on by default.

If you enable this policy setting, Switchback will be turned off. Turning Switchback off may degrade the compatibility of older applications. This option is useful for server administrators who require performance and are aware of compatibility of the applications they are using. 

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, the Switchback will be turned on.

Please reboot the system after changing the setting to ensure that your system accurately reflects those changes.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: AppCompatTurnOffEngine
explainText:
This policy controls the state of the application compatibility engine in the system.

The engine is part of the loader and looks through a compatibility database every time an application is started on the system.  If a match for the application is found it provides either run-time solutions or compatibility fixes, or displays an Application Help message if the application has a know problem.

Turning off the application compatibility engine will boost system performance.  However, this will degrade the compatibility of many popular legacy applications, and will not block known incompatible applications from installing.  (For Instance: This may result in a blue screen if an old anti-virus application is installed.)

The Windows Resource Protection and User Account Control features of Windows use the application compatibility engine to provide mitigations for application problems. If the engine is turned off, these mitigations will not be applied to applications and their installers and these applications may fail to install or run properly.

This option is useful to server administrators who require faster performance and are aware of the compatibility of the applications they are using.  It is particularly useful for a web server where applications may be launched several hundred times a second, and the performance of the loader is essential.

NOTE: Many system processes cache the value of this setting for performance reasons.  If you make changes to this setting, please reboot to ensure that your system accurately reflects those changes.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2003

name: AppCompatTurnOffProgramCompatibilityAssistant_1
explainText: This setting exists only for backward compatibility, and is not valid for this version of Windows. To configure the Program Compatibility Assistant, use the 'Turn off Program Compatibility Assistant' setting under Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Application Compatibility.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: AppCompatTurnOffProgramCompatibilityAssistant_2
explainText:
This policy setting controls the state of the Program Compatibility Assistant (PCA).
      
The PCA monitors applications run by the user. When a potential compatibility issue with an application is detected, the PCA will prompt the user with recommended solutions.  To configure the diagnostic settings for the PCA, go to System->Troubleshooting and Diagnostics->Application Compatibility Diagnostics. 

If you enable this policy setting, the PCA will be turned off. The user will not be presented with solutions to known compatibility issues when running applications. Turning off the PCA can be useful for system administrators who require better performance and are already aware of application compatibility issues. 

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, the PCA will be turned on. To configure the diagnostic settings for the PCA, go to System->Troubleshooting and Diagnostics->Application Compatibility Diagnostics.

Note: The Diagnostic Policy Service (DPS) and Program Compatibility Assistant Service must be running for the PCA to run. These services can be configured by using the Services snap-in to the Microsoft Management Console.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: AppCompatTurnOffUserActionRecord
explainText:
This policy setting controls the state of Steps Recorder.

Steps Recorder keeps a record of steps taken by the user. The data generated by Steps Recorder can be used in feedback systems such as Windows Error Reporting to help developers understand and fix problems. The data includes user actions such as keyboard input and mouse input, user interface data, and screen shots.  Steps Recorder includes an option to turn on and off data collection.

If you enable this policy setting, Steps Recorder will be disabled.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, Steps Recorder will be enabled.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: AppCompatTurnOffProgramInventory
explainText:
This policy setting controls the state of the Inventory Collector.      

The Inventory Collector inventories applications, files, devices, and drivers on the system and sends the information to Microsoft.  This information is used to help diagnose compatibility problems.

If you enable this policy setting, the Inventory Collector will be turned off and data will not be sent to Microsoft. Collection of installation data through the Program Compatibility Assistant is also disabled.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, the Inventory Collector will be turned on.

Note: This policy setting has no effect if the Customer Experience Improvement Program is turned off. The Inventory Collector will be off.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2008 R2 or Windows 7

name: TurnOffInstallTracing
explainText:
This policy controls the state of Install Tracing. Install Tracing is a mechanism that tracks application installs to help diagnose compatibility problems.

If you enable this policy, Install Tracing will not be run.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, Install Tracing will be turned on.
supportedOn: At least Windows 11 Version 24H2

name: TurnOffAPISampling
explainText:
This policy controls the state of API Sampling. API Sampling monitors the sampled collection of application programming interfaces used during system runtime to help diagnose compatibility problems.

If you enable this policy, API Sampling will not be run.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, API Sampling will be turned on.
supportedOn: At least Windows 11 Version 24H2

name: TurnOffApplicationFootprint
explainText:
This policy controls the state of Application Footprint. Application Footprint monitors the sampled collection of registry and file usage to help diagnose compatibility problems.

If you enable this policy, Application Footprint will not be run.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, Application Footprint will be turned on.
supportedOn: At least Windows 11 Version 24H2

name: TurnOffWin32AppBackup
displayName: Turn off compatibility scan for backed up applications
explainText:
This policy controls the state of the compatibility scan for backed up applications. The compatibility scan for backed up applications evaluates for compatibility problems in installed applications.

If you enable this policy, the compatibility scan for backed up applications will not be run.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, the compatibility scan for backed up applications will be run.
supportedOn: At least Windows 11 Version 24H2

name: TurnOffApplicationInboxDependencyData
displayName: Turn off application inbox dependency component
explainText:
This policy controls the state of the application inbox dependency component. The application inbox dependency component tracks application dependencies for compatibility problems.

If you enable this policy, the application inbox dependency component will not be run.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, the application inbox dependency component may run.
supportedOn: At least Windows 11 Version 24H2

name: AppHVSI_AllowAppHVSIConfig
displayName: Turn on Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Managed Mode
explainText:
This policy setting enables application isolation through Microsoft Defender Application Guard.

Application Guard uses Windows Hypervisor to create a virtualized environment for apps that are configured to use virtualization-based security isolation. While in isolation, improper user interactions and app vulnerabilities can’t compromise the kernel or any other apps running outside of the virtualized environment.

If you enable this setting, Application Guard is turned on for your organization.
supportedOn: Windows 10 Enterprise, Windows 10 Education, or later

presentationElements.label:
Options:
0. Disable Microsoft Defender Application Guard
1. Enable Microsoft Defender Application Guard for Microsoft Edge ONLY
2. Enable Microsoft Defender Application Guard for isolated Windows environments ONLY
3. Enable Microsoft Defender Application Guard for Microsoft Edge AND isolated Windows environments

name: AppHVSI_ClipboardConfig
displayName: Configure Microsoft Defender Application Guard clipboard settings
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to decide how the clipboard behaves while in Microsoft Defender Application Guard.

If you enable this setting, you must choose from the following behaviors:

- Disable clipboard functionality completely between the host and Application Guard

- Enable the clipboard to copy content from Application Guard to the host

- Enable the clipboard to copy content from the host to Application Guard.

Note:
We recommend that you don't enable copying from the host to Application Guard. If you enable this functionality, a potentially compromised Application Guard session will have access to the host device’s clipboard and its content.

If you choose to enable copying, you must also choose the type of content that can be copied, by using the content options:

- 1. Allows text copying.

- 2. Allows image copying.

- 3. Allows both text and image copying.

If you disable or don't configure this setting, all clipboard functionality is turned off in Application Guard.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

items.displayName: Enable clipboard operation from an isolated session to the host
Enable clipboard operation from an host to the isolated session

name: AppHVSI_CertificateThumbprints
displayName: Allow Microsoft Defender Application Guard to use Root Certificate Authorities from the user’s device
explainText:
This policy setting allows certain device level Root Certificates to be shared with the Microsoft Defender Application Guard container.

If you enable this setting, certificates with a thumbprint matching the ones specified will be transferred into the container. Multiple certificates can be specified by using a comma to separate the thumbprints for each certificate you want to transfer.

If you disable or don’t configure this setting, certificates are not shared with the Microsoft Defender Application Guard container.

Example:  b4e72779a8a362c860c36a6461f31e3aa7e58c14,1b1d49f06d2a697a544a1059bd59a7b058cda924
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

presentationElements.label: Thumbprints of the certificates to share

name: AppHVSI_PrintingConfig
displayName: Configure Microsoft Defender Application Guard print settings
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to decide how the print functionality behaves while in Microsoft Defender Application Guard.

If you enable this setting, you must choose one or many of the following behaviors:

- Disable all print functionality in Application Guard.

- Enable printing to existing network printers.

- Enable printing to local printers.

- Enable printing to PDF, allows people to print as PDF and save the resulting file on the host.

- Enable printing to XPS, allows people to print as XPS and save the resulting file on the host.

If you disable or don't configure this setting, all print functionality is turned off in Application Guard.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

presentationElements.label: Allowed print types in Application Guard.

To determine which types of printing to allow, you must choose:
     - 0. Disables all print functionality.
     - 1. Enables only XPS printing.
     - 2. Enables only PDF printing.
     - 3. Enables both PDF and XPS printing.
     - 4. Enables only local printing.
     - 5. Enables both local and XPS printing.
     - 6. Enables both local and PDF printing.
     - 7. Enables local, PDF, and XPS printing.
     - 8. Enables only network printing.
     - 9. Enables both network and XPS printing.
     - 10. Enables both network and PDF printing.
     - 11. Enables network, PDF, and XPS printing.
     - 12. Enables both network and local printing.
     - 13. Enables network, local, and XPS printing.
     - 14. Enables network, local, and PDF printing.
     - 15. Enables all printing.

name: AppHVSI_BlockNonEnterpriseContentConfig
displayName: Prevent enterprise websites from loading non-enterprise content in Microsoft Edge and Internet Explorer
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to decide whether websites can load non-enterprise content in Microsoft Edge and Internet Explorer.

If you enable this setting, non-enterprise content embedded on enterprise sites are stopped from opening in Internet Explorer or Microsoft Edge outside of Microsoft Defender Application Guard.

If you disable or don't configure this setting, non-enterprise sites can open outside of the Microsoft Defender Application Guard container, directly in Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

name: AppHVSI_AllowCameraMicrophoneRedirectionConfig
displayName: Allow camera and microphone access in Microsoft Defender Application Guard
explainText:
The policy allows you to determine whether applications inside Microsoft Defender Application Guard can access the device’s camera and microphone when these settings are enabled on the user’s device.

If you enable this policy, applications inside Microsoft Defender Application Guard will be able to access the camera and microphone on the user’s device.

If you disable or don't configure this policy, applications inside Microsoft Defender Application Guard will be unable to access the camera and microphone on the user’s device.

Important: If you turn on this policy, a compromised container could bypass camera and microphone permissions and access the camera and microphone without the user’s knowledge. To prevent unauthorized access, we recommend that camera and microphone privacy settings be turned off on the user’s device when they are not needed.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

name: AppHVSI_AllowPersistence
displayName: Allow data persistence for Microsoft Defender Application Guard
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to decide whether data should persist across different sessions in Microsoft Defender Application Guard.

If you enable this setting, Application Guard saves user-downloaded files and other items (such as, cookies, Favorites, and so on) for use in future Application Guard sessions.

Note:
If you enable this setting, you can still delete a user's data from a specific device using the Reset-ApplicationGuard PowerShell command. Running this command deletes all employee data, regardless of configuration, and can result in data loss for the employee.

If you disable or don't configure this setting, Application Guard deletes all user data within the Application Guard container.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

name: AppHVSI_AllowVirtualGPU
displayName: Allow hardware-accelerated rendering for Microsoft Defender Application Guard
explainText:
This policy setting determines whether Microsoft Defender Application Guard renders graphics using hardware or software acceleration.

If you enable this setting, Microsoft Defender Application Guard uses Hyper-V to access supported, high-security rendering graphics hardware (GPUs). These GPUs improve rendering performance and battery life while using Microsoft Defender Application Guard, particularly for video playback and other graphics-intensive use cases. If you enable this setting without connecting any high-security rendering graphics hardware, Microsoft Defender Application Guard will automatically revert to software-based (CPU) rendering.

Note:
Be aware that enabling this setting with potentially compromised graphics devices or drivers might pose a risk to the host device.

If you disable or don’t configure this setting, Microsoft Defender Application Guard uses software-based (CPU) rendering and won’t load any third-party graphics drivers or interact with any connected graphics hardware.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

name: AppHVSI_AuditApplicationGuardConfig
displayName: Allow auditing events in Microsoft Defender Application Guard
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to decide whether auditing events can be collected from Microsoft Defender Application Guard.

If you enable this setting, Application Guard inherits auditing policies from your device and logs system events from the Application Guard container to your host.

If you disable or don't configure this setting, event logs aren't collected from your Application Guard container.
supportedOn: Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

name: AppHVSI_SaveFilesToHost
displayName: Allow files to download and save to the host operating system from Microsoft Defender Application Guard
explainText:
This policy setting determines whether to save downloaded files to the host operating system from the Microsoft Defender Application Guard container.

If you enable this setting, people can save downloaded files from the Microsoft Defender Application Guard container to the host operating system.

If you disable or don't configure this setting, people can't save downloaded files from the Microsoft Defender Application Guard container to the host operating system.
supportedOn: Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 Enterprise or Windows 10 Education with Microsoft Defender Application Guard in Enterprise mode

name: LetAppsAccessAccountInfo
displayName: Let Windows apps access account information
explainText:
This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access account information.

You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name. You can get the Package Family Name for an app by using the Get-AppPackage Windows PowerShell cmdlet. A per-app setting overrides the default setting.

If you choose the "User is in control" option, employees in your organization can decide whether Windows apps can access account information by using Settings > Privacy on the device.

If you choose the "Force Allow" option, Windows apps are allowed to access account information and employees in your organization cannot change it.

If you choose the "Force Deny" option, Windows apps are not allowed to access account information and employees in your organization cannot change it.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, employees in your organization can decide whether Windows apps can access account information by using Settings > Privacy on the device.

If an app is open when this Group Policy object is applied on a device, employees must restart the app or device for the policy changes to be applied to the app.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

If you choose the "User is in control" option, employees in your organization can decide whether Windows apps can access text content from foreground applications by using Settings > Privacy on the device.

If you choose the "Force Allow" option, Windows apps are allowed to access text content from foreground applications and employees in your organization cannot change it.

If you choose the "Force Deny" option, Windows apps are not allowed to access text content from foreground applications and employees in your organization cannot change it.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, employees in your organization can decide whether Windows apps can access text content from foreground applications by using Settings > Privacy on the device.

If an app is open when this Group Policy object is applied on a device, employees must restart the app or device for the policy changes to be applied to the app.

name: Reporting_Server_Policy
explainText:
Reporting Server URL: Displays the URL of reporting server.

      Reporting Time: When the client data should be reported to the server. Acceptable range is 0~23, corresponding to the 24 hours in a day. A good practice is, don't set this time to a busy hour, e.g. 9AM.
      
      Delay reporting for the random minutes: The maximum minutes of random delay on top of the reporting time. For a busy system, the random delay will help reduce the server load.
      
      Repeat reporting for every (days): The periodical interval in days for sending the reporting data.
      
      Data Cache Limit: This value specifies the maximum size in megabytes (MB) of the XML cache for storing reporting information. The default value is 20 MB. The size applies to the cache in memory. When the limit is reached, the log file will roll over. When a new record is to be added (bottom of the list), one or more of the oldest records (top of the list) will be deleted to make room. A warning will be logged to the Client log and the event log the first time this occurs, and will not be logged again until after the cache has been successfully cleared on transmission and the log has filled up again.

      Data Block Size: This value specifies the maximum size in bytes to transmit to the server at once on a reporting upload, to avoid permanent transmission failures when the log has reached a significant size. The  default value is 65536. When transmitting report data to the server, one block at a time of application records that is less than or equal to the block size in bytes of XML data will be removed from the cache and sent to the server. Each block will have the general Client data and global package list data prepended, and these will not factor into the block size calculations; the potential exists for an extremely large package list to result in transmission failures over low bandwidth or unreliable connections.

name: AppxDeploymentAllowAllTrustedApps
displayName: Allow all trusted apps to install
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to manage the installation of trusted line-of-business (LOB) or developer-signed packaged Microsoft Store apps.

If you enable or do not configure this policy setting, you can install any LOB or developer-signed packaged Microsoft Store app (which must be signed with a certificate chain that can be successfully validated by the local computer).

If you disable this policy setting, you cannot install LOB or developer-signed packaged Microsoft Store apps.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012, Windows 8 or Windows RT

name: AllowAutomaticAppArchiving
explainText:
This policy setting controls whether the system can archive infrequently used apps.

If you enable this policy setting, then the system will periodically check for and archive infrequently used apps.

If you disable this policy setting, then the system will not archive any apps.

If you do not configure this policy setting (default), then the system will follow default behavior, which is to periodically check for and archive infrequently used apps, and the user will be able to configure this setting themselves.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: AllowDeploymentInSpecialProfiles
displayName: Allow deployment operations in special profiles
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to manage the deployment of packaged Microsoft Store apps when the user is signed in using a special profile. Special profiles are the following user profiles, where changes are discarded after the user signs off:

Roaming user profiles to which the "Delete cached copies of roaming profiles" Group Policy setting applies

Mandatory user profiles and super-mandatory profiles, which are created by an administrator

Temporary user profiles, which are created when an error prevents the correct profile from loading

User profiles for the Guest account and members of the Guests group


If you enable this policy setting, Group Policy allows deployment operations (adding, registering, staging, updating, or removing an app package) of packaged Microsoft Store apps when using a special profile.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, Group Policy blocks deployment operations of packaged Microsoft Store apps when using a special profile.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012, Windows 8 or Windows RT

name: AllowDevelopmentWithoutDevLicense
displayName: Allows development of packaged Microsoft Store apps and installing them from an integrated development environment (IDE)
explainText:
Allows or denies development of Microsoft Store applications and installing them directly from an IDE.

        If you enable this setting and enable the "Allow all trusted apps to install" Group Policy, you can develop Microsoft Store apps and install them directly from an IDE.

        If you disable or do not configure this setting, you cannot develop Microsoft Store apps or install them directly from an IDE.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012, Windows 8 or Windows RT

name: DisableDeploymentToNonSystemVolumes
displayName: Disable installing Windows apps on non-system volumes
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to manage installing Windows apps on additional volumes such as secondary partitions, USB drives, or SD cards.

        If you enable this setting, you can't move or install Windows apps on volumes that are not the system volume.

        If you disable or do not configure this setting, you can move or install Windows apps on other volumes.
supportedOn: At least Windows 8.1 Update 2

name: RestrictAppDataToSystemVolume
displayName: Prevent users' app data from being stored on non-system volumes
explainText:
Prevent users' app data from moving to another location when an app is moved or installed on another location.

        If you enable this setting, all users' app data will stay on the system volume, regardless of where the app is installed.

        If you disable or do not configure this setting, then when an app is moved to a different volume, the users' app data will also move to this volume.
supportedOn: At least Windows 8.1 Update 2

name: AllowSharedLocalAppData
displayName: Allow a Windows app to share application data between users
explainText:
Manages a Windows app's ability to share data between users who have installed the app.

        If you enable this policy, a Windows app can share app data with other instances of that app. Data is shared through the SharedLocal folder. This folder is available through the Windows.Storage API.

        If you disable this policy, a Windows app can't share app data with other instances of that app. If this policy was previously enabled, any previously shared app data will remain in the SharedLocal folder.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: BlockNonAdminUserInstall
displayName: Prevent non-admin users from installing packaged Windows apps
explainText:
Manages non-Administrator users' ability to install Windows app packages.

        If you enable this policy, non-Administrators will be unable to initiate installation of Windows app packages. Administrators who wish to install an app will need to do so from an Administrator context (for example, an Administrator PowerShell window). All users will still be able to install Windows app packages via the Microsoft Store, if permitted by other policies.

        If you disable or do not configure this policy, all users will be able to initiate installation of Windows app packages.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10

name: ConfigureMSIXAuthenticationAuthorizedDomains
displayName: Set authorized domains for HTTPS authentication in MSIX streaming install
explainText:
This policy setting determines whether an EntraID OAuth token will be included in HTTPS communications to a specified fully qualified domain name for performing an MSIX streaming installation.

If you enable this policy setting, HTTPS communications to the predefined fully qualified domains will incorporate the user's EntraID OAuth token when performing a streaming MSIX install. The value provided is a regular expression (ECMA Script) that will be used to match against the uppercased, fully qualified domain of the URL.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, the user's EntraID OAuth token will only be shared with the default configured domains.
supportedOn: At least Windows 11 Version 22H2

name: DisableBackgroundAutoUpdates
displayName: Not allow sideloaded apps to auto-update in the background
explainText:
Manages a sideloaded apps' ability to auto-update in the background.

        If you enable this policy, sideloaded apps will not auto-update in the background.

        If you disable this policy, sideloaded apps will auto-update in the background.

        Default is 'disabled' (key not present).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10 Version 2106

name: DisableMeteredNetworkBackgroundAutoUpdates
displayName: Not allow sideloaded apps to auto-update in the background on a metered network
explainText:
Manages a sideloaded apps' ability to auto-update in the background on a metered network.

        If you enable this policy, sideloaded apps will not auto-update in the background on a metered network.

        If you disable this policy, sideloaded apps will auto-update in the background on a metered network.

        Default is 'disabled' (key not present).
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2016, Windows 10 Version 2106

displayName: Not allow per-user unsigned packages to install by default (requires explicitly allow per install)
explainText:
Not allow per-user unsigned packages to install by default (requires explicitly allow per install)

        If you enable this policy, the AllowUnsigned option defaults to 'false'.

        If you disable this policy, the AllowUnsigned option defaults to 'true'.

        Default is 'disabled' (key not present).
