name: ScreenShare_Allow
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, screen sharing is always allowed for specified origins.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, screen sharing requests follow the default policy.
supportedOn: Firefox 142 or later, Firefox 140.2 ESR or later

name: ScreenShare_Block
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, screen sharing is blocked for specified origins.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, screen sharing requests follow the default policy.
supportedOn: Firefox 142 or later, Firefox 140.2 ESR or later

name: ScreenShare_BlockNewRequests
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, sites that are not in the Allow policy cannot request screen sharing.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, any site that is not in the Block policy can request screen sharing.
supportedOn: Firefox 142 or later, Firefox 140.2 ESR or later

name: ScreenShare_Locked
displayName: Do not allow screen sharing preferences to be changed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, screen sharing preferences cannot be changed by the user.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change their screen sharing preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 142 or later, Firefox 140.2 ESR or later

name: DefaultBrowserSettingEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled or not configured, the user can set Firefox as the default browser.

If this policy is disabled, the default browser check is disabled and the controls for setting Firefox as the default browser are removed from Firefox preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 154 or later, Firefox 153 ESR or later

name: DefaultDownloadDirectory
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can set the default directory for downloads. ${home} can be used for the native home path.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default Firefox download directory is used.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: DownloadDirectory
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can set and lock the directory for downloads. ${home} can be used for the native home path.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default Firefox download directory is used and the user can change it.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: DNSOverHTTPS_Enabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, DNS over HTTPS is disabled.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, DNS Over HTTPS is enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DNSOverHTTPS_ProviderURL
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the URL specified is used as the provider URL.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default provider is used.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DNSOverHTTPS_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, DNS over HTTPS settings cannot be changed by the user.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, DNS over HTTPS settings can be changed by the user.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DNSOverHTTPS_ExcludedDomains
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the specified domains are excluded from DNS over HTTPS.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no domains are excluded from DNS over HTTPS.
supportedOn: Firefox 75 or later, Firefox 68.7 ESR or later

name: DNSOverHTTPS_Fallback
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, Firefox will not fallback to your default DNS resolver if there is a problem with the secure DNS provider.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, Firefox will use your default DNS resolver if there is a problem with the secure DNS provider.
supportedOn: Firefox 124 or later, Firefox 115.9 ESR or later

name: DisableAppUpdate
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the browser does not receive updates.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the browser receives updates.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableBuiltinPDFViewer
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, PDF files are not viewed within Firefox.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, PDF files are viewed within Firefox.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableDefaultBrowserAgent
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the default browser agent is disabled.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default browser agent is enabled.

For more information about the default browser agent, see https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/toolkit/mozapps/defaultagent/default-browser-agent/index.html
supportedOn: Firefox 75 or later, Firefox 68.7 ESR or later

name: DisableDeveloperTools
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, web developer tools are not available within Firefox.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, web developer tools are available within Firefox.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableFeedbackCommands
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the "Submit Feedback" and "Report Deceptive Site" menu items are not available from the help menu.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the "Submit Feedback" and "Report Deceptive Site" menu items are available from the help menu.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableFirefoxAccounts
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox Accounts is disabled which includes disabling Sync.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox Accounts and Sync are available.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableFirefoxScreenshots
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox Screenshots is not available.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox Screenshots is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableFirefoxStudies
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will never run SHIELD studies or do Heartbeat surveys.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can choose to enable SHIELD studies or Heartbeat surveys.

For more information, see https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/shield and https://wiki.mozilla.org/Firefox/Shield/Heartbeat
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableForgetButton
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the "Forget" button is not available.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the "Forget" button is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableFormHistory
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will not remember form or search history.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will remember form and search history.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableLaunchOnLogin
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox does not launch automatically when the user logs in. Any existing launch-on-login entry is removed and the "Open Firefox automatically when your computer starts up" checkbox in Settings > General > Startup is hidden.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user controls whether Firefox launches on login.
supportedOn: Firefox 155 or later

name: HardwareAcceleration
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, hardware acceleration is disabled and cannot be enabled.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, hardware acceleration is enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 62 or later, Firefox 60.2 ESR or later

name: DisableMasterPasswordCreation
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot create a master password.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can create a master password.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisablePasswordReveal
displayName: Do not allow passwords to be revealed in saved logins
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot show passwords in saved logins.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can show passwords in saved logins.
supportedOn: Firefox 71 or later, Firefox 68.3 ESR or later

name: DisablePocket
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Pocket is not available.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Pocket is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisablePrivateBrowsing
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, private browsing is not allowed.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, private browsing is allowed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableProfileImport
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you cannot import data from other browsers.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, you can import data from other browsers.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableProfileRefresh
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the "Refresh Firefox" button is not available on the about:support page or on support.mozilla.org.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the "Refresh Firefox" button is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableSafeMode
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot restart the browser into safe mode.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, safe mode is allowed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableSetDesktopBackground
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot set an image as their desktop background.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can set images as their desktop background.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableSystemAddonUpdate
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, new system add-ons will not be installed and existing system add-ons will not be updated.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, system add-ons are installed and updated.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisableTelemetry
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, telemetry is not uploaded.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, telemetry is collected and uploaded.

Mozilla recommends that you do not disable telemetry. Information collected through telemetry helps us build a better product for businesses like yours.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisplayBookmarksToolbar
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the bookmarks toolbar is displayed by default. The user can still hide it.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the bookmarks toolbar is not displayed by default.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisplayBookmarksToolbar_Enum
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the default bookmarks toolbar display can be configured.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the bookmarks toolbar is displayed on the new tab page by default.
supportedOn: Firefox 109 or later, Firefox 102.7 ESR or later

name: DisplayMenuBar
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the menu bar is displayed by default. The user can still hide it.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the menu bar is not displayed by default.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DisplayMenuBar_Enum
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can choose whether or not the menu bar is displayed and whether or not the user can show and hide the menu bar.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the menu bar is not displayed by default.
supportedOn: Firefox 73 or later, Firefox 68.5 ESR or later

name: Extensions_Install
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a list of extension URLs or paths that will be installed when Firefox is started.
Anytime this list is changed, the extensions will be reinstalled.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no extensions are installed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: Extensions_Uninstall
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a list of extension IDs that will be uninstalled.
Anytime this list is changed, the extensions will be uninstalled.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no extensions are uninstalled.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: Extensions_Locked
displayName: Prevent extensions from being disabled or removed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a list of extension IDs that the user will be unable to uninstall or disable.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no extensions are locked.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: ExtensionSettings
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can use JSON to describe the extension management policy.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, extensions will not be managed.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/extensionsettings/.
supportedOn: Firefox 69 or later, Firefox 68.1 ESR or later

name: ExtensionSettingsOneLine
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can use JSON to describe the extension management policy.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, extensions will not be managed.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/extensionsettings/.
supportedOn: Firefox 69 or later, Firefox 68.1 ESR or later

name: NoDefaultBookmarks
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the default bookmarks and Smart Bookmarks (Most Visited, Recent Tags) are not created.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, default bookmarks and Smart Bookmarks (Most Visited, Recent Tags) are created.

Note: this policy is only effective if used before the first run of the profile.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: DontCheckDefaultBrowser
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox does not check to see if it is the default browser at startup.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox checks to see if it is the default browser at startup.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: ExtensionUpdate
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, extensions will not be updated automatically.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, extensions will be updated automatically.
supportedOn: Firefox 67 or later, Firefox 60.7 ESR or later

name: LegacyProfiles
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will not try to create different profiles for installations of Firefox in different directories. This is the equivalent of the MOZ_LEGACY_PROFILES environment variable.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will create a new profile for each unique installation of Firefox.
supportedOn: Firefox 70 or later, Firefox 68.2 ESR or later

name: LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will revert to the legacy behavior of SameSite. This means that cookies that don't explicitly specify a SameSite attribute are treated as if they were SameSite=None.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will enforce SameSite=lax.
supportedOn: Firefox 96 or later

name: LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList
displayName: Revert to legacy SameSite behavior on specific domains
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will revert to the legacy behavior of SameSite for the specified domains. This means that cookies that don't explicitly specify a SameSite attribute are treated as if they were SameSite=None.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will enforce SameSite=lax for all domains.
supportedOn: Firefox 96 or later

name: LocalFileLinks
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify origins where linking to local files is allowed.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, websites can't link to local files.
supportedOn: Firefox 68.5 ESR or later

name: NetworkPrediction
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, network prediction (DNS prefetching) will be disabled.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, network prediction (DNS prefetching) will be enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 67 or later, Firefox 60.7 ESR or later

name: NewTabPage
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the new tab page will be blank.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, the new tab page will be the default.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: OfferToSaveLogins
explainText:
If this policy is enabled or not configured, Firefox will offer to save website logins and passwords.

If this policy is disabled, Firefox will not offer to save website logins and passwords.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: OfferToSaveLoginsDefault
explainText:
If this policy is enabled or not configured, Firefox will offer to save website logins and passwords.

If this policy is disabled, Firefox will not offer to save website logins and passwords.

In either case, the user will be able to change the value (it is not locked).
supportedOn: Firefox 70 or later, Firefox 68.2 ESR or later

name: PopupBlocking_Allow
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, pop-up windows are always allowed for the origins indicated. If a top level domain is specified (http://example.org), pop-up windows are allowed for all subdomains as well.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default pop-up policy is followed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: PopupBlocking_Default
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, pop-up windows are allowed from websites by default.

If this policy is not configured or enabled, popups are not allowed from websites.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: PopupBlocking_Locked
displayName: Do not allow preferences to be changed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, pop-up preferences cannot be changed by the user.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change their pop-up preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: InstallAddonsPermission_Allow
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, add-ons are always allowed for the origins indicated unless add-on install is disabled. If a top level domain is specified (http://example.org), add-ons are allowed for all subdomains as well.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default add-on policy is followed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: InstallAddonsPermission_Default
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, add-ons cannot be installed.

If this policy is not configured or enabled, add-ons can be installed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: CustomizeFirefoxHome
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can choose the sections displayed on Firefox Home and prevent the user from changing them.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default sections are displayed and the user can change them.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

presentationElements.label: Don't allow settings to be changed

name: FlashPlugin_Allow
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Flash is activated by default for the origins indicated unless Flash is completely disabled. If a top level domain is specified (http://example.org), Flash is allowed for all subdomains as well.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default Flash policy is followed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: FlashPlugin_Block
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Flash is blocked for the origins indicated. If a top level domain is specified (http://example.org), Flash is blocked from all subdomains as well.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default Flash policy is followed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: FlashPlugin_Default
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Flash is always activated on websites.

If this policy is disabled, Flash is never activated on websites, even if they are in the specified in the Allow list.

If this policy is not configured, Flash is click to play.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: FlashPlugin_Locked
displayName: Do not allow preferences to be changed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Flash preferences cannot be changed by the user.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change their Flash preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: OverrideFirstRunPage
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a URL to be used as the first run page. If you leave the URL blank, no first run page will be shown.

Starting with Firefox 83, Firefox ESR 78.5, you can also specify multiple URLS separated by a vertical bar (|).

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the first run page is displayed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: OverridePostUpdatePage
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a URL to be displayed after Firefox is updated. If you leave the URL blank, no upgrade page will be shown.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the upgrade page is displayed.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: PromptForDownloadLocation
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the user is not prompted for a download location.

If this policy is enabled, the user is always prompted for a download location.

If this policy is not configured, the user is prompted for a download location, but can change the default.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: P_DisableSecurityBypass_InvalidCertificate
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the "Add Exception" button is not available when a certificate is invalid. This prevents the user from overriding the certificate error.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, certificate errors can be overridden.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: P_DisableSecurityBypass_SafeBrowsing
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, a user cannot bypass the warning and visit a harmful site.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, a user can choose to visit a harmful site.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: HomepageURL
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can set a default home page. You can also lock the home page.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can set and change the home page.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

presentationElements.label: Don't allow the homepage to be changed.

name: HomepageAdditional
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can have additional home pages. They are opened in multiple tabs.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, there is only one home page.
supportedOn: Firefox 60 or later, Firefox 60 ESR or later

name: HomepageStartPage
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can change what is displayed when Firefox starts. It can be the homepage, the previous session, or a blank page.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the start page defaults to the previous session.
supportedOn: Firefox 64 or later, Firefox 60.4 ESR or later

name: Homepage_ShowHomeButton
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the home button will appear on the toolbar by default.

If this policy is disabled, the home button will not appear on the toolbar by default.

If this policy is not configured, Firefox will determine whether or not the home button appears on the toolbar by default.
supportedOn: Firefox 88 or later, Firefox 78.10 ESR or later

name: Homepage_NewTabOnRestore
displayName: Also open a new tab when restoring previous windows and tabs
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, a new tab is also opened when restoring previous windows and tabs.

If this policy is disabled, a new tab is not opened when restoring previous windows and tabs.

If this policy is not configured, the Firefox default applies (Firefox may enable this on its own).
supportedOn: Firefox 154 or later

name: A_BookmarksOneLine
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can use JSON to configure bookmarks, including [] to clear all bookmarks.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the individual bookmark policies are used.

If this policy is enabled along with individual bookmarks, those bookmarks will not be added.

This policy has no effect on Managed Bookmarks.

For detailed information on the JSON, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/bookmarks/.
supportedOn: Firefox 95 or later, Firefox 91.4 ESR or later

name: A_Bookmarks
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can use JSON to configure bookmarks, including [] to clear all bookmarks.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the individual bookmark policies are used.

If this policy is enabled along with individual bookmarks, those bookmarks will not be added.

This policy has no effect on Managed Bookmarks.

For detailed information on the JSON, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/bookmarks/.
supportedOn: Firefox 95 or later, Firefox 91.4 ESR or later

explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can configure a bookmark to be added to Firefox. Due to a bug, you must select the location. Note that you must specify the bookmarks in order.

displayName: Disable warnings based on file extension for specific file types on domains
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can define a list of domains and file type extensions that will be exempt from executable warnings.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, warnings are shown for all executable file types.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/exemptdomainfiletypepairsfromfiletypedownloadwarnings/.
supportedOn: Firefox 102 or later

name: StartDownloadsInTempDirectory
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will start downloads in a temporary directory and they will be automatically deleted when you close the browser.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will put downloads in the download folder and they will not be automatically deleted when you close the browser.
supportedOn: Firefox 102 or later

name: GoToIntranetSiteForSingleWordEntryInAddressBar
displayName: Force direct intranet site navigation on single word entries in the address bar
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, typing single word entries in the address bar will attempt to navigate to intranet sites first, falling back to search if the DNS request fails.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, typing single word entries in the address bar will search.
supportedOn: Firefox 104 or later, Firefox 102.2 ESR or later

name: AppUpdatePin
displayName: Pin updates to a specific version
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a Firefox version as xx. or xx.xx. and Firefox will not be updated beyond that major or minor version.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will update normally.
supportedOn: Firefox 102 or later

name: DisableThirdPartyModuleBlocking
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user is not allowed to block third-party modules from the about:third-party page.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user is allowed to block third-party modules from the about:third-party page.
supportedOn: Firefox 110 or later, Firefox 102.8 ESR or later

name: ContainersOneLine
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can use JSON to configure the default containers.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the built-in defaults are used.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/containers/.
supportedOn: Firefox 113 or later

name: Containers
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can use JSON to configure the default containers.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the built-in defaults are used.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/containers/.
supportedOn: Firefox 113 or later

name: SecurityDevices_Add
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a list of PKCS #11 modules to be installed. Modules are specified as a name and a fully qualified path.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no additional PKCS #11 modules will be installed.
supportedOn: Firefox 114 or later, Firefox 102.12 ESR or later

name: SecurityDevices_Delete
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify the names of PKCS #11 modules to be deleted.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no PKCS #11 modules will be deleted.
supportedOn: Firefox 114 or later, Firefox 102.12 ESR or later

name: FirefoxSuggest_WebSuggestions
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you will get suggestions from Firefox related to your search.

If this policy is disabled, you will not get these suggestions.

If this policy is not configured, you will get suggestions from Firefox related to your search.
supportedOn: Firefox 118 or later, Firefox 115.3 ESR or later

name: FirefoxSuggest_SponsoredSuggestions
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you will support the development of Firefox with occasional sponsored suggestions.

If this policy is disabled, you will not get these suggestions.

If this policy is not configured, you will get occasional sponsored suggestions.
supportedOn: Firefox 118 or later, Firefox 115.3 ESR or later

name: FirefoxSuggest_ImproveSuggest
explainText:
This policy is deprecated. Use "Enable online suggestions" instead. If both are set, "Enable online suggestions" takes precedence.

If this policy is enabled, you will help create a richer search experience by allowing Mozilla to process your search queries.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, you do not allow Mozilla to process your search queries.
supportedOn: Firefox 118 or later, Firefox 115.3 ESR or later

name: FirefoxSuggest_Locked
displayName: Do not allow preferences to be changed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox Suggest preferences cannot be changed by the user.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change their Firefox Suggest preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 118 or later, Firefox 115.3 ESR or later

name: PrintingEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, printing is disabled.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, printing is enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 120 or later, Firefox 115.5 ESR or later

name: ManualAppUpdateOnly
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user will not be prompted to install updates and Firefox will not check for updates in the background. The user must manually check and install updates from the About dialog.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the browser receives updates.

This policy is not recommended for most users.
supportedOn: Firefox 88 or later, Firefox 78.10 ESR or later

name: AllowFileSelectionDialogs
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the user will not be able to open file selection dialogs. In most cases, Firefox will act as if the user clicked the cancel button.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, users can open file selection dialogs.
supportedOn: Firefox 124 or later

name: AutofillAddressEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, addresses will not be autofilled for Firefox versions and regions that support it.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, addresses will be autofilled for Firefox versions and regions that support it.
supportedOn: Firefox 125 or later, Firefox 115.10 ESR or later

name: AutofillCreditCardEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, payment methods will not be autofilled for Firefox versions and regions that support it.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, payment methods will be autofilled for Firefox versions and regions that support it.
supportedOn: Firefox 125 or later, Firefox 115.10 ESR or later

name: TranslateEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, web page translation will not be available.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, web page translation will be available.

Note: Web page translation is done completely on the client, so there is no data or privacy risk.
supportedOn: Firefox 126 or later

name: DisableEncryptedClientHello
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the TLS feature Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) will be disabled.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the TLS feature Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) will be enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 127 or later

name: PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, post-quantum key agreement for TLS will be enabled.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, post-quantum key agreement for TLS will be disabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 127 or later

name: CNSA2KeyAgreementEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, CNSA 2.0 ML-KEM-1024 key agreement for TLS will be enabled.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, CNSA 2.0 ML-KEM-1024 key agreement for TLS will be disabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 154 or later

name: HttpsOnlyMode
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can set the default behavior for HTTPS-Only Mode.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, HTTPS-Only Mode is not enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 127 or later

name: HttpAllowlist
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a list of origins that will not be upgraded to HTTPS.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, all origins are upgraded to HTTPS if HTTPS-Only Mode is enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 127 or later

name: PrivateBrowsingModeAvailability
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can set the availability of Private Browsing Mode.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Private Browsing Mode is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 130 or later, Firefox 128.2 ESR or later

name: ContentAnalysis_AgentName
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify the name of the DLP agent, used in dialogs and notifications about DLP operations.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the agent name "A DLP Agent" is used.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_AgentTimeout
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify the timeout in number of seconds after a DLP request is sent to the agent. After this timeout, the request will be denied unless 'Default Result' is set to 1 or 2.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the timeout is 30 seconds.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_AllowUrlRegexList
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a space-separated list of regular expressions that indicates URLs for which DLP operations will always be allowed without consulting the agent. The default is "^about:(?!blank|srcdoc).*", meaning that any pages that start with "about:" will be exempt from DLP except for "about:blank" and "about:srcdoc", as these can be controlled by web content.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the DLP agent will always be consulted.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_BypassForSameTabOperations
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will automatically allow DLP requests whose data comes from the same tab and frame - for example, if data is copied to the clipboard and then pasted on the same page.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will not pass DLP requests whose data comes from the same tab and frame to the DLP agent as normal.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_ClientSignature
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can set the required signature of the DLP agent connected to the pipe. If this is a non-empty string and the DLP agent does not have a signature with a Subject Name that exactly matches this value, Firefox will not connect to the pipe.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the signature will not be verified.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_DefaultResult
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can indicate the desired behavior for DLP requests if there is a problem connecting to the DLP agent.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the DLP request will be denied if there is a problem connecting to the agent.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

items.displayName: Warn the user and allow them to choose whether to allow or deny

name: ContentAnalysis_DenyUrlRegexList
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify a space-separated list of regular expressions that indicates URLs for which DLP operations will always be denied without consulting the agent.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the DLP agent will always be consulted.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_Enabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will use DLP.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will not use DLP.

Note: If this policy is enabled and no DLP agent is running, all DLP requests will be denied unless Default Result is set to 1 or 2.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_IsPerUser
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the pipe the DLP agent creates is per-system.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, the pipe the DLP agent creates is per-user.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_PipePathName
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can change the name of the pipe for the DLP agent.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the default pipe name of 'path_user' is used.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_ShowBlockedResult
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, Firefox will not show a notification when a DLP request is denied.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, Firefox will show a notification when a DLP request is denied.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_Clipboard
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, clipboard operations will not use DLP.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, clipboard operations will use DLP.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_Clipboard_PlainTextOnly
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, all formats will be analyzed on the clipboard, which some DLP agents may not expect.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, only the text/plain format will be analyzed on the clipboard.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_DragAndDrop
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, drag and drop operations will not use DLP.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, drag and drop operations will use DLP.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_DragAndDrop_PlainTextOnly
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, all formats will be analyzed in what is being dropped, which some DLP agents may not expect.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, only the text/plain format will be analyzed in what is being dropped.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_FileUpload
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, file upload operations will not use DLP.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, file upload operations will use DLP.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_Print
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, print operations will not use DLP.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, print operations will use DLP.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_Download
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, download operations will not use DLP.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, download operations will use DLP.
supportedOn: Firefox 142 or later, Firefox 140.2 ESR or later

name: ContentAnalysis_TimeoutResult
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can indicate the desired behavior for DLP requests if the DLP agent does not respond to a request in less than AgentTimeout seconds. 

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the request will be denied.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

items.displayName: Warn the user and allow them to choose whether to allow or deny

name: SkipTermsOfUse
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the Firefox Terms of Use (https://www.mozilla.org/about/legal/terms/firefox/) and Privacy Notice (https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/firefox/) do not display upon startup.

You represent that you accept and have the authority to accept the Terms of Use on behalf of all individuals to whom you provide access to this browser.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the Firefox Terms of Use and Privacy Notice do display upon startup.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: FirefoxHome_Search
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the search field is not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, the search field is displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: FirefoxHome_TopSites
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, shortcuts are not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, shortcuts are displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: FirefoxHome_SponsoredTopSites
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, sponsored shortcuts are not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, sponsored shortcuts are displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 95 or later, Firefox 91.4 ESR or later

name: FirefoxHome_Highlights
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, recent activity is not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, recent activity is displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: FirefoxHome_Stories
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, stories are not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, stories are displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: FirefoxHome_SponsoredStories
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, sponsored stories are not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, sponsored stories are displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 95 or later, Firefox 91.4 ESR or later

name: FirefoxHome_Weather
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the weather widget is not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, the weather widget is displayed on the new tab page.
supportedOn: Firefox 152 or later

name: FirefoxHome_Locked
displayName: Do not allow preferences to be changed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox Home preferences cannot be changed by the user.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change their Firefox Home preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 68 or later, Firefox 68 ESR or later

name: VisualSearchEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, visual search is disabled.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, visual search is enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 144 or later

name: GenerativeAI_Enabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, all generative AI features are disabled by default. Individual generative AI policies can override this setting.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, generative AI features are enabled by default, unless overridden by individual generative AI policies.
supportedOn: Firefox 144 or later, Firefox 140.4 ESR or later

name: GenerativeAI_Chatbot
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, AI chatbots are not available in the sidebar.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, AI chatbots are available in the sidebar.
supportedOn: Firefox 144 or later, Firefox 140.4 ESR or later

name: GenerativeAI_LinkPreviews
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, AI is not used to generate link previews.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, AI can be used to generate link previews.
supportedOn: Firefox 144 or later

name: GenerativeAI_TabGroups
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, AI is not used to suggest names and tabs for tab groups.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, AI is used to suggest names and tabs for tab groups.
supportedOn: Firefox 144 or later

name: GenerativeAI_Locked
displayName: Do not allow preferences to be changed
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change generative AI preferences.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change generative AI preferences.
supportedOn: Firefox 144 or later, Firefox 140.4 ESR or later

name: BrowserDataBackup_AllowBackup
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, browser profile data can be backed up when backup is supported on the platform.

If this policy is disabled, browser profile data cannot be backed up.

If this policy is not configured, backup availability follows the platform default.

This policy cannot be used to enable backup on platforms or in configurations where backup is not otherwise supported.
supportedOn: Firefox 146 or later

name: BrowserDataBackup_AllowRestore
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, browser profile data can be restored from backups when restore is supported on the platform.

If this policy is disabled, browser profile data cannot be restored from backups.

If this policy is not configured, restore availability follows the platform default.

This policy cannot be used to enable restore on platforms or in configurations where restore is not otherwise supported.
supportedOn: Firefox 146 or later

name: DisableRemoteImprovements
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox will not apply performance, stability, and feature changes between updates.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Firefox will apply performance, stability, and feature changes between updates.
supportedOn: Firefox 148 or later

name: DisableRemoteSettingsAndAcceptSecurityConsequences
displayName: Disable Remote Settings and accept security consequences
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Remote Settings updates are disabled and Firefox will no longer receive updated data such as blocklists.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, Remote Settings updates are enabled.
supportedOn: Firefox 153 or later

name: IPProtectionAvailable
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, the built-in VPN (IP Protection) is not available to users.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, the built-in VPN (IP Protection) is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: Default_Value
explainText:
Controls the default state for AI features not explicitly configured by other AIControls policies.

If set to "available", unlisted AI features are accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", unlisted AI features are disabled and users will not see them. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: Default_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the default AI controls setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the default AI controls setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: Translations_Value
explainText:
Controls AI-powered page translations.

If set to "available", translations are accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", translations are disabled and users will not see the feature. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: Translations_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the translations setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the translations setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: PDFAltText_Value
explainText:
Controls AI-generated alternative text for images in PDF documents.

If set to "available", PDF alt text is accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", PDF alt text is disabled and users will not see the feature. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: PDFAltText_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the PDF alt text setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the PDF alt text setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: SmartTabGroups_Value
explainText:
Controls AI-powered tab grouping suggestions.

If set to "available", smart tab groups are accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", smart tab groups are disabled and users will not see the feature. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: SmartTabGroups_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the smart tab groups setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the smart tab groups setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: LinkPreviewKeyPoints_Value
explainText:
Controls AI-generated key point summaries shown in link previews.

If set to "available", link preview key points are accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", link preview key points are disabled and users will not see the feature. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: LinkPreviewKeyPoints_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the link preview key points setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the link preview key points setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: SidebarChatbot_Value
explainText:
Controls the AI chatbot panel in the Firefox sidebar.

If set to "available", the sidebar chatbot is accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", the sidebar chatbot is disabled and users will not see the feature. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: SidebarChatbot_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the sidebar chatbot setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the sidebar chatbot setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 149.0.2 or later

name: SmartWindow_Value
explainText:
Controls AI-powered window arrangement features.

If set to "available", smart window is accessible to users and can be enabled or disabled.

If set to "blocked", smart window is disabled and users will not see the feature. For on-device AI, any models already downloaded are removed.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: SmartWindow_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change the smart window setting.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change the smart window setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: LocalNetworkAccess_Enabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled or not configured, local network access security checks are enforced.

If this policy is disabled, local network access security checks are not enforced.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

name: LocalNetworkAccess_BlockTrackers
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, third-party trackers are prevented from accessing localhost and local network resources.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, third-party trackers are not blocked from accessing local network resources.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

name: LocalNetworkAccess_EnablePrompting
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, websites must request explicit user permission before accessing local network resources.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, websites are not prompted for local network access permission.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

name: LocalNetworkAccess_SkipDomains
explainText: A list of domain names for which local network access checks are skipped.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

name: LocalNetworkAccess_Locked
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the user cannot change Local Network Access settings.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the user can change Local Network Access settings.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

name: DefaultSerialGuardSetting
displayName: Control use of the Web Serial API
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can control whether websites can request access to serial ports.

Note: If any other policies are configured and this policy is not set, the Web Serial API is blocked by default.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

items.displayName: Do not allow any site to request access to serial ports via the Web Serial API
Allow sites to ask the user to grant access to a serial port

name: XSLTEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, XSLT (Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations) is enabled.

If this policy is disabled, XSLT (Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations) is disabled.

If this policy is not configured, the Firefox default applies.
supportedOn: Firefox 151 or later

name: SitePolicies
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify per-site policy overrides via JSON.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no site-specific policies are applied.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/sitepolicies/.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: SitePoliciesOneLine
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, you can specify per-site policy overrides via JSON.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, no site-specific policies are applied.

For detailed information on creating the policy, see https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/sitepolicies/.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: FirefoxHome_Widgets_Enabled
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, widgets are not displayed on the new tab page.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, widgets are displayed on the new tab page.

This setting follows the Firefox Home "Locked" policy.
supportedOn: Firefox 156 or later

name: FirefoxHome_Widgets_Blocked
explainText:
A list of widget ids to turn off individually on the new tab page. Blocked widgets are always locked, whether or not "Locked" is set, so the user cannot turn them back on.

Valid ids are clocks, crossword, focusTimer, lists, pictureOfTheDay, privacy, recentSearches, sportsWidget, stocks and weather.
supportedOn: Firefox 156 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_MaxConnectionsCount
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, it sets the maximum number of concurrent connections to the DLP agent. For stability reasons, values exceeding 256 are ignored.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the Firefox default of 32 applies.
supportedOn: Firefox 138 or later

name: RelaunchRequired_NotificationPeriodHours
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, users are notified at least this many hours before a required relaunch. This takes effect once an update has been downloaded or staged and is ready to install.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the Firefox default applies.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: RelaunchRequired_RestartTimeOfDay_Hour
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the required relaunch is scheduled at this hour, in 24-hour format between 0 and 23.

At the scheduled time Firefox closes and reopens automatically. Tabs are restored, but the user is not prompted and cannot cancel the restart.

Note: If less than one hour remains until the scheduled time, the restart is deferred to the same time the following day.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the Firefox default applies.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: RelaunchRequired_RestartTimeOfDay_Minute
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the required relaunch is scheduled at this minute, between 0 and 59.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, the Firefox default applies.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: FirefoxSuggest_OnlineEnabled
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, Firefox Suggest fetches suggestions as the user types.

If this policy is disabled, Firefox Suggest is limited to suggestions stored locally.

If this policy is not configured, the Firefox default applies.

This setting replaces the deprecated "Improve the Firefox Suggest experience" setting.
supportedOn: Firefox 118 or later, Firefox 115.3 ESR or later

name: SearchEngines_DefaultPrivate
displayName: Default search engine for private browsing
explainText:
If this policy is enabled, the named search engine is used as the default in private browsing windows. The name must match an available search engine exactly.

If this policy is disabled or not configured, private browsing windows use the same default search engine as normal windows.
supportedOn: Firefox 71 or later, Firefox 68.3 ESR or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_ClipboardCopy
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, clipboard copy operations will not use DLP.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, clipboard copy operations will use DLP.
supportedOn: Firefox 158 or later

name: ContentAnalysis_InterceptionPoints_ClipboardCopy_PlainTextOnly
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, all formats will be analyzed on clipboard copy, which some DLP agents may not expect.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, only the text/plain format will be analyzed on clipboard copy.
supportedOn: Firefox 158 or later

name: GenerativeAI_SmartWindow
explainText:
If this policy is disabled, Smart Window is not available.

If this policy is enabled or not configured, Smart Window is available.
supportedOn: Firefox 150 or later

name: LocalizeXPRelativePaths_1
displayName: Use localized subfolder names when redirecting Start Menu and My Documents
explainText:
This policy setting allows the administrator to define whether Folder Redirection should use localized names for the All Programs, Startup, My Music, My Pictures, and My Videos subfolders when redirecting the parent Start Menu and legacy My Documents folder respectively.

If you enable this policy setting, Windows Vista, Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows Server 2012 will use localized folder names for these subfolders when redirecting the Start Menu or legacy My Documents folder.

If you disable or not configure this policy setting, Windows Vista, Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows Server 2012 will use the standard English names for these subfolders when redirecting the Start Menu or legacy My Documents folder.

Note: This policy is valid only on Windows Vista, Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows Server 2012 when it processes a legacy redirection policy already deployed for these folders in your existing localized environment.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: DisableFRAdminPin
displayName: Do not automatically make all redirected folders available offline
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to control whether all redirected shell folders, such as Contacts, Documents, Desktop, Favorites, Music, Pictures, Videos, Start Menu, and AppData\Roaming, are available offline by default.

If you enable this policy setting, users must manually select the files they wish to make available offline.  

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, redirected shell folders are automatically made available offline. All subfolders within the redirected folders are also made available offline.  

Note: This policy setting does not prevent files from being automatically cached if the network share is configured for "Automatic Caching", nor does it affect the availability of the "Always available offline" menu option in the user interface.  

Note: Do not enable this policy setting if users will need access to their redirected files if the network or server holding the redirected files becomes unavailable.

Note: If one or more valid folder GUIDs are specified in the policy setting "Do not automatically make specific redirected folders available offline", that setting will override the configured value of "Do not automatically make all redirected folders available offline".
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2003 operating systems or Windows XP Professional

name: DisableFRAdminPinByFolder
displayName: Do not automatically make specific redirected folders available offline
explainText:
This policy setting allows you to control whether individual redirected shell folders are available offline by default.

For the folders affected by this setting, users must manually select the files they wish to make available offline.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, all redirected shell folders are automatically made available offline. All subfolders within the redirected folders are also made available offline.

Note: This policy setting does not prevent files from being automatically cached if the network share is configured for "Automatic Caching", nor does it affect the availability of the "Always available offline" menu option in the user interface.

Note: The configuration of this policy for any folder will override the configured value of "Do not automatically make all redirected folders available offline".
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012, Windows 8 or Windows RT

presentationElements.label: Set the checkbox for any redirected shell folder that should not automatically be made available offline.

name: FolderRedirectionEnableCacheRename
displayName: Enable optimized move of contents in Offline Files cache on Folder Redirection server path change
explainText:
This policy setting controls whether the contents of redirected folders is copied from the old location to the new location or simply renamed in the Offline Files cache when a folder is redirected to a new location.

If you enable this policy setting, when the path to a redirected folder is changed from one network location to another and Folder Redirection is configured to move the content to the new location, instead of copying the content to the new location, the cached content is renamed in the local cache and not copied to the new location. To use this policy setting, you must move or restore the server content to the new network location using a method that preserves the state of the files, including their timestamps, before updating the Folder Redirection location.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, when the path to a redirected folder is changed and Folder Redirection is configured to move the content to the new location, Windows copies the contents of the local cache to the new network location, then deleted the content from the old network location.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012, Windows 8 or Windows RT

name: PrimaryComputer_FR_1
displayName: Redirect folders on primary computers only
explainText:
This policy setting controls whether folders are redirected on a user's primary computers only. This policy setting is useful to improve logon performance and to increase security for user data on computers where the user might not want to download private data, such as on a meeting room computer or on a computer in a remote office.

To designate a user's primary computers, an administrator must use management software or a script to add primary computer attributes to the user's account in Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS). This policy setting also requires the Windows Server 2012 version of the Active Directory schema to function.

If you enable this policy setting and the user has redirected folders, such as the Documents and Pictures folders, the folders are redirected on the user's primary computer only.

If you disable or do not configure this policy setting and the user has redirected folders, the folders are redirected on every computer that the user logs on to.

Note: If you enable this policy setting in Computer Configuration and User Configuration, the Computer Configuration policy setting takes precedence.
supportedOn: At least Windows Server 2012, Windows 8 or Windows RT

name: NoPreviewPane
displayName: Turn on or off details pane
explainText:
This policy setting shows or hides the Details Pane in File Explorer.

If you enable this policy setting and configure it to hide the pane, the Details Pane in File Explorer is hidden and cannot be turned on by the user.

If you enable this policy setting and configure it to show the pane, the Details Pane is always visible and cannot be hidden by the user. Note: This has a side effect of not being able to toggle to the Preview Pane since the two cannot be displayed at the same time.

If you disable, or do not configure this policy setting, the Details Pane is hidden by default and can be displayed by the user. This is the default policy setting.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

name: NoReadingPane
explainText:
Hides the Preview Pane in File Explorer.

If you enable this policy setting, the Preview Pane in File Explorer is hidden and cannot be turned on by the user.

If you disable, or do not configure this setting, the Preview Pane is hidden by default and can be displayed by the user.
supportedOn: At least Windows Vista

Specifies the type of virtual disk to auto-create. The default is VHD which is the same as "Not Configured".

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\VolumeType
Type:  REG_SZ
Values:  VHD, VHDX
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcVolumeWaitTimemilliseconds
explainText:
Specifies the number of milliseconds to wait for the volume to be attached by the system. The default is 20000 (20 sec) which is the same as "Not Configured".

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\VolumeWaitTimeMS
Type:  DWORD
Values:  Min = 1000, Max = 1000000
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcCCDLocations
explainText:
CCDLocations are formatted using a type and a connectionString separated using a ; as the delimiter. The type will accept either smb or azure. The connectionString for smb type must include the full UNC path to the file share. The connectionString for azure type should be secured as per the documentation (https://aka.ms/fslogix). The strings are case sensitive.

- CCDLocations using SMB:  type=smb,name="SMB Share 1",connectionString=\\<server 1 fqdn>\<share name>;type=smb,name="SMB Share 2"connectionString=\\<server 2 fqdn>\<share name>

- CCDLocations using Azure (secure):  type=smb,name="SMB Share 1",connectionString=\\<server 1 fqdn>\<share name>;type=azure,name="Azure Blob 1",connectionString="|fslogix/stgacct1-connectionstring|"

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\CCDLocations
Type:  REG_SZ
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcCCDMaxCacheSizeinMBs
displayName: CCD Max Cache Size in MBs
explainText:
CcdMaxCacheSizeInMBs specifies the maximum local cache size in megabytes, per user, during normal operation. Normal operation assumes that all Cloud Cache providers are available, and that storage performance is adequate to accept I/O at the rate necessary to accommodate profile utilization.

CAUTION: Do not use this setting unless the performance and technical aspects to this setting are fully understood as this setting is a leading cause to poor performance and has limited use cases.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\CcdMaxCacheSizeInMBs
Type:  DWORD
Values: Min (No Limit) = 0, Max = 10000000
supportedOn: v2105 or later

presentationElements.label: CCD Max Cache Size in MBs

name: OdfcCCDUnregisterTimeout
explainText:
CCD Unregister Timeout represents the number of seconds that a user's sign out will be delayed if the number of available providers is less than specified in Healthy Providers Required For Unregister.

If CCD Unregsiter Timeout is set to 0, then the user sign out will be held until the number of providers specified in Healthy Providers Required For Unregister are available. NOTE: If CCDUnregisterTimeout is set to 0, and the number of providers specified in Healthy Providers Required For Unregister is not met, then the user's sign out may appear to the user as if the session is locked. The sign out may be held infinitely.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\CCDUnregisterTimeout
Type:  DWORD
Values:  Min = 0, Max = 10000000
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcClearCacheOnForcedUnregister
explainText:
If the desired behavior is for the local cache to be deleted, even if the data has not been flushed to a CCD Location, then Clear Cache On Forced Unregister should be set to Enabled.  Setting Clear Cache On Forced Unregister to Enabled may result in user data saved in the registry to be lost during the current session. It is important to understand that this data isn't recoverable if the local cache is cleared in this scenario. Verify that you understand the implications of changing the default value of this setting prior to making changes.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\ClearCacheOnForcedUnregister
Type:  DWORD
Values:  0 = Disabled, 1 = Enabled
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcClearCacheOnLogoff
explainText:
By default, the Local Cache file won't be removed when the user sign out. If a user accesses a system where it's desirable to have the Local Cache file deleted when they sign out, set Clear Cache On Logoff to Enabled.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\ClearCacheOnLogoff
Type:  DWORD
Values:  0 = Disabled, 1 = Enabled
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcHealthyProvidersRequiredForRegister
explainText:
This setting specifies the number of healthy CCD Locations required to allow a sign in. If using the default setting, users will always be allowed to sign in, even if no CCD Locations are available.

If a user signs in with no available CCD Locations, FSLogix assumes that one or more CCD Locations will become available prior to the user signing out. If a CCD Locations does not become available during the time of the user session, then the user is prevented from signing out (discussed in Healthy Provider Required For Unregister).

If it is desired to block a user from signing in and a minimum number of CCD Locations are not available, the Healthy Providers Required For Register may be set to the number of CCD Locations required for a sign in.

If the minimum number of CCD Locations required for registration aren't available, then the sign in will fail. When setting Healthy Providers Required For Register to anything other than 0, then Prevent Login With Failure and/or Preven tLogin With Temp Profile should be used in order to create the desired user experience.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\HealthyProvidersRequiredForRegister
Type:  DWORD
Values:  Min = 0, Max = 4
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcHealthyProvidersRequiredForUnregister
explainText:
This setting specifies the number of healthy CCD Locations required for a user to sign out. The default setting is 1, meaning that at least one remote CCD Location is required for the user to sign out.

If the number of available CCD Locations, when a user attempts to sign out, is less than the number set for Healthy Providers Required For Unregister, the user's sign out will be prevented for the time specified in CCD Unregister Timeout.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\HealthyProvidersRequiredForUnregister
Type:  DWORD
Values:  Min = 0, Max = 4
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcDiffDiskParentFolderPath

NOTE:

- This setting has NO EFFECT when NoProfileContainingFolder is enabled

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\FlipFlopProfileDirectoryName
Type:  DWORD
Values:  0 = Disabled, 1 = Enabled

NOTE:  This setting will override ANY OTHER setting related to container folders.

- SIDDIRNameMatch has NO EFFECT when used in conjunction with this setting.
- SIDDIRNamePattern has NO EFFECT when used in conjunction with this setting.
- FlipFlopProfileDirectoryName has NO EFFECT when used in conjunction with this setting.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\NoProfileContainingFolder
Type:  DWORD
Values:  0 = Disable, 1 = Enabled
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcSIDDirectoryNameMatch
explainText:
Specifies a string pattern used when matching a Profile or ODFC container folder. Use this setting to define how FSLogix will attempt to locate a users Profile or ODFC container. FSLogix will use the VHDLocations or CCDLocations as the location where to search and this setting defines what to search.

NOTE:  When using this configuration setting, be sure the SIDDIRNamePattern value matches this setting.

- This setting has NO EFFECT when FlipFlopProfileDirectoryName is enabled.
- This setting has NO EFFECT when NoProfileContainingFolder is enabled.
- NoProfileContainingFolder > FlipFlopProfileDirectoryName > SIDDirNameMatch (this setting)

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\SIDDirNameMatch
Type:  REG_SZ
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcSIDDirectoryNamePattern
explainText:
Specifies a string pattern used when creating a Profile or ODFC container folder. Use this setting to define how FSLogix will attempt to create a users Profile or ODFC container folder. FSLogix will use the VHDLocations or CCDLocations as the location where to create and this setting defines what to create.

NOTE:  When using this configuration setting, be sure the SIDDIRNameMatch value matches this setting.

- This setting has NO EFFECT when FlipFlopProfileDirectoryName is enabled.
- This setting has NO EFFECT when NoProfileContainingFolder is enabled.
- NoProfileContainingFolder > FlipFlopProfileDirectoryName > SIDDirNamePattern (this setting)

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\SIDDirNamePattern
Type:  REG_SZ
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcVHDNameMatch

NOTE: When using this configuration setting, be sure the VHDNamePattern value matches this setting.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\VHDNameMatch
Type:  REG_SZ
supportedOn: v2105 or later

name: OdfcVHDNamePattern
explainText:
Specifies a string pattern used when creating a users ODFC container. Use this setting to define how FSLogix will attempt to create a users ODFC container (VHD(x) file). FSLogix will use the VHDLocations or CCDLocations as the location where to search and this setting defines what to create.

NOTE: When using this configuration setting, be sure the VHDNameMatch value matches this setting.

Registry Entry:  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC\VHDNamePattern
Type: REG_SZ
supportedOn: v2105 or later
