explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, when the client resolves both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and the IPv6 TLS connection fails, the client will retry the connection using IPv4.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not perform this IPv4 retry for IPv6 TLS errors.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ForceEnableWebViewRecycle_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Force enable WebView recycle behavior (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will force WebView recycle behavior to reclaim memory from supported WebView-based tabs according to the configured recycle rules.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not force WebView recycle behavior and will use the normal Memory Saver and WebView recycle settings.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableWebRequestRateLimit_Server_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable server-driven passive rate limiting for web requests (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will enable server-driven passive rate limiting for web requests and report related rate limit telemetry.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not enable server-driven passive rate limiting for web requests.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: WebRequestRateLimit_ClientMode_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set the client mode for web request rate limiting (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is 1.
If this policy is set, the client will use the specified mode for web request rate limiting.
The value range is 0 to 3: 0 disables client-side web request rate limiting, 1 enables telemetry only, 2 enables rate limiting without telemetry, and 3 enables both telemetry and rate limiting.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set the client mode for web request rate limiting

name: AutoStartPhoneMyNotes_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable auto-start for Zoom Phone My Notes (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will automatically start Zoom Phone My Notes.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not automatically start Zoom Phone My Notes.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableAsyncProxyResolve_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will resolve proxy settings asynchronously.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not use asynchronous proxy resolution.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableBatchProxyResolveViaAsync_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable batch proxy resolution through the async path (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will resolve multiple proxy requests in a batch through the asynchronous proxy path.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not use batch proxy resolution through the asynchronous path.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableHandleRedirectProxy_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable handling of redirect proxy (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will handle redirect proxy during proxy resolution.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not handle redirect proxy during proxy resolution.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableNewHomePage_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable the new home page (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will use the new home page.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not use the new home page.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableWinZSafeChecker_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set whether zSafeChecker is allowed to run (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is 0.
If this policy is set to 0, the client will allow zSafeChecker.exe to run.
If this policy is set to 1, the client will skip the Program Files folder when running zSafeChecker.exe.
If this policy is set to 2, the client will disallow zSafeChecker.exe from running.
The value range is 0 to 2.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set whether zSafeChecker is allowed to run

name: SetMultipleSSOVanityUrl_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set multiple SSO vanity URLs (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is empty.
If this policy is set, the client will use the specified SSO vanity URLs and users can select from them.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnforceFipsForGovSignin_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enforce FIPS mode when switching to a Zoom for Government sign-in domain (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will switch from its default mode to FIPS mode when the user switches from a commercial sign-in domain to a Zoom for Government sign-in domain.
If this policy is disabled, the client will use its default behavior and this policy will not enforce a switch to FIPS mode when the user switches to a Zoom for Government sign-in domain.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_EnableAutoUpdate_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to enable the auto-update feature (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.

If this policy is enabled, client will auto update itself.

If this policy is disabled, client will not auto update itself.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_SetUpdateChannel_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set the specified update channel when auto-update feature is enabled (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty, client will subscribe 'Slow' as update channel when the auto-update feature is enabled.

This policy depends on AU2_EnableAutoUpdate, if AU2_EnableAutoUpdate is disabled, AU2_SetUpdateChannel will not work.

If this policy is a valid string, client will use the specified channel listed as below:
'0' - Slow
'1' - Fast

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set the specified update channel when auto-update feature is enabled

name: AU2_EnableShowZoomUpdates_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show 'Zoom Updates' in the general settings (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.

If this policy is enabled, client will show 'Zoom Updates' in the general settings.

If this policy is disabled, client will hide 'Zoom Updates' in the general settings.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_EnableUpdateAvailableBanner_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show a banner on the homepage when updates are available (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.

If this policy is enabled, client will show a banner on the homepage when updates are available.

If this policy is disabled, client will not show a banner on the homepage when updates are available.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_EnablePromptUpdateForAU2_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to prompt the user to update when exiting a meeting or webinar if an update is available (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, client will prompt the user to update when exiting a meeting or webinar if an update is available.

If this policy is disabled, client will not prompt the user to update when exiting a meeting or webinar if an update is available.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_EnableUpdateSuccessNotification_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show a toast indicating that an update has been successfully applied (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.

If this policy is enabled, client will show a toast indicating that an update has been successfully applied on the next launch after an update has been applied.

If this policy is disabled, client will not show a toast indicating that an update has been successfully applied on the next launch after an update has been applied.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_EnableManualUpdate_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to enable the manual 'Check for Updates' option (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.

If this policy is enabled, client will enable the 'Check for Updates' option.

If this policy is disabled, client will disable the 'Check for Updates' option.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_DeploySpecificVersion_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Specify the update target version (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.

If this policy is empty or invalid, client will ignore this policy.

If this policy is a valid string, client will use this string as the update target version.

If the Zoom's version is lower than the specific version, the client will auto update to the specific version. If the Zoom's version is higher than the specific version, the client will not do anything.

The format of this string should be major.minor.patch.build, for example: "5.10.4.5035"

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_Update3rdStorageUrl_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set a local storage url for update (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.

This policy depends on AU2_DeploySpecificVersion, if AU2_DeploySpecificVersion is empty, AU2_Update3rdStorageUrl will not work.

Stored installation package needs to be named according to the following rules: ZoomInstallerFull.msi, x64_ZoomInstallerFull.msi, winarm64_ZoomInstallerFull.msi.

If the user's installation package can be downloaded through such a link: "http://127.0.0.1/x64_ZoomInstallerFull.msi", this string should be "http://127.0.0.1".

If this policy is a valid string, client will use this string as the update download url when the target version of the update is specified.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set a local storage url for update

name: AU2_SetUpdateSchedule_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is empty.

If this policy is empty or invalid, client will download the update package at anytime.

If this policy is a valid string, client will download the update package within the specified time period.

The format of this string should be HHMM-HHMM, for example: "0900-1800" means 09:00 to 18:00, "1800-0400" means 18:00 to the next day 04:00.

If this setting is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set the specified update channel when auto-update feature is enabled

name: AU2_InstallAtIdleTime_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to enable auto update installation when idle (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

This policy depends on AU2_EnableAutoUpdate, if AU2_EnableAutoUpdate is disabled, AU2_InstallAtIdleTime will not work.

If this policy is enabled, client will enable auto update installation when idle.

If this policy is disabled, client will disable auto update installation when idle.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_SafeUpgradePeriod_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to install auto updates within a specified time period (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is "0000-0400".

This policy depends on AU2_InstallAtIdleTime, if AU2_InstallAtIdleTime is disabled, AU2_SafeUpgradePeriod will not work.

If this policy is empty or invalid, client will install auto updates within the default time period when idle.

If this policy is a valid string, client will install auto updates within the specified time period when idle.

The format of this string should be HHMM-HHMM, for example: "0900-1800" means 09:00 to 18:00, "1800-0400" means 18:00 to the next day 04:00.

If this setting is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set to install auto updates within a specified time period

name: AU2_UpdateChannelCandidates_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set the update channel list (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.

If this policy is empty or invalid, client will set Slow and Fast as the default update channel list.

If this policy is a valid string, client will set the update channel list according to the string.

The format of this string should be {channel id}:{channel name} and use semicolon to separate different channels, for example: "0:Slow" will add Slow to the update channel list, "0:Slow;1:Fast" will add Slow and Fast to the update channel list.

The following are the two public update channels:
"0" - Slow
"1" - Fast

Note:
1.Slow will be added to the list even if it is not written to string.

If this setting is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AU2_LimitManualUpdateVersion_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set manual check for updates to the version defined by Auto Update (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

This policy depends on AU2_EnableAutoUpdate and AU2_EnableManualUpdate, if AU2_EnableAutoUpdate or AU2_EnableManualUpdate is disabled, AU2_LimitManualUpdateVersion will not work.

If this policy is enabled, client will set manual check for updates to the version defined by Auto Update.

If this policy is disabled, client will set manual check for updates to the latest version.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableLinkPreviewInChat_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Client will disable and hide link preview feature in chat (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is disabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will disable and hide link preview feature in chat.

If this setting is disabled, link preview feature will be enabled in chat.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: SetMessengerDoNotDropThread_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to move messages with new replies to the bottom of the chat (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will move messages with new replies to the bottom of the chat.

If this setting is disabled, client will not move messages with new replies to the bottom of the chat.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ShowVoiceMessageButton_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show audio message button (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will show audio message button.

If this setting is disabled, client will not show audio message button.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AlwaysShowIMNotificationBanner_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show notification banner on screen util dismissed (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is disabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will show notification banner on screen util dismissed.

If this setting is disabled, client will not show notification banner on screen util dismissed.

If this setting is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: PlaySoundForIMMessage_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to play sound when receive a new message (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will play sound when receive a new message.

If this setting is disabled, client will not play sound when receive a new message.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ShowIMMessagePreview_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show message preview (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will show message preview.

If this setting is disabled, client will not show message preview.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: MuteIMNotificationWhenInMeeting_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to mute chat notifications while in a meeting or internal call (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will mute chat notifications while in a meeting or internal call.

If this setting is disabled, client will not mute chat notifications while in a meeting or internal call.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ShowVideoMessageButton_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show video message button (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will show video message button.

If this setting is disabled, client will not show video message button.

If this setting is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ShowProfilePhotosInChat_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to show profile photos next to direct messages (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, client will show profile photos next to direct messages.

If this setting is disabled, client will not show profile photos next to direct messages.

If this setting is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: KeepOnlyOneSectionOpenInChat_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Keep only one section open in Team Chat (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client only allow one section opened at a time.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not limit sections
If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: SeparateIMChatAndChannel_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client organize chats by section.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not Organize chats by section
If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableIMFileTransfer_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will disable IM file transfer feature when current domain is not exist in the list of AllowedIMFileTransferDomain.
If this policy is disabled, the client will use the default setting.
If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AllowedIMFileTransferDomain_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Allowed IM file transfer domain list (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.
If this policy is a valid string(for example:zoom1.us),and DisableIMFileTransfer is enabled, the client will only allow the domain zoom1.us to IM transfer feature. Multiple domains can be separated with & (for example: zoom1.us&zoom2.us)
If this setting is empty, and DisableIMFileTransfer is enabled, client will disable IM transfer feature for all domains.

If this policy is not set, client will use default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Allowed IM file transfer domain list

name: MessageNotificationPreference_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Setting up message notifications preferences for Team Chat (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
This policy is exactly same as the manual setting: "Settings"-"Team Chat"-"Message Preferences". Its default policy is 1, client will default to notify direct messages, mentions, and replies.

If this policy is a valid integer, client will use the specified type listed as below:
0 - All messages
1 - Direct messages, mentions, and replies
2 - Off

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Setting up message notifications preferences for Team Chat

name: KeepUnreadMessagesOnTop_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Keep all unread messages at the top of recent chats (Recommendation Setting)

If this setting is false, client will not keep all unread messages at the top of recent chats.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.

categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ShowUnreadCountForChannel_Policy_Recommend

name: UnreadViewOrder_Policy_Recommend

If this policy is a valid integer, client will use the specified type listed as below:
0 - Start at the first unread message
1 - Start at the latest unread message

categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ReceiveNotificationsByKeyword_Policy_Recommend

Default policy is empty.
If this policy is a valid string, the client will trigger message notifications based on these keywords.
If this setting is empty, client will trigger message notifications normally.

If this policy is not set, client will use default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Setting keywords as the basis for triggering message notifications

name: PreferredLanguage_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Use this language when translating messages (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.
If this policy is a valid string(for example:en), the client will use this language when translating messages
If this setting is empty, the client will use the default language when translating messages.

If this policy is not set, client will use default setting.

categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Use this language when translating messages

name: TurnOffVideoCameraOnJoin_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Turn off video camera when joining meeting (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is false.

If this policy is set to true, client will turn off video camera when joining meeting.

If this policy is set to false, client will turn on video camera when joining meeting.

If this policy is not set, client will default policy.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AutoJoinVoIP_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Auto connect audio with VoIP when joining meeting (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is false.

If this policy is set to true, client will automatically connect audio with VoIP when joining meeting.

If this policy is set to false, client will not automatically connect audio with VoIP when joining meeting.

If this policy is not set, client will use default policy.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AutoEnableDualMonitor_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable dual monitor if system supports (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is disbled.

If this setting is enabled, client will enabled dual monitor mode for meeting.

If this setting is disabled, client will disable dual monitor mode for meeting.

If this setting is not set, client will use default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnterFullScreenWhenViewingSharedScreen_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Client will enter full screen mode when viewing shared screen (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is true.

If this policy is set to true, client will enter full screen mode when viewing shared screen.

If this policy is set to false, client will stay in windowed mode when viewing shared screen.

If this policy is not set, client will use default policy.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: FitContentWhenViewingSharedScreen_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Client will resize content to fit the window when viewing shared screen (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is true.

If this policy is set to true, client will resize content to fit the window when viewing shared screen.

If this policy is set to false, client will not resize content to fit the window when viewing shared screen.

If this policy is not set, client will default policy.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableHDVideo_Policy_Recommend

If this setting is disabled, client will capture and send camera video in 360p format.

If this setting is not set, client will use default setting.

name: ControlAllAppsWhenRemoteControl_Policy_Recommend

explainText:
Default policy is true.

If this policy is set to true, all applications can be controlled during remote control session.

If this policy is set to false, system applications cannot be controlled during remote control session.

If this policy is not set, client will use default policy.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: RecordingFilePath_Policy_Recommend

Default path is User/Document folder.

Allows you to set path for local meeting recording files.

For example: C:\MyZoomRecordings
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set path for local meeting recording files

name: DisableAeroModeDuringShareScreen_Policy_Recommend

Default setting is enabled.

If this setting is enabled, Aero mode will be disabled when screen sharing on Windows 7 system.

If this setting is disabled, Aero mode will not be disabled when screen sharing on Windows 7 system.

If this setting is not set, client will default setting.

name: EnterFullScreenWhenJoinMeeting_Policy_Recommend

Default policy is false.

If this policy is set to false, client will stay in windowed mode when joining a meeting.

Admins can choose other IP addresses within the range of [224.0.0.1, 239.255.255.255].

name: MeshListenPortRange_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set network port range for Zoom Mesh parent-child node communication (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.

If this policy is a valid port range address, the client will use this range to set up listen sockets for connection requests between Mesh parents and children nodes. The nodes will also use this range to send signals and media data.

If this policy is invalid or empty, the client will use "18801-19800" as the default port range.

The format of this string should be "port-port", for example: "18801-19800".

For Zoom Mesh Windows Firewall rules, the configured range must start at port 2000 or higher and span fewer than 5120 ports; otherwise, the firewall rule will not be added.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Set network port range for Zoom Mesh parent-child node communication

name: EnableGuestMesh_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Allows users to join an external Webinar as a guest through another account's local Zoom Mesh-enabled network (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this setting is enabled, this policy will allow users (not on your account) to join an external Webinar through the local Zoom Mesh-enabled network. Other requirements must be met, such as the device having the minimum supported client version for Mesh connections and the associated account setting in the web portal also enabled.

If this setting is disabled, this policy will not allow external users (not on your account) to join an external Webinar through the local Zoom Mesh-enabled network.

If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: HideCallQueue_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, this policy will hide the 'Call Queues' in settings.

If this policy is disabled, this policy will not hide the 'Call Queues' in settings.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: HideBlockNumber_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set to hide 'Block Number' feature (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, this policy will hide the 'Block Number' feature.

If this policy is disabled, this policy will not hide the 'Block Number' feature.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableInMeetingZoomNotes_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Disable Zoom Notes for Meetings (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, this policy will disable Zoom Notes for Meetings.

If this policy is disabled, this policy will not disable Zoom Notes for Meetings.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableSmartMeetingSummaries_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Disable Meeting Summary with AI Companion (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, this policy will disable meeting summary with AI companion.

If this policy is disabled, this policy will not disable meeting summary with AI companion.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableAICQueries_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, this policy will disable AI Companion questions.

If this policy is disabled, this policy will not disable AI Companion questions.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableAutoCopyConfInvitationURL_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable Automatically copy invite link once the meeting starts (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is disabled.
If this setting is enabled, client will automatically copy invite link once the meeting starts.
If this setting is disabled, client will not automatically copy invite link once the meeting starts.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableAssignTypist_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Disable Allow host to type or assign a participant to type(Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is disabled.
If this setting is enabled, client will disable allow host to type or assign a participant to type.
If this setting is disabled,  client will not disable allow host to type or assign a participant to type.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableInMeetingZoomDocs_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Disable Zoom Docs for Meetings (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, this policy will disable Zoom Docs for Meetings.

If this policy is disabled, this policy will not disable Zoom Docs for Meetings.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AllowedMeetingSurvivability_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Allow the client to switch to survivable mode (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is empty.
If this policy is a valid survivability info string, the client can switch to survivable mode.
If this policy is empty, the client does not support survivable mode.

If this policy is not set, client will use default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

presentationElements.label: Allow the client to switch to survivable mode

name: KeepMeetingOnTop_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Force Zoom Meetings on top of other apps during meetings (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, Zoom Meetings will be forced to sit on top of other apps during meetings.

If this policy is disabled, Zoom Meetings will not be forced to sit on top of other apps during meetings.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableLocalASR_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, the client will not use local ASR feature.

If this policy is disabled, the client will use local ASR feature.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: OptimizeSlideControlWithOfficeAPI_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable the use of Office API to control PowerPoint slides (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, clients will be able to use the Office API to control PowerPoint slides.

If this policy is disabled, clients will be unable to use the Office API to control PowerPoint slides.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableWindowsMeshUAC_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Prevents the Mesh feature from initiating any User Account Control (UAC) prompts (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.

If this policy is enabled, the client will not trigger any User Account Control (UAC) elevation for adding firewall rules required for the mesh feature.

If this policy is disabled, the client may trigger a User Account Control (UAC) prompt.

If this policy is not set, the client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableAutoFraming_Policy_Recommend
explainText:
Default policy is false.

If this policy is true, client will enable auto-framing.

If this setting is false, client will disable auto-framing.

If this policy is not set, client will use default setting or user setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableForceMaximumCameraSizeForSending_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Prevent camera restart during video sending (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will keep the maximum camera capture size while sending video to avoid camera restart when higher video resolution is requested during a meeting.
If this policy is disabled, the client may adjust the camera capture size as needed during video sending.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: AlwaysUseDarkThemeForMeetings_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Always use a dark theme for meetings (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is enabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will always use a dark theme for in-meeting surfaces.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not force a dark meeting theme and will follow the user appearance preference where supported.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: DisableWebinarAttendeeAudio_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Disable computer audio for webinar attendees (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will disable computer audio for webinar attendees.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not disable computer audio for webinar attendees.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnableSharedCameraAmongZoomApps_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enable sharing the camera among Zoom apps (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, the client will allow Zoom apps to share the camera through the unified camera setting.
If this policy is disabled, the client will not enable sharing the camera among Zoom apps.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: SelfViewMode_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Set the default self-view option (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default setting is 0.
If this policy is set to 0, the client will show self view in the gallery.
If this policy is set to 1, the client will hide self view in the meeting.
If this policy is set to 2, the client will float self view over the gallery.
The value range is 0 to 2.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: EnforceFipsForGovMeeting_Policy_Recommend
displayName: Enforce FIPS mode when joining a Zoom for Government meeting (Recommendation Setting)
explainText:
Default policy is disabled.
If this policy is enabled, a commercial Zoom client will switch to FIPS mode when joining a Zoom for Government meeting.
If this policy is disabled, the client will use its default behavior and this policy will not enforce a switch to FIPS mode when joining a Zoom for Government meeting.
If this policy is not set, client will use the default setting.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
categoryPath: Zoom Meetings - Default Settings (users can override)

name: ShareSubscribeFps_Policy
explainText:
If the ShareSubscribeFps registry entry is not set, the default value when viewing shared content is 5.

If the registry entry is set:

when value < 3, the frame rate is 1

when 3<=value < 15, the frame rate is 5

when value >= 15, the frame rate is 25
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: ShareCaptureFps_Policy
explainText:
This is a user-defined screen capture frame rate.

The value can be any number from 1 to 5.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: UDPPortBegin_Policy
explainText:
Admin-specified port range when connecting with UDP.

The range for begin port is (1700, 64000).

The range for end port is (1800, 65000).

Also, note the begin-end range cannot be less than 100.

Port range (7200-17210) is the default range for the Firewall inbound rules used by the Zoom VDI client on the VM side. Before testing UDPPortBegin-End, you will need to set the following:

DisableUDPBridge=0; DisableICABridge=1;DisableMMRDirect=1  and configure a new Firewall inbound rule, like Port range (17000-65000)

Additionally, be aware that if there are multiple users that share the same VM machine, reserving 8 ports for each user is recommended.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: UDPPortEnd_Policy
explainText:
Admin-specified port range when connecting with UDP.

The range for begin port is (1700, 64000).

The range for end port is (1800, 65000).

Also, note the begin-end range cannot be less than 100.

Port range (7200-17210) is the default range for the Firewall inbound rules used by the Zoom VDI client on the VM side. Before testing UDPPortBegin-End, you will need to set the following:

DisableUDPBridge=0; DisableICABridge=1;DisableMMRDirect=1  and configure a new Firewall inbound rule, like Port range (17000-65000)

Additionally, be aware that if there are multiple users that share the same VM machine, reserving 8 ports for each user is recommended.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableBoostPowerScheme_Policy
explainText:
Specify a value of one (1) to disable. Specify a value of zero (0) or not available to enable.

This setting only applies to thin clients with 2 core CPU or less. By default, the VDI Client will force the thin client power settings to high-performance mode if this setting is not set or set to 0.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: FallbackMode_Policy
explainText:
If the registry settings are not configured, the default mode is one (1).

Each number corresponds to a specific mode:

(1) Normal mode (Behaves like the regular zoom client)

(2) Runs as a screen share meeting (Audio and video are muted by default)

(3) A pop-up appears that will say unable to meet and join

(4) A dialogue prompt will display an error message. When the user closes the prompt the Zoom app will also be closed.

(5) Video is disabled.

(6) Video and sharing are disabled.

(7) Video and computer audio are disabled
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: LogLevel_Policy
explainText:
If set to zero (0), there may be some null log files generated.

The log of the init procedure of the VDI plugin will always be generated.

The following values determine the log output:

(0) no log output

(1) output error log

(2) output warning log

(3) output info log

(4) output all logs
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AllowEnableLog_Policy
explainText:
(0)Disabled: users cannot enable logging

(1)Enabled: users can enable logging
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: LogReserveHours_Policy
explainText:
If set to 0 or not set, then there is no limitation.

The duration (in hours) logs are kept.

Set as a numerical value.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: LogReserveSize_Policy
explainText:
If set to 0 or not set, then there is no limitation.

The total size of log files (in MB) to keep.

Set as a numerical value.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: MaxLogFileSize_Policy
explainText:
Applicable to Windows thin client.

Set value from 1 to 100 in MBs.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: MaxLogFileCount_Policy
explainText:
Applicable to Windows thin client.

Set Value between 8-50.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableUDPBridge_Policy
explainText:
If your thin client cannot connect to the Virtual Desktop VM by UDP, setting this to enabled (1) may speed up the process of joining a meeting.

Enabled (1): Cannot transfer data stream on UDP connection between VM and thin clientIf this is configured on the thin client, those settings will override the settings on the VM.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableICABridge_Policy
explainText:
If the MMR is inaccessible for the thin client, and the UDP connection from the thin client to the VM is not available, you will see the message "Zoom Plugin can not connect to the server according to your Zoom config and network status" and attempts to join or start meetings will fail when you set this value to enabled (1).

If this is configured on the thin client those settings will override the settings on the VM.

Enabled (1): Cannot transfer data stream on an ICA connection.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableMMRDirect_Policy
explainText:
If your network firewall has disabled the zoom connection process to Zoom MMRs on thin clients, setting this configuration to enabled (1) may speed up the procedure of joining a meeting.

If this is configured on the thin client those settings will override the settings on the VM.

Enabled (1): Cannot connect to an MMR on the thin client.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AudioAECLevel_Policy
explainText:
The default value is 1.

Advanced AEC offers higher-quality audio than Simple AEC, but it will use more CPU power on the thin client.

(1) Simple AEC

(2) Advanced AEC
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: SortBuddyMaxCount_Policy
explainText:
(0) Company buddies will be sorted.

(x) Company buddies will be sorted if the number is less than or equal to the value set.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: PingServerFromThinClient_Policy
explainText:
Enabled (1): Ping from the thin client.

Disabled (0): Ping from the VDI VM.

Customers need to ask zoom to Enable choose ZC by ip_for_zc.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableDifferentVersionTip_Policy
explainText:
This enables or disables an error message display when the VDI client and VDI plugin versions do not match.

Enabled (1): Will display one.

Disabled (0): Will display no warning message when there is a version mismatch
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: ServiceUnavailableTipMsg_Policy
explainText:
The registry table string type does not support line return. If a line return is required, "backslash n" should be used to add the line return.

The length of the content string cannot be greater than 1024 characters.

Displays an administrator-defined message when the meeting cannot be started because the client is running fallback mode 3 or 4.

When this entry does not exist (or the string value is empty), a default message will be displayed.

When the string value is not empty, it will show the provided error message for either error condition.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: FallbackModeTipMsg_Policy
explainText:
The registry table string type does not support line return. If a line return is required, "backslash n" should be used to add the line return.

The length of the content string cannot be greater than 1024 characters.

Displays a user-defined message when the VDI plugin is not usable and fallback mode is set to 1, 2, 5, 6, or 7.

When this registry key does not exist or the string value is empty, no dialog message will be shown.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: IncompatibleTipMsg_Policy
explainText:
precondition:

1 Encrypted plugin before 3.3.0

2 Join or start an e2e meeting

Configure the meeting incompatibility message to match your internal helpdesk processes. The default message is "The Zoom Media Plugin is incompatible with the meeting, please contact your system administrator".
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: MinPluginVersion_Policy
explainText:
Configure the version to match your existing thin client plugin deployment.

Note that the default version for this setting is 2.1.5.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableWallView7x7_Policy
explainText:
Enabled (1): Revert to old logic and only display 5x5

Disabled (0): Use new logic and offer 7x7 option if hardware requirements are met (release 5.9.6 and greater)
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: ForceWallView3x3_Policy
explainText:
Enabled (1): Forces the use of 3x3.

Disabled (0): This is the default value. Use 720HD to determine if 5x5 should be used.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AllowPluginDSCPMarking_Policy
explainText:
DSCP marking must be enabled in the Zoom web portal for this to work on the plugin side.

Enabled (1): Add DSCP Marking to the plugin traffic.

Disabled (0): DSCP Marking is absent from plugin traffic (even if it is enabled on the account).
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableShareOffload_Policy
explainText:
The default value is 0.

Value 1 uses a simple judgment method. When viewing a share, move the window quickly, and there will be no delay in the share window.

Enabled (1): VDI view share does not offload.

Disabled (0): VDI view share offloads.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableShareAudioSound_Policy
explainText:
The default value is 0.

Enabled (1): "share sound" option will be visible. 

Disabled (0): "share sound" option will be hidden.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableOptimizeForVideo_Policy
explainText:
The default value is 0.

Enabled (1): "optimize for video clip" option will be visible.

Disabled (0): "optimize for video clip" option will be hidden.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableWMIProvider_Policy
explainText:
Enabled (1): Enable the in-process WMI provider for the VDI client.

Disabled (0): Disable the provider.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DSCPValueForAudio_Policy
explainText:
Both values must be set for DSCP tagging to be applied and must be between 1 and 63, otherwise, the value from the Zoom web portal (account settings) is set. This value overrides the account settings if set, and doesn’t require the user to be logged in to an account.

Applies DSCP tagging for audio and video. If using any values besides the default (40 for video, 56 for audio), DSCP tagging requires admin privileges and that the “EnableIndependentDataPort” key be set to 1 to tag the VDI client traffic.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DSCPValueForVideo_Policy
explainText:
Both values must be set for DSCP tagging to be applied and must be between 1 and 63, otherwise, the value from the Zoom web portal (account settings) is set. This value overrides the account settings if set, and doesn’t require the user to be logged in to an account.

Applies DSCP tagging for audio and video. If using any values besides the default (40 for video, 56 for audio), DSCP tagging requires admin privileges and that the “EnableIndependentDataPort” key be set to 1 to tag the VDI client traffic.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: GPOBandwidthOverrideWeb_Policy
explainText: If the policy GPOBandwidthOverrideWeb is enabled, we will ONLY use the bandwidth values from Policy Bandwidth Settings, regardless of whether the value exists under the device location and connection type (our default value is 0, and we use the previous bandwidth configuration rules if the value is not set).
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableMMRDirect_Phone_Policy
explainText:
If your network firewall prevents the zoom process from connecting to the Zoom Phone Server on the thin client, setting this registry option to enabled (1) may speed up Zoom Phone calls.

If this is configured on the thin client, those settings will take override the settings on the virtual desktop.

Enabled (1): Do not attempt to connect directly to the Zoom Phone Server from the thin client.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableUDPBridge_Phone_Policy
explainText:
If your thin client cannot connect to the Virtual Desktop over UDP, setting this to enabled (1) may speed up the process of making a call.

If this is configured on the thin client, the settings will override settings on the virtual desktop.

Enabled (1): Prevent sending Zoom Phone audio over a UDP connection from the thin client to the virtual desktop.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableChannelBridge_Phone_Policy
explainText:
This option allows you to disable sending Zoom Phone audio over the protocol channel.

If your configuration is expected to use Direct or UDP, setting this option to enabled (1) would prevent Zoom Phone from using the unintended media transport of the channel.

Enabled (1): Prevent sending Zoom Phone audio over a channel connection (or example the ICA protocol connection channel).

Disabled (0): No restrictions.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableVDIToolFileTransfer_Policy
explainText:
The default value is disabled (0)

This option allows you to disable the ability for the ZoomVDITool to pull log files from the remote client.

Enabled (1): File transfer from Plugin to VM is disabled when using ZoomVDITool.

Disabled (0): No restriction on Zoom VDI tool.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: CheckHdxMediaOptimization_Policy
explainText:
A value of disabled (0) will check to see if Lync (Skype for Business) or Teams is running to determine if Zoom can allocate HID devices. If either process is running, Zoom does not attempt to take control of HID devices.

If the value is set to enabled (1), the check is to determine if HDX Media Optimization is active (using HID devices). If not, Zoom takes control of HID support.

These options to force HID redirection are provided for evaluation in 5.10.6. A default value for this option will be determined for a future release.

Enabled (1): Check if “HDX media optimization” is active and, if it is, do not force HID redirection.

Disabled (0): Check if Skype for Business or Teams are running (the “lync.exe” process is running) and do not force HID redirection if they are.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableVDIPluginAutoUpgrade_Policy
explainText:
The default value on the VM is enabled (1) starting from Zoom VDI client version 7.0.10. Earlier versions defaulted to disabled (0).

This option is required to enable the VDI plugin auto-update feature.

Adding the policy on the VM will enable the VDI plugin auto-update to install or upgrade VDI plugins if the VDI auto-update component has been installed on the thin client. This feature is currently only supported for Windows devices.

Adding this policy to the Windows Thin Client can be used to DISABLE the auto-update feature for a specific device. An example would be to add the policy for managed devices to disable updates internally, while still allowing auto-update to update users' personal devices at home.

Enabled (1): (Default on VM) Enable plugin auto-update.

Disabled (0): Disable plugin auto-update.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AutoUpdatePluginVersion_Policy
explainText:
This option specifies the auto-upgrade plug-in version. The auto-update plugin will give priority to the specified version. If the specified version is invalid, the web server configuration should prevail.

Example "5.9.6", plugin release version
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: UpdatePluginLater_Policy
explainText:
(0) Plugin auto-update later option is disabled.

(1) Include the Later option, which closes the dialog. The next time the user connects, the same dialog will be presented if the VDI plugin management software detects an action is still required. This policy requires Zoom VDI client version 5.11.6 or higher.

(2) Default. Include the Later option, which waits until the user disconnects from their virtual desktop(s) and then performs the update. This policy requires the Zoom VDI client version version 5.13.0 or higher.

(3) Same as option 2, but disables the "OK" button in the dialog. This policy requires the Zoom VDI client version 6.4.10 or higher.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableSyncDesktopVolumeToTerminal_Policy
displayName: Disable sync desktop volume to terminal
explainText:
This policy will sync changes made for the Virtual Desktop volume slider in the OS taskbar to the Thin Client device, if the VDI speaker output selection is configured as Same as system. This policy requires VDI version 5.14.10 or higher.

Note: Changing the volume on the Thin Client directly will not sync to the Virtual Desktop and change the volume slider in the taskbar.

(0) Sync volume changes made to the Virtual Desktop volume slider in the OS taskbar to the Thin Client device.

(1) Volume changes are not synced (Default)
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableScreenshotOptimization_Policy
explainText:
(Beta) This policy can be used to offload screen capture commands to the plugin side, where the screenshot can capture video received by the VDI plugin. This requires VDI version 5.14.10 or higher.

Currently, the default is disabled (1), but may be changed in a future release.

0 - VDI Client Screenshot will be offloaded

1 - (Default) Disable Screenshot offload
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: PhoneCallTipMsg_Policy
explainText:
This policy disables the audio quality popup message. This requires Zoom VDI client version 5.15.2 or higher

(0) - (Default) "Poor network connection. Audio quality may be affected" notifications during phone calls will be displayed as needed.

(1) - "Poor network connection. Audio quality may be affected" notifications during phone calls will be disabled.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AutoUpdatePluginVersionWin_Policy
explainText: In order to distinguish Win version and Mac version in case of different hotfix version between Win and Mac, these 2 new register keys are created. If none of them are setup or all of them are set as empty string, AutoUpdatePluginVersion still works. If anyone of these new reg key is not empty, AutoUpdatePluginVersion will be skipped. (We plan to retire AutoUpdatePluginVersion after several release)
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

presentationElements.label: Set auto update plugin version Win

name: AutoUpdatePluginVersionMac_Policy
explainText: In order to distinguish Win version and Mac version in case of different hotfix version between Win and Mac, these 2 new register keys are created. If none of them are setup or all of them are set as empty string, AutoUpdatePluginVersion still works. If anyone of these new reg key is not empty, AutoUpdatePluginVersion will be skipped. (We plan to retire AutoUpdatePluginVersion after several release)
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

presentationElements.label: Set auto update plugin version Mac

name: DisableGreenRoom_Policy
explainText:
0 - (Default) Enable GreenRoom

1 - Disable GreenRoom
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: HideAdvancedSettings_Policy
explainText:
Enabled (1): The advanced settings will be hidden.

Disabled (0): This is the default value. Advanced settings will be displayed.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableVDIPluginAutoUpdateOptOut_Policy
displayName: Enable VDI Plugin Auto Update Opt Out
explainText:
VDI 5.17.10 or later

0 - Default

1 - Enabled

By setting EnableVDIPluginAutoUpdateOptOut=1 in VM side, customers can have "Opt Out" option in VDI plugin auto update.

The purpose of this flag is to let Zoom VDI Client share HID devices with other applications.

Prior to this policy, the Zoom VDI client would always give up control from HID device in case it detected other competitive meeting apps (ex. MS Teams VDI 2.0) would be running in parallel in VM machine.

name: SetUpWaitingTimeUpperBoundInSeconds_Policy
displayName: Set Up Waiting Time Upper Bound in Seconds
explainText:
240 (Default)

Valid range: 240 – 172,800

Introduced in version 6.5.10.

By default, after startup, the Zoom Client waits a random amount of time between 60 and 240 seconds before initiating the auto-update process. If the client is restarted, the timer resets and starts over from zero.

This registry setting allows customers to configure the upper bound of that random delay. The valid range is from 240 seconds (4 minutes) to 172,800 seconds (48 hours). With this setting applied, the Zoom Client will wait a random amount of time between 60 seconds and the configured upper bound before starting the auto-update process.

name: UDPPortBegin_Policy
explainText:
Admin-specified port range when connecting with UDP.

The range for begin port is (1700, 64000).

The range for end port is (1800, 65000).

Also, note the begin-end range cannot be less than 100.

Port range (7200-17210) is the default range for the Firewall inbound rules used by the Zoom VDI client on the VM side. Before testing UDPPortBegin-End, you will need to set the following:

DisableUDPBridge=0; DisableICABridge=1;DisableMMRDirect=1  and configure a new Firewall inbound rule, like Port range (17000-65000)

Additionally, be aware that if there are multiple users that share the same VM machine, reserving 8 ports for each user is recommended.

If the value is set to enabled (1), the check is to determine if HDX Media Optimization is active (using HID devices). If not, Zoom takes control of HID support.

Adding the policy on the VM will enable the VDI plugin auto-update to install or upgrade VDI plugins if the VDI auto-update component has been installed on the thin client. This feature is currently only supported for Windows devices.

Adding this policy to the Windows Thin Client can be used to DISABLE the auto-update feature for a specific device. An example would be to add the policy for managed devices to disable updates internally, while still allowing auto-update to update users' personal devices at home.

name: DisableMMRDirect_Phone_Policy
explainText:
If your network firewall prevents the zoom process from connecting to the Zoom Phone Server on the thin client, setting this registry option to enabled (1) may speed up Zoom Phone calls.

If this is configured on the thin client, those settings will take override the settings on the virtual desktop.

Enabled (1): Do not attempt to connect directly to the Zoom Phone Server from the thin client.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableUDPBridge_Phone_Policy
explainText:
If your thin client cannot connect to the Virtual Desktop over UDP, setting this to enabled (1) may speed up the process of making a call.

If this is configured on the thin client, the settings will override settings on the virtual desktop.

Enabled (1): Prevent sending Zoom Phone audio over a UDP connection from the thin client to the virtual desktop.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableChannelBridge_Phone_Policy
explainText:
This option allows you to disable sending Zoom Phone audio over the protocol channel.

If your configuration is expected to use Direct or UDP, setting this option to enabled (1) would prevent Zoom Phone from using the unintended media transport of the channel.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableVDIPluginAutoUpgrade_Policy
explainText:
The default value is disabled (0)

This option is required to enable the VDI plugin auto-update feature.

Adding the policy on the VM will enable the VDI plugin auto-update to install or upgrade VDI plugins if the VDI auto-update component has been installed on the thin client. This feature is currently only supported for Windows devices.

Adding this policy to the Windows Thin Client can be used to DISABLE the auto-update feature for a specific device. An example would be to add the policy for managed devices to disable updates internally, while still allowing auto-update to update users' personal devices at home.

Enabled (1): Enable plugin auto-update.

Disabled (0): Disable plugin auto-update.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: PluginLabel_Policy
explainText:
Supported in versions 6.3.10 and higher.

A label is generated by administrators, which is collected from the virtual machine using WMI.

The character limit for the string is 127 characters. The setting supports strings longer than 127 characters, however, strings longer than 127 characters will be truncated when sent to the virtual machine.

The following characters are not supported and will be replaced with a space if entered in the string: <, >, {, }, [, ], %, /, \, “, ' @, $, &, *,#

The value is added in HKEY_CURRENT_USER first, then read from HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE if there are no settings from HKEY_CURRENT_USER.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableVDIPluginMgmtAutoUpdate_Policy
displayName: Enable VDI Plugin Mgmt Auto Update
explainText:
1 (Default): Enabled

0: Disabled

Auto updates for VDI Plugin Management.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: EnableVDIPluginMgmtAutoDiagnose_Policy
displayName: Enable VDI plugin management auto diagnose
explainText:
The default value is enabled (1)

This policy is supported in Zoom VDI client version 7.0.10 or higher.

When enabled, the Zoom VDI client will automatically check whether the Zoom Universal Plugin is installed properly and whether its configuration is set up correctly. If not, it will attempt to repair it.

Enabled (1): (Default) Plugin management auto diagnose is enabled.

Disabled (0): Plugin management auto diagnose is disabled.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableUDPBridge_Policy
explainText:
If your thin client cannot connect to the Virtual Desktop VM by UDP, setting this to enabled (1) may speed up the process of joining a meeting.

Enabled (1): Cannot transfer data stream on UDP connection between VM and thin clientIf this is configured on the thin client, those settings will override the settings on the VM.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableICABridge_Policy
explainText:
If the MMR is inaccessible for the thin client, and the UDP connection from the thin client to the VM is not available, you will see the message "Zoom Plugin can not connect to the server according to your Zoom config and network status" and attempts to join or start meetings will fail when you set this value to enabled (1).

If this is configured on the thin client those settings will override the settings on the VM.

Enabled (1): Cannot transfer data stream on an ICA connection.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: DisableMMRDirect_Policy
explainText:
If your network firewall has disabled the zoom connection process to Zoom MMRs on thin clients, setting this configuration to enabled (1) may speed up the procedure of joining a meeting.

If this is configured on the thin client those settings will override the settings on the VM.

Enabled (1): Cannot connect to an MMR on the thin client.

Disabled (0): No restrictions
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: PingServerFromThinClient_Policy
explainText:
Enabled (1): Ping from the VDI VM.

Disabled (0): Ping from the VDI VM.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AllowPluginDSCPMarking_Policy
explainText:
DSCP marking must be enabled in the Zoom web portal for this to work on the plugin side.

Enabled (1): Add DSCP Marking to the plugin traffic.

Disabled (0): DSCP Marking is absent from plugin traffic (even if it is enabled on the account).
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later

name: AllowDowngrade_Policy
explainText:
0 (default) - Downgrading or uninstalling the thin client via auto-update is disabled.

1 - Downgrading or uninstalling the thin client via auto-update is enabled.

Supported in versions 6.3.10 and higher.

If AllowDowngrade is set to 1, users can downgrade the client or uninstall the plugin via the auto-update function.

If AllowDowngrade is set to 0, users will not be able to downgrade or uninstall the plugin via auto-update and instead must have an IT Admin manage it.

AllowDowngrade=1 must be enabled on the thin client side to avoid any potential security issues.
supportedOn: Microsoft Windows XP SP2 or later
